NO PEOPLE visible anywhere — not on the street, not on the stoops, not in the lit windows: only empty glowing rooms behind the curtains. Shot on vintage anamorphic lenses wide open: anamorphic blur — a razor-thin plane of focus locked on the dark three-story brownstone's stoop and entrance, foreground sidewalk and the deep end of the street melting into thick creamy defocus, every lit window and the lamp swelling into large oval vertically-stretched bokeh blobs, branches smearing into soft dark shapes. 场景背景

深夜,凌晨时分。纽约,翻修中的战前公寓三层——杰克的狙击巢。他伏在步枪后待命,等待目标。对面的褐石住宅在整个片段中绝不出现——它只以极远处微弱的声音存在。三十秒内:开场全景交代杰克与黑暗的房间 → 漫长的静止等待 → 极远处汽车抵达的微弱声响,他跟踪 → 一声孩童喊声,失神一秒 → 强行收拢自己 → 取出一发子弹压入枪膛,上膛 → 手指落上扳机,击发前的长呼气 → 就在此刻他认出目标是自己的战友。

风格

深夜场景——整个片段处于夜间黑暗中,绝无日光。大卫·芬奇《七宗罪》与《搏击俱乐部》的视觉气质:病态的绿黄与铁灰色调,画面精确、冷酷、临床般克制。摄影机是芬奇式的机器:构图锁死,水平严谨,运动只有极缓慢、绝对平稳的机械推近,没有一丝手持晃动;节奏克制到残忍——静止越长,崩塌越狠。

摄影机与镜头

RED Gemini双原生高感光度,专为极暗夜景拍摄,Leica定制镜头,加低反差滤镜:柔化的反差曲线,无刺眼高光,无光晕;复古2倍变形宽银幕质感:椭圆拉伸焦外,画面边缘猫眼光斑,失焦高光抹成水平长椭圆,轻微色差,柔和暗角衰减,低饱和的克制色彩,暗部干净无噪点。无镜头眩光,无光线拉丝。浅景深:杰克保持清晰焦平面,房间融化为深暗绿灰的模糊焦外。

灯光

深夜曝光锁定,每一个镜头都必须是暗的:整体曝光贴近下限再往下半档,房间是一个黑洞——如果画面看起来"照亮了",就是错的。色调:黑暗本身带着病态的绿——阴影被浑浊的橄榄绿浸透,暗部是绿黑色而非蓝黑色,唯一例外是窗外远处一两点暖光。地板:杰克身下铺的是一张深色哑光垫布,垫布下才是施工塑料布——地面绝不反光、绝不发亮、绝不成为画面里的浅色面;塑料布只在画面边缘的黑暗里以褶皱质感隐约存在。墙面、窗框、木梯全部沉在绿黑的阴影里。唯一亮的元素是窗洞里的夜色本身,而它也绝不过曝、绝不发白。极微弱的城市反射光只勾出杰克的帽兜、颧骨和步枪上缘一线;无高光点;黑位深沉但保留质感;无补光,脸部四分之三留在阴影中。自查:若房间里任何一个面在亮度上与窗洞竞争——曝光就是错的。

首帧与空间调度

深夜。广一点的中景,机位在房间深处黑暗中,与窗呈对角:绿黑色的黑暗房间,唯一亮的是右侧窗洞。窗的状态,仔细读:上下推拉窗的下扇已经完全推起,窗的下半部是一个敞开的空洞,没有玻璃——枪管穿过这个敞开的空洞探出到夜空里,枪口在窗框之外;枪管绝不指向窗台,绝不指向玻璃,绝不停在窗框之内。步枪明显向下倾斜几度——从三层朝对面楼下瞄准,瞄准线穿过敞开的下半窗直达街对面。杰克伏在深色哑光垫布上,帽兜戴起,脸颊贴枪托。三分法:窗在右力点,杰克的轮廓沉在下三分之一的黑暗里。

格式模式

三十秒多镜头序列,共八个镜头,硬切。全部为杰克本人、他的手、他的脸与步枪的全景、中景、特写和微距。摄影机绝不沿枪管看向窗外的街道与住宅——全部戏剧都在杰克和这个房间里。

动作时间轴

镜头1——0.0至5.0秒——заявочный全景,锁死构图,极缓慢机械推近贯穿全镜。画面整体是绿黑的暗调,只有窗洞是亮的:黑暗的翻修客厅,右侧窗洞悬着夜色,窗前深色垫布上杰克的轮廓伏枪不动,枪管穿过敞开的下半窗探向夜空。呼吸的白雾缓慢升起、散去、再升起——两个完整的呼吸循环。房间的黑暗里渐渐读出木梯、油漆桶、垂落的电线——被眼睛发现,而非被光照亮。远处纽约的底噪极低地铺着。

5.0秒硬切

镜头2——5.0至9.0秒——中景,机位在他左侧,锁死。画面依然绿黑暗调,只有窗洞是亮的:纯粹的等待。他伏枪静止,只有呼吸在动;右手食指沿护圈外侧缓慢地敲了两下——整个镜头里唯一的动作。垫布下的塑料布极轻微地响了一声。夜风擦过窗外防护网。

9.0秒硬切

镜头3——9.0至12.5秒——特写,四分之三正面拍他持镜的脸,机位纹丝不动:右眼贴目镜,左眼先睁着随后眯起。极远处,隔着街道与玻璃,几乎听不见:一声引擎驶近、减速、熄火。一声车门。他的眼睛缓慢地从右向左追踪着什么,呼吸变短。然后——一声极细小清亮的孩童喊声,远得像错觉。他追踪的眼睛骤然停死。

12.5秒硬切

镜头4——12.5至15.5秒——极近特写,正面拍脸,缓慢机械推近:他离开目镜半寸,双眼睁开,越过步枪向下呆望——失神,职业面具脱落,屏住呼吸整整两拍。随后下颌咬紧;一口克制的白雾狠狠呼出;面具重新戴上,眼睛垂向枪身。

15.5秒硬切

镜头5——15.5至20.5秒——微距插入,拍戴手套的双手与机匣,构图锁死。画面深暗,黑暗中只有金属上缘泛着微弱冷绿光——装弹仪式以真实的、刻意放慢的节奏完整呈现:右手指从枪身旁捏起一发长长的步枪弹,黄铜弹壳在黑暗里一线幽光;指尖将弹体转正,稳稳压入敞开的枪膛——金属滑入的顺滑一声;枪机拉柄抬起、推进、锁定,一气呵成,清脆的咬合声在死寂的房间里格外响。双手随后回到据枪位,纹丝不动。

20.5秒硬切

镜头6——20.5至23.0秒——微距,同机位:食指离开护圈,落到扳机上,收走第一毫米的行程。手套皮革在指节处起褶,可见微弱的脉搏跳动。一次长长的、准备击发的呼气开始——白雾缓缓流过画面上缘。

23.0秒硬切

镜头7——23.0至24.0秒——一秒的中景插入,机位同镜头2,绿黑暗调:整个身体进入击发前的绝对静止——呼吸停在呼气末端,轮廓像房间里的家具一样死寂。

24.0秒硬切

镜头8——24.0至30.0秒——极近特写,拍他贴着目镜的右眼,极缓慢推近贯穿全镜,直至画面只剩眼睛:黑暗中眼白和虹膜是画面里最亮的东西。纹丝不动的击发据枪,眼神冰冷锁定——两拍绝对静止。然后,目标的脸落进眼底深处——瞳孔缓缓放大,眼睑抽动一次,眼睛细微睁大:认出来了。为击发攒住的那口气卡死在胸腔里,喉结艰难地动了一下。推近继续,眼睛充满画面——里面的冰冷正在碎。定格在凝固的眼睛上。切黑。

表演任务——杰克(全情投入;全部功课发生在眼睛里):

目标:让机器继续运转——等待、抵达、跟踪、装弹、击发、撤离。

障碍:先是远处孩子的声音,然后是镜中的那张脸——每一个都把机器卡得更深。

战术:镜头2——等待本身是任务:眼睛贴镜,身体数着时间,手指敲护圈是唯一漏出来的人性;镜头3——他的眼睛像仪表一样处理远处的声音:标记引擎、标记车门、等待脚步;镜头4——他挣扎着把孩子的声音"没听见":视线越过步枪向下,搜寻一个她不存在的方案版本,失败,随即强迫自己回到程序;镜头5——装弹是他给自己的惩戒仪式:动作比必要的更慢、更精确,用程序压住刚才那一秒的失神;镜头8——眼睛审问镜片里那张脸:与记忆比对一次、两次——希望自己认错——两次都得到同一张脸。

(安全线:目光始终投入任务——绝不僵死、绝不呆滞;自然眨眼节奏,唯认出的两拍屏住。)

物理

子弹有真实的黄铜重量,入膛有金属滑入的顺滑与到位的一声轻响;枪机抬、推、锁带真实钢铁阻力;步枪在两脚架上纹丝不偏;白雾在冷夜空气里绽开又散去;垫布下的塑料布随微小重心变化极轻地响;手套皮革在指节处起褶;喉结的吞咽真实可见。

声音

对面住宅只以极远处的声音存在,隔着街道、玻璃与夜风,微弱到几乎错觉:一声引擎、减速、熄火、车门、一声细小的孩童喊声、第二声车门。杰克近处被放大的死寂:白雾呼吸的循环、指尖敲护圈的两声轻响、垫布下塑料布的窸窣、黄铜弹壳入膛的一声、枪机咬合的脆响、手套在扳机上的皮革吱响、镜头8里一次艰难的吞咽。一切之下,夜风擦过脚手架和防护网的低鸣。无音乐,无对白。 <<<cd7d691a-d4f5-46ca-920c-00b72c36ebee>>>

场景背景
深夜。翻修中公寓楼的临街楼门。杰克戴着黑色针织面罩、左手提着长条硬箱,猛地推开金属楼门冲上人行道——瞬间僵住:两米外,喘息未定的特伦斯双手举着一件黑色手持器械,直指他的脸。特写特伦斯——然后反打杰克:面罩开口里的双眼先是震住,随即——认出来了,眼里涌上的不是恐惧,是喜悦:老友。他抬手去摘面罩想让对方看见自己——面罩只掀到一半,三声急促的闷响。杰克缓缓沉落到地面。特伦斯转身跑进黑暗。杰克躺在人行道上,自己扯下面罩,胸口起伏渐弱——他望着夜空,全片第一次,微笑了。

风格
深夜——绝无日光。《七宗罪》与《搏击俱乐部》的芬奇气质:病态绿黄与铁灰,冷酷临床;色调《泰坦》式双温度沼泽——阴影深青蓝绿,受光面肮脏芥末黄,全画面无干净的白。前半段(镜头1至4)节奏绷紧,构图锁死;后半段(镜头5至8)时间变得粘稠——长镜头,极缓慢机械推近,死亡以近乎温柔的节奏展开。无手持。

首帧与空间调度
深夜。中景,机位在杰克背后偏右肩,楼门内的黑暗里:金属门正被推开,门轴长鸣;门外昏黄路灯下,特伦斯已站在两米外的人行道上,双手举着器械据定,正对门口,胸口剧烈起伏但双臂纹丝不动。杰克僵在门框里,面罩只露双眼,硬箱悬在左手。

目标:镜头3至4——让老友看见自己:此刻他不是执行者,不是目标,只是一个在深夜街头突然遇到兄弟的人。

战术:眼睛先笑——面罩遮不住眼角的细纹;抬手摘面罩的动作是敞开,不是防御——手心几乎是向外的;镜头6——摘下面罩不再是为了被认出,是为了最后用自己的脸躺在这条街上;镜头7——那个微笑是补送的:他终于把认出你的那一刻还给了老友,哪怕老友已经不在。

目标:威胁必须终结——女儿之外什么都不存在。

场景背景
深夜。翻修中公寓楼的临街楼门。杰克戴着黑色针织面罩、左手提着长条硬箱,猛地推开金属楼门冲上人行道——瞬间僵住:两米外,喘息未定的特伦斯双手举着一件黑色手持器械,直指他的脸。特写特伦斯——反打杰克:面罩开口里的双眼先是震住,随即认出来了——喜悦只在眼睛里,安静地亮起来。他缓缓抬手,把面罩下缘掀到鼻子——只露出下巴和嘴,脸的上半仍被面罩遮着,特伦斯认不出他——三声急促的闷响。杰克缓缓沉落到地面。特伦斯举着器械上前半步,俯视地上的人两拍——确认,不认识——然后转身跑进黑暗。杰克躺在人行道上,慢慢把面罩整个扯下,望着夜空,呼吸渐弱——嘴角安静地、几乎不可察觉地弯起:全片第一次,一个平静的微笑。

风格
深夜——绝无日光。《七宗罪》与《搏击俱乐部》的芬奇气质:病态绿黄与铁灰,冷酷临床;色调《泰坦》式双温度沼泽——阴影深青蓝绿,受光面肮脏芥末黄,全画面无干净的白。前半段(镜头1至4)节奏绷紧,构图锁死;后半段(镜头5至9)时间粘稠——长镜头,极缓慢机械推近,死亡以近乎温柔的节奏展开。无手持。

摄影机与镜头
RED Gemini双原生高感光度,专为极暗夜景,Leica定制镜头加低反差滤镜:柔化反差,无刺眼高光,无光晕;复古2倍变形宽银幕:椭圆拉伸焦外,边缘猫眼光斑,失焦高光抹成水平长椭圆,轻微色差,柔和暗角,低饱和克制色彩,暗部干净无噪点。无镜头眩光,无光线拉丝。浅景深:人物保持清晰焦平面,街道融化在深暗绿灰的焦外。

深夜曝光锁定:整体欠曝两档,画面大部分沉在黑暗里。唯一暖色实际光源:一盏昏黄路灯,在特伦斯身后偏左——勾出他的肩线和器械上缘,他的脸大半沉在阴影;同一盏灯给倒下的杰克铺一小片浑浊的黄色光池——他死在全片唯一一块暖光里。楼门内一片黑。无高光点,黑位深沉但保留质感——面罩针织纹理、外套织纹、人行道颗粒在暗部隐约可读。自查:若任何一张脸被完整照亮——太亮。

深夜。中景,机位在杰克背后偏右肩,楼门内的黑暗里:金属门正被推开,门轴长鸣;门外昏黄路灯下,特伦斯已站在两米外的人行道上,双手举着器械据定,正对门口,寸头轮廓被路灯从身后勾出,胸口剧烈起伏但双臂纹丝不动。杰克僵在门框里,面罩只露双眼,硬箱悬在左手。

三十秒多镜头序列,共九个镜头。镜头1至4绷紧的对峙与爆发;镜头5至9缓慢的沉落与告别。全程同一地点:楼门、人行道、路灯。

2.5秒硬切
镜头2——2.5至5.0秒——特写,特伦斯,极缓慢推近:路灯从身后偏左勾出寸头的轮廓、肩线和器械上缘,脸大半沉在阴影,只有下颌绷紧的线条和急促起伏的胸口;器械纹丝不动。他不说话——一个父亲在做算术。
5.0秒硬切
镜头3——5.0至8.5秒——反打,特写,杰克,缓慢推近:面罩开口里的双眼——先是震住,瞳孔缩紧;随后,认出来了。没有任何夸张:只是眼神安静地变了——戒备融开,眼里升起一点温度,像深夜里认出家门口的灯。全部喜悦只在这双眼睛里,克制,几乎温柔。他的右手松开,缓缓抬向面罩下缘——
8.5秒硬切
镜头4——8.5至11.5秒——中景,侧位,两人同框,路灯在画面深处:杰克的右手把面罩下缘掀到鼻子——只露出胡茬的下巴和微微张开想说话的嘴,眼睛和脸的上半仍在面罩里,他仍是一个无法辨认的影子——三声急促压扁的闷响,三点急促的光在画面深处闪过。杰克的身体连着三次微微一顿,像被看不见的手推了三下。硬箱从左手脱落,砸在人行道上一声闷响。
11.5秒硬切
镜头5——11.5至14.5秒——中景偏特写,锁死:杰克缓缓沉落——先靠上门框,滑下,膝盖触地,侧倒进路灯那片浑浊的黄色光池里。动作没有戏剧性,只有重量。面罩仍卡在鼻梁上,下巴裸露。

镜头8——22.0至27.0秒——极近特写,正面俯视,极缓慢推近贯穿:他的脸在浑浊的黄光里,眼睛望着上方的夜空。呼吸越来越浅。然后,嘴角非常缓慢地、几乎不可察觉地向上弯了一点——安静的、疲惫的、终于可以停下来的微笑;眼神柔和下来,不悲不喜,像一件做完的事。眼里的光缓缓退潮。

6-14s: SNORRICAM — the camera is rigged to his body and locked directly IN FRONT of him at chest height, so JACK (<<<cd7d691a-d4f5-46ca-920c-00b72c36ebee>>>) stays absolutely fixed dead centre of frame while the whole stairwell behind him whips, tilts and rushes past as he goes DOWN flight after flight, three treads at a time, the case on his shoulder. TERRENCE (<<<d9aeaf90-db99-4c74-8606-a13730f3c54f>>>) is standing right there in his way, a couple of steps in front of him, planted in a locked two-handed stance with a black pistol raised level at Jack.

ACTING TASK — JACK: outrun the mistake — the hands run the drill on their own while the mind is already on the sidewalk working out where the man will have gone; he refuses himself any movement that is not travel. At the door the whole calculation dies in one step: what he was racing toward is standing in front of him. He stops because there is nowhere left to run — and what comes up in him is not fear: the man he was sent for is alive and pointing at him, which is the one outcome tonight he can live with.
ACTING TASK — TERRENCE: hold the ground and give nothing away — he got here first and he needs this man to understand it before anything else happens; his eyes stay on the hands, reading them for the next move, not on the face.
Sound: the muttered word, the magazine and bolt, latches snapping, boots hammering treads with the echo of the empty shaft, fabric pulling over his head, breath going hard behind the mask, the steel door banging open, the flat open air of the street, two men breathing — then one report and silence. 场景背景
深夜。一栋包裹着脚手架和绿色防护网、正在整体翻修的战前公寓楼——它临街的公共楼道大门。杰克戴着黑色针织巴拉克拉瓦头套、左手提着长条硬箱,从楼内猛地推开这扇楼道大门冲上人行道——瞬间僵住:两米外,喘息未定的特伦斯双手举着一件黑色手持器械,直指他的脸。特写特伦斯——反打杰克:巴拉克拉瓦眼部开口里的双眼先是震住,随即认出来了——喜悦只在眼睛里,安静地亮起来。他缓缓抬手,把巴拉克拉瓦的下缘掀到鼻子——只露出下巴和嘴,眼睛和脸的上半仍在头套里,特伦斯认不出他——三声急促的闷响。杰克缓缓沉落到地面。特伦斯举着器械上前半步,俯视地上的人两拍——确认,不认识——然后转身跑进黑暗。杰克躺在人行道上,慢慢把巴拉克拉瓦整个从头上扯下,望着夜空——嘴角安静地、几乎不可察觉地弯起,然后他缓缓闭上眼睛,像终于允许自己睡去。最后的俯视全景里,一小张白纸被夜风卷着掠过画面。

场景背景
深夜。一栋包裹着脚手架和绿色防护网、正在整体翻修的战前公寓楼——它临街的公共楼道大门。杰克戴着黑色针织巴拉克拉瓦头套、左手提着长条硬箱,从楼内猛地推开这扇楼道大门冲上人行道——瞬间僵住:两米外,喘息未定的特伦斯双手举着一件黑色手持器械,直指他的脸。特写特伦斯——反打杰克:巴拉克拉瓦眼部开口里的双眼先是震住,随即认出来了——喜悦只在眼睛里,安静地亮起来。他缓缓抬手,把巴拉克拉瓦的下缘掀到鼻子——只露出下巴和嘴,眼睛和脸的上半仍在头套里,特伦斯认不出他——三声急促的闷响。杰克缓缓沉落到地面。特伦斯举着器械上前半步,俯视地上的人两拍——确认,不认识——然后转身跑进黑暗。杰克躺在人行道上,慢慢把巴拉克拉瓦整个从头上扯下,望着夜空——嘴角安静地、几乎不可察觉地弯起,然后他缓缓闭上眼睛,像终于允许自己睡去。最后的俯视全景里,一小张白纸被夜风卷着掠过画面。

风格
深夜——绝无日光。《七宗罪》与《搏击俱乐部》的芬奇气质:病态绿黄与铁灰,冷酷临床;色调《泰坦》式双温度沼泽——阴影深青蓝绿,受光面肮脏芥末黄,全画面无干净的白。前半段(镜头1至4)节奏绷紧,构图锁死;后半段(镜头5至9)时间粘稠——长镜头,极缓慢机械推近,死亡以近乎温柔的节奏展开。无手持。

摄影机与镜头
RED Gemini双原生高感光度,专为极暗夜景,Leica定制镜头加低反差滤镜:柔化反差,无刺眼高光,无光晕;复古2倍变形宽银幕:椭圆拉伸焦外,边缘猫眼光斑,失焦高光抹成水平长椭圆,轻微色差,柔和暗角,低饱和克制色彩,暗部干净无噪点。无镜头眩光,无光线拉丝。浅景深:人物保持清晰焦平面,街道融化在深暗绿灰的焦外。

灯光
深夜曝光锁定:整体欠曝两档,画面大部分沉在黑暗里。唯一暖色实际光源:一盏昏黄路灯,在特伦斯身后偏左——勾出他的肩线和器械上缘,他的脸大半沉在阴影;同一盏灯给倒下的杰克铺一小片浑浊的黄色光池——他死在全片唯一一块暖光里。楼道门内一片黑——楼里没有一盏灯亮着,这是一栋停工过夜的空楼。无高光点,黑位深沉但保留质感——巴拉克拉瓦的针织纹理、外套织纹、人行道颗粒、防护网的网眼在暗部隐约可读。自查:若任何一张脸被完整照亮——太亮。

首帧与空间调度
深夜。中景,机位在杰克背后偏右肩,楼道内的黑暗里:那扇旧楼道大门正被推开,门轴长鸣,门洞外框着脚手架钢管和防护网的影子;门外昏黄路灯下,特伦斯已站在两米外的人行道上,双手举着器械据定,正对门口,寸头轮廓被路灯从身后勾出,胸口剧烈起伏但双臂纹丝不动。杰克僵在门框里,巴拉克拉瓦只露双眼,硬箱悬在左手。

三十秒多镜头序列,共九个镜头。镜头1至4绷紧的对峙与爆发;镜头5至9缓慢的沉落与告别。全程同一地点:翻修楼的楼道门口、门前人行道、路灯。

动作时间轴
镜头1——0.0至2.5秒——中景,杰克背后偏右肩位,锁死:旧楼道大门被推开,门轴长长一声,门上糊纸的小玻璃窗晃了一下,门洞上方防护网的影子在他肩上掠过——特伦斯在路灯下,器械直指门口,喘息剧烈,双臂如石。杰克全身僵在门框里,硬箱悬停在左手中。
2.5秒硬切
镜头2——2.5至5.0秒——特写,特伦斯,极缓慢推近:路灯从身后偏左勾出寸头的轮廓、肩线和器械上缘,脸大半沉在阴影,只有下颌绷紧的线条和急促起伏的胸口;器械纹丝不动。他不说话——一个父亲在做算术。
5.0秒硬切
镜头3——5.0至8.5秒——反打,特写,杰克,缓慢推近:巴拉克拉瓦眼部开口里的双眼——先是震住,瞳孔缩紧;随后,认出来了。没有任何夸张:只是眼神安静地变了——戒备融开,眼里升起一点温度,像深夜里认出家门口的灯。全部喜悦只在这双眼睛里,克制,几乎温柔。他的右手松开,缓缓抬向巴拉克拉瓦的下缘——
8.5秒硬切
镜头4——8.5至11.5秒——中景,侧位,两人同框,身后是包着防护网的楼门,路灯在画面深处:杰克的右手把巴拉克拉瓦的下缘掀到鼻子——针织布料卷叠在鼻梁下,只露出胡茬的下巴和微微张开想说话的嘴,眼部开口与脸的上半仍被头套罩着,他仍是一个无法辨认的影子——三声急促压扁的闷响,三点急促的光在画面深处闪过。杰克的身体连着三次微微一顿,像被看不见的手推了三下。硬箱从左手脱落,砸在人行道上一声闷响。
11.5秒硬切
镜头5——11.5至14.5秒——中景偏特写,锁死:杰克缓缓沉落——先靠上楼道门的门框,肩膀擦着门上糊纸的玻璃滑下,膝盖触地,侧倒进路灯那片浑浊的黄色光池里;身后那扇旧门缓缓自行合拢,一声闷响。动作没有戏剧性,只有重量。卷到鼻梁的巴拉克拉瓦卡在原处,下巴裸露。
14.5秒硬切
镜头6——14.5至18.0秒——中近景,特伦斯,锁死:他举着器械上前半步,俯视地上一动不减的身影——两拍的评估:眼睛扫过卷起一半的巴拉克拉瓦、露出的下巴、旁边的长条硬箱——确认威胁终结;那张遮着的脸对他什么都不是,一个陌生的影子。胸口的起伏开始压平。然后他后退一步,转身,跑进黑暗——脚步声急促远去。街道空了。
18.0秒硬切
镜头7——18.0至21.5秒——特写,俯视偏侧,极缓慢推近:杰克躺在光池边缘,呼吸浅而费力。他抬起右手——不急了,很慢——把巴拉克拉瓦从头上整个扯下来,灰白短发散在人行道上,脸终于露在夜里。黑色针织头套留在摊开的手边,像一小团脱下的影子。
21.5秒硬切
镜头8——21.5至26.5秒——极近特写,正面俯视,极缓慢推近:他的脸在浑浊的黄光里,眼睛望着上方的夜空——夜空前是防护网和脚手架的暗影格栅。呼吸越来越浅。嘴角非常缓慢地、几乎不可察觉地向上弯了一点——安静的、疲惫的、终于可以停下来的微笑。他望了夜空最后一拍——然后眼睑缓缓地、自愿地合上,像一个终于允许自己睡去的人。微笑留在合眼的脸上。呼吸融进夜的底噪。
26.5秒硬切
镜头9——26.5至30.0秒——广一点的俯视全景,锁死,极缓慢升起半米:空荡的深夜人行道,包着脚手架和防护网的楼门口,一盏路灯,一小片黄色光池,杰克静静躺在光池里,双眼合着,那个安静的微笑还留在脸上,巴拉克拉瓦在手边,长条硬箱在两步外。夜风卷起一小张白色的纸——窄窄的一条,像一张收银小票——它翻滚着掠过光池边缘,擦过杰克身旁的人行道,飘出画面。远处一声城市低鸣。定格。切黑。

表演任务——杰克(全情投入;功课全在眼睛里):
目标:镜头3至4——让老友知道是自己:不是求生,是相认。
障碍:巴拉克拉瓦把他变成了该被射杀的影子;他只有两秒。
战术:镜头3——喜悦被压进眼睛:不允许身体庆祝,只有眼神的温度变化——从冰到认出家门口的灯;镜头4——掀头套的手是敞开的,掌心向外,动作不快——他相信站在对面的人;镜头7——扯下头套只为用自己的脸躺在这条街上;镜头8——微笑极小、极慢、平静,然后合眼是主动的:不是失去意识,是终于下班的人自己关了灯。
表演任务——特伦斯(镜头2、4、6;功课在算术里):
目标:威胁必须终结——女儿之外什么都不存在。
战术:镜头2至4——双眼死锁巴拉克拉瓦的眼部开口,只读一件事:那只手在动;深夜、蒙面、长条硬箱、抬起的手——算术只有一个答案。镜头6——评估是职业的最后一步:目标不动、面孔陌生、威胁清零;那两拍里没有胜利,只有清点;清点完成,人才涌上来——转身奔逃,逃的不是现场,是刚才那道题。
(安全线:双方目光始终投入任务,绝不僵死呆滞;自然眨眼;唯杰克镜头8的合眼例外。)

物理
旧楼道大门厚重,门轴有真实阻力,自行合拢时一声闷响;糊纸的玻璃窗随开合轻晃;硬箱脱手落地一声闷响,弹半下停住;杰克的沉落分三段——门框、膝盖、侧倒——每段有真实重量;巴拉克拉瓦掀到鼻梁时针织布料真实卷叠、卡住不滑落;整个扯下时布料拉扯带乱头发;眼睑合上是缓慢自主的动作,不是骤然松弛;那张窄纸片轻、薄,贴地翻滚,遇到光池边缘微微一跳,轨迹随夜风真实摆动;特伦斯上前半步与后退转身有真实重心转移;脚步声由近及远消失。

声音
镜头1:厚重门轴的长鸣、糊纸玻璃的轻晃,然后只有两个人的呼吸——巴拉克拉瓦下的闷息,狂奔后渐渐压平的喘息。镜头4:三声急促压扁的闷响,硬箱砸地。镜头5:布料与混凝土的摩擦,身后旧门自行合拢的一声闷响。镜头6:两拍近乎完全的静默;然后远去的脚步。镜头7至8:越来越浅的呼吸、针织布料的窸窣——合眼之后,呼吸声融进底噪,街道彻底安静。镜头9:只有夜风、纸片贴地翻滚的极轻沙沙声、防护网的轻响、远处城市低鸣。无音乐;全片段无一句台词。 <<<cd7d691a-d4f5-46ca-920c-00b72c36ebee>>>

时长：10秒。夜晚。狙击手巢穴内部，<<<974ac2f3-fa89-41ec-9531-e6d0ad0a7679>>> —— 与该素材完全一致的机位：摄影机就在窗外、贴着窗口，笔直向内看进巢穴；前景是纯黑剪影的窗框、窗台与窗棂，右缘挂着绿色防护网和一片破塑料布；窗台后面，长木射击台朝纵深伸去，台面空无一物。
灯光，硬性规则：房间内没有任何光源，也没有街灯漏进来——巢穴是一个黑洞，画面九成五是纯黑、毫无细节；开场时唯一可辨的东西就是窗框的剪影。绝对没有日光、没有明亮的环境光。调色：芬奇/克罗嫩威斯《搏击俱乐部》风格，污浊绿青色阴影、病态钠色偏色、压死的浑浊黑位、去饱和、细腻胶片颗粒。
0-4秒：几乎全黑。<<<cd7d691a-d4f5-46ca-920c-00b72c36ebee>>> 卧在射击台上、正对着我们（也就是正对着窗），步枪 <<<5cf041e3-3a8e-42ea-81ae-4c8bc52da795>>> 的枪管朝镜头伸出——他只是黑暗里一团更黑的形状，看不清脸，只有呼吸让肩膀极轻微地起伏，塑料布在纵深处轻轻晃动。
4-7秒：他身边的手机屏幕亮了——冷白微绿的屏光从下方打上他的脸，这是全片唯一的光源：突然之间，从黑暗里浮出来的是被屏幕从下方照亮的半张脸，眼窝深陷、颧骨发亮、其余仍在黑里；他低眼读屏，一动不动。
7-10秒：他把手机压在台面上、屏幕朝下，光灭了——他和整个房间重新沉进纯黑，只剩窗框的剪影和一次缓慢的呼气。定格。
他必须像活人：真实缓慢的呼吸，屏光下可见的呼吸白气、自然不规律的眨眼、眼球的细微移动。
声音：只有巢穴——贴近麦克风的缓慢呼吸、手机在木台面上短促的一声轻响、织物与两脚架的吱呀、塑料布声、远处下方闷闷的纽约夜。

一切被重运动模糊涂抹;每条边缘有强烈色差镶边;一圈柔和失焦晕影在四周游动,四角融化成模糊带色差的焦外,只一个不稳定的小中心勉强清晰;时间抽格、掉帧、地平线永不水平;高频耳鸣时时吞掉声音。

不演情绪,演贯彻战术的过程,戏在眼睛里。安全线:视线始终执行任务,绝不呆滞空洞;自然眨眼。

【ACTION / 动作】20秒,动作语法,机枪般急切
引爆(0–2秒):快特写——杰克(美军军服头盔),向前射击,枪口频闪照亮沾尘的脸。四声急促枪响,每次闪光撕开一格过去:白色天空/奔跑军靴/无声张嘴/——第四声,声音塌成耳鸣,已在战争里。
伏击(2–6秒):爆炸性的混乱,每格0.4至0.6秒,全带失焦色差晕影:武装分子从土墙后与屋顶开火,枪口火光在巷子两侧频闪;杰克贴墙据枪回击,弹壳旋出;身旁一名战友被打得猛地一顿、瘫向墙根,另一名战友拖住他向掩体后拽;尘土被弹雨犁起一条条。倾斜,抽格,天空猛甩。
交火(6–11秒):杰克压低冲过街口,朝巷子尽头持续开火——枪口连续的火光,一个武装分子的身影在火光里被打得旋身撞墙、滑下(不给特写,只在动作中一闪);杰克继续推进,呼吸粗重,眼睛冷硬,是纯粹的战斗机器。急切的正反打:他的脸、他的枪、翻滚的尘烟。
孩子(11–16秒,核心,骤然切入慢镜):就在他持续的火线里——几个阿富汗孩子突然从横巷冲出,穿过他射击的方向奔逃,慢动作,尘埃在他们周围悬浮,惊恐的小脸、飞扬的衣角;杰克的枪口还在闪,他猛地看见他们——时间凝滞——他的眼睛在照门之上骤然睁大,那副纯粹战斗机器的冷硬一瞬间碎裂。定格在孩子奔跑的慢镜与他震裂的眼睛之间。这一刻是伤口:二十年后他会在窗前再次僵住。
爆炸(16–20秒):慢镜猛地弹回实时——一团巨大爆炸在巷子里炸开,白色尘土与强光扑向镜头,冲击波掀翻画面——一记巨大的次声波撞击穿透耳鸣——画面在撞击瞬间炸成全黑。保持黑。

杰克与特伦斯是一队美军:统一美军沙漠迷彩、头盔、防弹背心,并肩一处,朝同一方向——巷子另一侧——作战。杰克是精确射手,特伦斯是他的掩护。敌人是伏击的武装分子:便装、缠头巾、无制服无头盔,躲在对面土墙后、屋顶、巷口开火。杰克与特伦斯从不互相射击——他们是一对搭档,共同对抗便装武装分子。

【SCENE / 场景】
战争闪回,阿富汗白天。杰克架枪在一处高点(半塌土楼的窗口),特伦斯贴身掩护;一支美军小队在下方土坯村庄突遭武装分子伏击。烈日、尘土、硝烟。整段是被创伤扭曲的记忆:模糊、抽格、耳鸣。由当下的四声枪响引爆。

【ACTION / 动作】22秒,动作语法,机枪般急切
引爆(0–2秒):快特写——杰克(美军军服头盔)贴着精确射手步枪的瞄准镜向前射击,枪口频闪照亮沾尘的脸。四声急促枪响,每次闪光撕开一格过去:白色天空/奔跑军靴/无声张嘴/——第四声,声音塌成耳鸣,已在战争里。
伏击爆发(2–6秒):爆炸性混乱,每格0.4至0.6秒,全带失焦色差晕影:巷子另一侧,缠头巾的便装武装分子从土墙后与屋顶开火,枪口火光在对面频闪;高点上,杰克据枪精确点射,弹壳弹出机匣旋落;身旁特伦斯半跪着朝侧翼短点射,替杰克挡住来袭方向,回头对他吼了句被耳鸣吞掉的话。清晰的两侧对抗。
狙击与掩护(6–11秒):正反打的急切节奏——杰克瞄准镜里,对面屋顶一个武装分子的身影被击中旋身翻倒出视野(只在动作中一闪,不给特写);特伦斯一把按住杰克的背心把他往窗侧一拽,一发流弹恰打碎他们头顶的土墙,碎土飞溅;两人重新据枪。他们像一台咬合的机器,一个射击一个掩护。
位置被打崩·特伦斯拖救(11–15秒):对面一波集火砸上他们的窗口,土墙成片炸裂,杰克被气浪掀得踉跄失衡、几乎从高点栽下。特伦斯一把抓住杰克的背心,把他整个人从暴露的窗口拖回掩体后——一边拖一边朝武装分子方向短点射压制。尘烟里那个宽肩身影死死拽住杰克不放。(观众此刻认不出这名搭档是谁。)

终身动机:掩护搭档是他的本分,搭档的命比自己的重。

GRADE, flashback look: warm GOLDEN Afghan daylight — honey-and-sand palette, creamy gold sun, dusty tan and khaki, warm sun-touched skin, soft warm bokeh, 16mm texture with fine grain and gentle halation; a memory soaked in gold. Handheld, alive, slightly loose framing. EDITED IN DISTINCT SHOT SIZES — every beat below is a separate camera position and a HARD CUT; the size changes every time, never a zoom, never a reframe within a beat.
MILITARY AUTHENTICITY throughout: real US Army field kit of the period, worn and used, never clean or costume-like — desert-tan camouflage uniforms dark with sweat and pale with dust, tan plate carriers, tan helmets with covers, dusty tan boots, dog tags, name tapes and unit patches; faces caked with dust and sweat, cracked lips, sunburn. WEAPONS COLOUR RULE: sniper rifles and carbines are SAND-COLOURED and dust-worn; only pistols are black.
0-5s | AERIAL WIDE, drone, HIGH AND VERY WIDE — this is a BIG base, a full brigade-sized airfield camp, and the shot has to sell that scale immediately: the camp runs from the bottom of the frame all the way to the horizon and off both edges, kilometres across, so no single part of it fits the picture. A long paved RUNWAY and taxiway down one side with transport aircraft parked in a row and helicopters lined up in revetments on a broad apron; hundreds of tan tents and containerised living blocks laid out in numbered grid streets; huge vehicle parks with rank after rank of Humvees, MRAPs and fuel trucks; hangars, aircraft shelters, warehouse tents, generator farms, water and fuel bladders, a communications field of masts and satellite domes, a gravel sports cage, a control tower. The whole thing ringed by kilometres of HESCO wall, razor wire, berms and sandbagged guard towers, with an ECP gate and a queue of trucks at one corner. Dust hanging over everything, long gold shadows off every structure, an American flag on a tall pole, small figures and vehicles moving along the grid streets — the people are tiny, which is what makes the size read. Pale desert plain and bare mountains all the way to the horizon beyond the wire. The drone flies slowly forward across it and then descends toward one small tent lost in one of the rows. This is the only aerial in the piece.

阴影沉入深青蓝绿,受光面是烈日晒白的赭黄与硫磺色;低饱和,黑位深沉但保留质感,重胶片颗粒。全画面无干净的白。

一切被重运动模糊涂抹;每条边缘有强烈色差镶边;一圈柔和失焦晕影在四周游动,四角融化成模糊带色差的焦外,只一个不稳定的小中心勉强清晰;时间抽格、掉帧、地平线永不水平;高频耳鸣时时吞掉声音。
■ 表演
不演情绪,演贯彻战术的过程,戏在眼睛里。安全线:视线始终执行任务,绝不呆滞空洞;自然眨眼。

动漫、漫画、赛璐璐、速度线、拖影线条、smear帧、插画平涂、游戏CG、塑料皮肤、过度锐化HDR;换脸、通用AI面孔;镜头耀光、横向光条、水平蓝白亮线、星芒、放射光、鬼影、光晕溢出、太阳直拍入画;文字、字幕、Logo、UI、边框、水印;音乐、配乐、旁白。

【FILM STYLE — 全片固定】
■ 比例与同一性
2.39:1，比例正确。人物脸与身体是真实人体比例,与角色参考图一致:骨相、眉眼间距、鼻梁、下颌线、肤色。若构图或风格会让脸偏离参考图,放弃指令,保住脸。此段是几年前的杰克,成熟、饱经战斗的男人。
■ 摄影机·胶片·镜头
RED Gemini 双原生高感,Leica 定制镜头,复古2倍变形宽银幕(强烈):竖椭圆焦外光斑、边缘猫眼、失焦高光横向抹成长条、明显色差、柔和暗角。镀膜洁净:无镜头耀光、无横向光条、无星芒。
■ 调色(《泰坦》与《搏击俱乐部》双温度沼泽)
阴影沉入深青蓝绿,受光面是烈日晒白的赭黄与硫磺色;低饱和,黑位深沉但保留质感,重胶片颗粒。全画面无干净的白。
■ 梦境记忆纹理(本段核心签名,贯穿全段)
这不是一场连贯的战斗,而是杰克被创伤反复回放的记忆碎片。画面在两种状态间不断切换:有的碎片被记忆异常锐利地定住,有的碎片深陷强烈失焦与运动模糊里——因为记忆已经抹掉了它们。一圈失焦色差晕影始终在四周游动,四角溶成模糊。碎片之间用变形镜头的过渡连接:横向的光带一抹而过、焦点从全糊猛拉到清晰再溃散、画面被甩接(whip)到下一格、偶尔一帧近白的闪光。时间抽格、掉帧、地平线永不水平。高频耳鸣时时吞掉声音。
■ 表演
不演情绪,演贯彻战术的过程,戏在眼睛里。安全线:视线始终执行任务,绝不呆滞空洞;自然眨眼。
■ 全片禁止
动漫、漫画、赛璐璐、速度线、拖影线条、smear帧、插画平涂、游戏CG、塑料皮肤、过度锐化HDR;换脸、通用AI面孔;镜头耀光、横向光条、水平蓝白亮线、星芒、放射光、鬼影、光晕溢出、太阳直拍入画;文字、字幕、Logo、UI、边框、水印;音乐、配乐、旁白。
本段无血、无伤口特写、无尸体——只呈现动作、位置、重心与掩护的变化,这是电影化的战争记忆。

【SCENE / 场景】
战争闪回,阿富汗白天,土坯村庄的伏击。作为被创伤反复回放的梦境碎片流呈现。由当下的四声枪响引爆。

【ACTION / 动作】20秒,极динамичный碎片流,变形镜头过渡
0–2秒 引爆:快特写,杰克贴瞄准镜向前射击,枪口频闪照脸。四声枪响,每闪一次撕开一格记忆碎片(白天空/奔跑军靴/无声张嘴),第四声声音塌成耳鸣——坠入梦境。
2–5秒 伏击碎片群(每格0.3–0.5秒,横向光带甩接):对面土墙后缠头巾武装分子的枪口火光(锐利)——甩接——杰克据枪点射、弹壳旋落(锐利)——甩接——一整片尘烟与奔跑的军靴(深度失焦、几乎认不出)——甩接——特伦斯半跪着朝侧翼短射,回头无声吼叫(半糊)。地平线乱倾。
5–8秒 焦点溃散的碎片:焦点从全糊猛拉到杰克瞄准镜里的一只眼(锐利定住一拍)——溃散成模糊——对面屋顶一个身影在火光里旋身翻出视野(一闪,深糊)——近白闪光——碎土从头顶土墙炸开、飞溅过镜头(锐利)。
8–11秒 特伦斯拖救(记忆里最模糊、最想抓住的一段):一波集火砸崩窗口,杰克被气浪掀得失衡;沙褐色军服的宽肩身影一把抓住他背心往回拖——但这段深陷强烈失焦与运动模糊,那张脸怎么也看不清,像记忆在这里被抹掉了;只有死死拽住不放的手是锐利的,其余全溶进变形焦外。耳鸣盖过一切。
11–15秒 孩子(核心,骤然切入慢镜,异常锐利):混乱中突然一段被记忆钉死的清晰慢镜——几个阿富汗孩子极度惊恐地奔逃,小脸因恐惧扭曲、张嘴无声尖叫、双臂抱头,尘埃在他们周围悬浮;切到杰克瞄准镜后骤然睁大、僵住的眼睛(同样异常锐利);两者在慢镜里交替定格。这一刻记忆不肯模糊——因为它最痛。这一刻是伤口。
15–18秒 崩解:慢镜猛地碎回实时,碎片加速甩接——枪火/尘烟/特伦斯的手/孩子的脸/瞄准镜——每格0.2秒,焦点疯狂拉扯,近白闪光频闪,一切开始解体。
18–20秒 空袭:一架战机低空掠过的巨响压过耳鸣,一连串航空炸弹沿街区成排落下,屋顶被逐个掀飞,爆炸墙由远及近推来,白光尘土席卷扑向镜头——一记接一记次声波撞击——画面在最后一击的瞬间炸成全黑。保持黑。

【CAMERA / 摄影】
动作语法为主:超广角贴身手持,机位随身体加速落定,荷兰角逐镜换向。碎片间的过渡是签名:横向光带甩接、拉焦(rack focus)从糊到清再溃散、whip甩接、近白闪帧。孩子段落切入慢动作、机位略稳但晕影色差不减。空袭机位被冲击波震得剧烈晃。全段地平线持续倾斜。

Duration: 30s. AFGHANISTAN, KABUL, DAY — an ambush during a street-clearing operation. GRADE, flashback look: warm GOLDEN Afghan daylight — honey-and-sand palette, creamy gold sun, dusty tan and khaki, warm sun-touched skin, 16mm texture with fine grain and gentle halation; a memory soaked in gold. Handheld, alive, real war-documentary energy, camera moving with the bodies. EDITED IN DISTINCT SHOT SIZES — every beat is a separate camera position and a HARD CUT, no zooms, no reframing inside a beat. Everything runs at normal speed EXCEPT the two beats marked SLOW MOTION at the end, which are Terrence's point of view.
THE PLACE: a narrow Kabul street of mud-brick and concrete buildings, shuttered shopfronts, a wrecked market stall, rubble and rebar, a half-collapsed compound wall, dust hanging gold in the air. A five-man American team is caught in the open and pinned in the shell of a gutted building on one side; the incoming comes from a rooftop and two window openings about two hundred metres up the street.
MILITARY AUTHENTICITY: real US Army field kit of the period, worn and used, never clean or costume-like — desert-tan camouflage uniforms dark with sweat and pale with dust, tan plate carriers with magazine pouches, radio, tourniquet, tan helmets with covers and mounts, ballistic glasses, gloves, knee pads, dusty boots, name tapes and unit patches; faces caked with dust and sweat. WEAPONS COLOUR RULE: the bolt-action sniper rifle and every carbine are SAND-COLOURED — flat dark-earth and tan furniture, tan rails, tan bipod, tan optics, dust-worn; the only BLACK weapon in the film is the pistol. THE OPPOSING FIGHTERS, always far off and never in close-up: insurgent fighters in mixed civilian clothing with chest rigs, armed mostly with AK-74 rifles, firing from a rooftop parapet and window openings up the street.
0-4s | WIDE, handheld, low: the street from behind the broken wall — gold dust, rubble, the team scattered along cover, muzzle flashes winking far up the street, concrete chips flying off the wall above their heads, everybody shouting. They are pinned and cannot move forward or back.
4-7s | MEDIUM ON TERRENCE behind a concrete pillar: <<<image_1>>> fires his sand-coloured carbine in short bursts, drops back into cover, rips the magazine out — and his hand comes off the rig empty.
TERRENCE (shouting): "I'm out! I'm dry!"
7-9s | MEDIUM ON JACK, prone on a slab of collapsed floor: <<<image_2>>> behind the sand-coloured bolt-action sniper rifle on its tan bipod, elbows planted in grit, calm inside the noise — settles, breaks a shot, cycles the bolt, shifts a few degrees, breaks another.
9-12s | LONG LENS DOWN THE STREET, not through any scope: the far rooftop and the two window openings, compressed and shimmering in the heat. NOW WE SEE THE HITS LAND: as each shot goes, the fighter at that position is struck and goes down — the one on the parapet is knocked backwards off his feet and tumbles over the edge, falling to the street below; the one in the first window is thrown back into the black of the room and drops out of frame; the one in the second window folds over the sill and slides down out of sight. Their weapons clatter loose. It is physical and unmistakable — they are hit and they fall. No blood, no wounds, no gore, no close-ups of anyone hit; the distance and the dust do the work.
12-14s | WIDE ON THE ROOFTOP, far up the street: another fighter rises with an AK-74, and the barrel swings round and settles ONTO the slab where <<<image_2>>> is lying.
14-16s | CLOSE-UP ON JACK: he does not see it. His eye is down behind the scope, his hand is cycling the bolt, he is hunting the next window — completely inside his own work.
16-18s | CLOSE-UP ON TERRENCE: he sees it. His eyes go rooftop, Jack, rooftop — and that is the whole decision; the body is already moving before the thought finishes.
18-21s | WIDE, handheld, following him: <<<image_1>>> comes up out of cover and runs at <<<image_2>>> across the open ground, three hard strides through the dust, and LAUNCHES himself flat across Jack's back as the far rifle goes off. The impact takes him between the shoulder blades and drives both men down onto the slab in a burst of dust. No blood, no wound, nothing graphic — the hit drives his body down and the dust goes up.
21-23s | CLOSE-UP, low on the slab: <<<image_2>>> pinned under his friend's weight, face in the grit; he shoves half out from under him but STAYS DOWN — he never gets up, never stands, never kneels. His gloved hand drags a BLACK pistol from the holster on his hip.
23-26s | LOW ANGLE, camera on the ground with him: still lying flat on his belly beside <<<image_1>>>, <<<image_2>>> rolls a shoulder, punches the black pistol out in both hands and fires twice up at the rooftop from the prone position. Far up the street the fighter is hit, snaps back and drops over the parapet into the street. The rooftop is empty. Silence rushes in.
26-28s | SLOW MOTION — POV OF TERRENCE, looking up from the ground: a low, unsteady, upside-tilted view of the sky, dust drifting gold, the broken roofline swaying — and <<<image_2>>>'s face leaning into that frame from above, filling it, shouting down at the lens with his hand gripping the camera-side shoulder. Everything soft at the edges, the sound dropped away and muffled, only his voice close:
JACK (shouting, holding him): "Hold on, brother. Hold on. I'm getting you out."
28-30s | SLOW MOTION — POV OF TERRENCE, still on the ground, being DRAGGED: right at the lens and badly out of focus, <<<image_2>>>'s hand fisted in his plate carrier and the mass of his shoulder and arm hauling backwards; behind them the street, the dust and the broken wall slide and jolt past with every pull, the sky tilting. ACTING TASK — JACK: he is running the job like a machine and refusing to be hurried — his whole attention is on windows and angles, one at a time, because that is the only way this street gets survived; the moment the weight lands on his back the machine stops and something much older takes over, and everything after that is one thing: get this man off the ground.
ACTING TASK — TERRENCE: he is out of ammunition and out of usefulness and he cannot stand it — his eyes hunt the street for the one thing he can still do, and the instant he finds it he does not weigh the cost, he goes; in the last two beats he is barely holding on to what he can see, and what he can see is his friend.

【ACTION / 动作】20秒,极динамичный碎片流,变形镜头过渡
0–2秒 引爆:快特写,杰克贴瞄准镜向前射击,枪口频闪照脸。四声枪响,每闪一次撕开一格记忆碎片(白天空/奔跑军靴/无声张嘴),第四声声音塌成耳鸣——坠入梦境。
2–5秒 伏击碎片群(每格0.3–0.5秒,横向光带甩接):对面土墙后缠头巾武装分子的枪口火光(锐利)——甩接——杰克据枪点射、弹壳旋落(锐利)——甩接——一整片尘烟与奔跑的军靴(深度失焦、几乎认不出)——甩接——特伦斯半跪着朝侧翼短射,回头无声吼叫(半糊)。地平线乱倾。
5–8秒 焦点溃散的碎片:焦点从全糊猛拉到杰克瞄准镜里的一只眼(锐利定住一拍)——溃散成模糊——对面屋顶一个身影在火光里旋身翻出视野(一闪,深糊)——近白闪光——碎土从头顶土墙炸开、飞溅过镜头(锐利)。
8–11秒 特伦斯拖救(记忆里最模糊、最想抓住的一段):一波集火砸崩窗口,杰克被气浪掀得失衡;沙褐色军服的宽肩身影一把抓住他背心往回拖——但这段深陷强烈失焦与运动模糊,那张脸怎么也看不清,像记忆在这里被抹掉了;只有死死拽住不放的手是锐利的,其余全溶进变形焦外。耳鸣盖过一切。

15–18秒 崩解:慢镜猛地碎回实时,碎片加速甩接——枪火/尘烟/特伦斯的手/孩子的脸/瞄准镜——每格0.2秒,焦点疯狂拉扯,近白闪光频闪,一切开始解体。
18–20秒 空袭:一架战机低空掠过的巨响压过耳鸣,一连串航空炸弹沿街区成排落下,屋顶被逐个掀飞,爆炸墙由远及近推来,白光尘土席卷扑向镜头——一记接一记次声波撞击——画面在最后一击的瞬间炸成全黑。保持黑。

杰克与特伦斯是一队美军,并肩朝同一方向作战;杰克精确射手,特伦斯掩护。敌人是便装缠头巾的武装分子,从对面开火。美军之间绝不互相射击。

【SCENE / 场景】
战争闪回,阿富汗白天,土坯村庄的伏击。作为大部分已被抹糊的梦境记忆碎片流呈现。由当下的四声枪响引爆。

【ACTION / 动作】20秒,以模糊为主导的碎片流,变形镜头过渡
0–2秒 引爆:快特写,杰克贴瞄准镜向前射击,枪口频闪照脸(半糊)。四声枪响,每闪一次撕开一格几乎全糊的记忆(化开的白天空/拖成光带的军靴/溶掉的张嘴),第四声声音塌成耳鸣——坠入模糊的梦境。
2–6秒 伏击的模糊碎片群(每格0.3–0.5秒,横向光带甩接,几乎全部厚重失焦):对面墙后一团晃动的枪口火光色块(认不清人)——甩接——杰克据枪的动作拖成长长的模糊光带,弹壳化成一道亮弧——甩接——一整片尘烟里奔跑的军靴,只剩晃动的暗块——甩接——特伦斯半跪短射的沙褐色身影,彻底化在尘烟里,脸不存在。地平线乱倾,一切在化开。
6–9秒 短促的锐利之刺:从满屏的模糊里,焦点猛地拉出一处——杰克瞄准镜里的一只眼,异常锐利,只钉住一拍——立刻溃散回模糊;近白闪光;头顶土墙炸开的碎土在极浅焦里飞过,大部分糊掉,只有一两块碎石一闪而清。
9–12秒 特伦斯拖救(记忆抹得最狠的一段,几乎全糊):一波集火砸崩窗口,杰克被掀得失衡;一个沙褐色的宽肩色块扑上来抓住他背心往回拖——但这段深陷最强烈的失焦与运动模糊,那张脸彻底不存在,连身形都在化开,像记忆在这里被整个抹掉;唯一从模糊里被钉清的,是死死拽住他背心不放的那只手——一拍锐利,随即又溶回糊。耳鸣盖过一切。
12–16秒 孩子(核心,唯一持续锐利的一段,骤然切入慢镜):在满段的模糊里,突然一段被记忆钉死的、异常清晰的慢镜——几个阿富汗孩子极度惊恐地奔逃,小脸因恐惧扭曲、张嘴无声尖叫、双臂抱头,尘埃在他们周围清晰悬浮;切到杰克瞄准镜后骤然睁大、僵住的眼睛(同样异常锐利);两者在慢镜里交替定格。全段唯有这里记忆不肯模糊——因为它最痛。这一刻是伤口。
16–18秒 崩解回模糊:清晰的孩子慢镜猛地被模糊吞回,碎片加速甩接,全部糊成晃动的光带——枪火/尘烟/拖救的手/孩子的残影/瞄准镜——每格0.2秒,焦点在糊里疯狂拉扯,近白闪光频闪。
18–20秒 空袭:一架战机低空掠过的巨响压过耳鸣,一连串航空炸弹沿街区成排落下,屋顶被逐个掀飞,爆炸墙由远及近推来(在模糊里化成一道道推近的白光墙),白光尘土席卷扑向镜头——一记接一记次声波撞击——画面在最后一击的瞬间炸成全黑。保持黑。

【CAMERA / 摄影】
动作语法为主:超广角贴身手持,机位随身体加速落定,荷兰角逐镜换向。全段以厚重失焦与运动模糊为主导,只有两三处最痛的瞬间被拉焦钉清一两拍。过渡是签名:横向光带甩接、焦点在糊与更糊间游移、whip甩接、近白闪帧。孩子段切入慢动作、异常锐利。空袭机位被冲击波震得剧烈晃。全段地平线持续倾斜。

【ACTING TASK — 杰克】
终身动机:训练把他磨成执行程序的战斗机器,不许迟疑。
本场目标:压制伏击、护住小队与搭档。
障碍:火线前突然冲出的、吓坏的孩子。
战术:整场冷硬如机器,眼睛只做测距锁定扣发;直到瞄准镜里出现惊恐的孩子,机器第一次卡死——这次卡死和二十年后窗前那次,是同一双眼睛、同一副瞄准镜。为什么整段记忆都糊成了光带、唯独孩子那段异常清晰:因为别的都能忘,那个忘不掉。
【ACTING TASK — 特伦斯】
终身动机:掩护搭档,搭档的命比自己重。
战术:位置一崩就抓住杰克往回拖,一次都不松手。
安全线:双方视线始终投入任务,绝不呆滞;自然眨眼;唯杰克看见孩子的定格例外。

【SOUND】
当下四声枪响清脆;第四声起硬切进统治全段的高频耳鸣。模糊碎片流的战斗声——枪火、弹壳、特伦斯被耳鸣吞掉的吼、碎土——忽近忽远、断续、发闷,像隔着水的记忆杂讯。孩子段骤然抽掉声音,只余一条高音与孩子模糊的脚步。空袭:低空战机巨大轰鸣压过一切,连环爆炸由远及近,一记接一记次声波撞击,然后死寂全黑。无音乐,无对白。

【FORBIDDEN / 禁止】
无血、无伤口、无尸体特写;美军之间绝不互相射击;武装分子中弹只在动作中一闪;不表现瞄准镜十字与孩子在同一构图对准锁定;空袭只展示屋顶被掀飞与尘土冲击波,不展示人被炸;无字幕、无音乐;地平线不得水平稳定。

BEARD RULE — ABSOLUTE: EVERY SINGLE MAN ON THIS SHEET HAS A BEARD, without exception. But no two beards are alike: long and full to the chest, squared off at the bottom, thick and short, wiry and unkempt, streaked with grey, fully white, a thin sparse beard joined only along the jaw, a young patchy beard, a dense beard with a shaved upper lip, a beard dyed with henna to a dull rust. DUST PASS — APPLIES TO ALL FIFTEEN, THIS IS THE LOOK OF THE WHOLE SHEET: nothing anybody wears is clean or saturated. Every garment is DUSTY, SUN-BLEACHED AND DESATURATED — a fine pale layer of desert dust worked into the weave, heaviest at the hems, knees, cuffs and shoulders, so the colours read chalky and greyed-down rather than bright. Clothes worn every day for years and washed in hard water: faded powdery earth tones, dye gone flat, sweat salt at the collars, old stains, mended seams, frayed hems, dust in the beards and on the sandals. Every colour named below is the FADED, DUSTED-DOWN version of that colour, never the vivid one. No fresh fabric, no clean whites — the whites are dirty cream and grey.

WARDROBE WORLD — the same clothing culture across all thirty, mixed and re-mixed so no two men look alike: long shalwar kameez in dirty cream, dust grey, faded olive, mud brown, washed-out slate; wool waistcoats, some quilted; a rough patu wool blanket over one shoulder or wrapped round the body; head coverings varied — flat woollen pakol caps, embroidered skullcaps, black or white or dust-brown turbans wound differently on every man, plain scarves wrapped over the head and PULLED DOWN CLEAR OF THE FACE for this plate, some men bare-headed; footwear varied — cracked leather sandals, plastic sandals, cheap trainers, scuffed boots, one man in odd mismatched shoes. GEAR: worn canvas or leather chest rigs and bandoliers with curved magazines, cloth pouches, a canvas shoulder bag, a water bottle on a strap, a cheap plastic wristwatch, a knife on a belt. NOTHING WESTERN OR MILITARY-ISSUE: no camouflage uniforms, no plate carriers, no helmets, no ballistic goggles, no night-vision, no radios with antennas, no branded tactical gear — this is irregular kit assembled by hand out of what exists.

WEAPONS — as film props, plainly and neutrally described, spread across the row so it never reads as fifteen copies: mostly worn AK-pattern rifles with wooden furniture darkened by handling and dull scratched steel, chipped stocks, taped magazines; among them older long bolt-action rifles with full wooden stocks, SKS-type rifles, a belt-fed machine gun carried across the shoulders, and RPG-type launcher tubes carried on the shoulder with the muzzle up and well clear of everyone. Metal is dull and worn, wood is scuffed and hand-oiled, nothing is new, nothing is black-and-tactical, no optics on any weapon except one battered old scope, no rails, no lasers, no modern accessories.

VARIETY LOCK — THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS SHEET: fifteen unrelated men from fifteen different villages, NOT one man rendered fifteen times. DIFFERENT FACES: different face shapes — long and narrow, oval, square, broad and flat-cheeked, angular and sharp-boned, gaunt, round-but-lean — different noses (hooked, aquiline, snub, flat, thin-bridged, straight), different eye shapes, brows, mouths and hairlines; a real range of Afghan colouring from pale olive through honey and ruddy sunburn to deep sun-darkened brown, and one man with pale grey-green eyes; DIFFERENT BEARDS on every man, no two the same length, shape or density, all of them young men's beards. DIFFERENT HOSTILE EXPRESSIONS as specified — all hard, none identical, none performed. DIFFERENT LEAN BUILDS: whip-thin, wiry, sinewy, rangy, loose-limbed, compactly athletic, broad-shouldered but flat-stomached — the variation is in frame and bone, never in fat. DIFFERENT HEIGHTS AND NOT A STAIRCASE — the height order is uneven and random, the tallest is not at either end, no two men are the same height, and the spread between tallest and shortest is obvious at a glance. DIFFERENT CLOTHES, HEADS AND SCARVES: no two turbans wound alike, no two garments the same faded colour, no two checked scarves the same pattern or worn the same way, no two pairs of shoes alike. SAME WEAPON, DIFFERENT RIFLES: all fifteen on the AK-74, every rifle different in furniture, magazine and wear.

PROPORTION LOCK: all fifteen stand at the same distance from the camera on one line, shot from far enough back on a normal lens that NOBODY is stretched, widened or bent — the figures at the ends of the frame have exactly the same true proportions as the figures in the middle. Every man anatomically normal: correct hands with five fingers, correct arms and necks, the rifle the correct size relative to the body, both hands correctly placed on it.

Fine photographic detail: skin texture, cloth weave, the woven grid of the scarves, worn wood, dull scratched steel.

Photorealistic full-length CASTING AND WARDROBE REFERENCE SHEET for a war film, shot in a photographic studio against a seamless DARK GREY backdrop, identical in look, lighting and background to a professional character reference plate: FIFTEEN young Afghan irregular fighters, ALL AGED BETWEEN TWENTY AND THIRTY, standing in ONE SINGLE STRAIGHT ROW, evenly spaced across the frame, never overlapping, ALL FIFTEEN FACING THE CAMERA DEAD-ON, FRONT VIEW ONLY. Every figure is FULL LENGTH — the whole body in frame from the top of the head to the shoes, feet flat on a plain dark grey floor of the same tone as the backdrop, nothing cropped, nobody cut by the frame edge. Soft even studio light from the front, gentle falloff, no hard shadows on the backdrop, no rim light, no coloured light, all fifteen lit exactly the same and rendered at exactly the same scale and the same true human proportion.

BODY RULE — ABSOLUTE: these are young fighters who walk twenty kilometres a day and eat badly. EVERY MAN IS LEAN AND HARD WITH A FLAT STOMACH — whip-thin, wiry, sinewy, rangy or compactly athletic. Visible collarbones, tendons in the forearms, hollow under the cheekbone, narrow waists, dense flat muscle without bulk. ABSOLUTELY NOBODY IS FAT: no bellies, no paunch, no gut, no soft middle, no double chin, no jowls, no heavy hips, nobody overweight, and equally nobody bodybuilt or gym-inflated. Nobody looks older than thirty — no grey beards, no white beards, no old men, no lined elderly faces, no stooped posture.

FACES — HARD AND HOSTILE, THIS IS THE MOOD OF THE WHOLE SHEET: nobody smiles, nobody is blank or neutral, nobody is friendly. Every man looks straight down the lens with a hard, cold, unwelcoming stare — jaw set, mouth closed and tight, brow low, eyes direct and unblinking, the look of men who have already decided about you. The hostility is DIFFERENT ON EVERY FACE and never a mask: one openly furious with the nostrils flared, one flat and dead-eyed, one coldly contemptuous with the chin lifted, one stony and patient, one seething with the jaw muscle showing, one bored and dangerous, one narrow-eyed and calculating, one hollow and burnt-out, one glaring from under the brow, one grimly amused with no warmth in it, one sullen, one appraising and unimpressed. Real human faces holding a real look, not actors pulling a face — no grimacing, no snarling, no bared teeth, no open mouths, no shouting, no theatrics.

BEARD RULE — ABSOLUTE: EVERY SINGLE MAN HAS A BEARD, without exception, and they are all young men's beards — black or dark brown, none grey, none white. No two are alike: full and long, thick and short, dense and squared off at the bottom, wiry and unkempt, curly, patchy and joined only along the jaw, thin and sparse, a heavy beard with a shaved upper lip, a beard dyed with henna to a dull rust, a soft young beard that has never been cut. Nobody clean-shaven, nobody with stubble only, nobody with a moustache alone.

ETHNIC AND REGIONAL FACE TYPE — WRITTEN PLAINLY: these are TALIBAN FIGHTERS. They are rural southern Afghan PASHTUN men out of Kandahar and Helmand, and the faces have to read as that specific type at a glance, not as generic extras. Strong heavy brow ridges with the eyes set deep underneath, hard high cheekbones, long narrow faces, long jaws, thin mouths, aquiline and hooked noses with high bridges, big ears, prominent Adam's apples on the thin ones. Skin ruined by wind, altitude and sun — weathered, dry, coarse-pored, sun lines fanning from the outer corner of the eye even on the twenty-year-olds, cracked lips, dust in the creases. Hair and beards black or very dark brown, eyebrows thick, straight and dark, often nearly meeting. Eyes mostly dark brown, but two or three men have the pale grey-green or light hazel eyes that genuinely occur among Pashtuns, and on those faces it reads colder. SEVERAL OF THEM WEAR SURMA: a thin smudged line of black kohl along the upper and lower lash line, an ordinary practice among Pashtun men and a signature look on Taliban fighters — it makes the eyes read harder, blacker and more direct, and it should be clearly visible on four or five of the fifteen and absent on the rest. NOT Arab faces, NOT urban Persian or Iranian faces, NOT Turkish, NOT Indian, NOT Central Asian or Turkic or Hazara faces with epicanthic folds and flat features, NOT smooth modern city faces, NOT western actors in beards — southern Pashtun village men.

SCARF RULE — NOT EVERYONE, AND THAT IS THE POINT: only SOME of them wear a large CHECKED COTTON SCARF — a shemagh / keffiyeh-type cloth with a woven grid or crosshatch check and knotted fringe at the ends — wound round the NECK and shoulders. All of them DARK, dusty and low-saturation: black-and-charcoal check, black-and-deep-grey check, dark umber-brown check, near-black olive check, dark oxblood-and-black check, a very dark check so dusty the pattern barely reads. No white in any scarf — where a check would normally be white it is dirty dark grey. NO TWO SCARVES SHARE A PATTERN, A COLOUR OR A WAY OF BEING WORN: loose round the neck with both fringed ends down the chest; wound twice tight to the throat; one end thrown back over a shoulder; bunched up under the chin; hanging open like a towel; tucked into the collar of a waistcoat; and exactly ONE man wears it pulled up over the chin and mouth with his eyes and the rest of his face completely clear.
WHO GETS A SCARF AND WHO DOES NOT — THIS OVERRIDES THE SCARF NAMED IN ANY ROSTER LINE BELOW: only men 1, 4, 7, 10, 13 and 15 wear the CHECKED scarf. Men 3, 6 and 12 wear instead a PLAIN DARK CLOTH — no check, no pattern — wound loosely round the neck, one of them a strip torn off a blanket. Men 2, 5, 8, 9, 11 and 14 wear NOTHING ON THE NECK AT ALL: bare open collar, throat and collarbones showing, dust on the skin. Nobody outside the six named men has a checked scarf anywhere on his body.

WEAPON RULE — ABSOLUTE, THE SAME WEAPON FOR ALL FIFTEEN: every man holds an AK-74 assault rifle IN HIS HANDS — the AK-74 specifically, with its slotted muzzle brake and curved magazine. He holds it with BOTH HANDS across the front of his body at waist height, one hand at the handguard and one at the grip, the MUZZLE ANGLED DOWN TOWARD THE FLOOR and clear of everyone. Nobody has it shouldered, nobody aims, nobody points it at the camera or at another figure, no finger inside a trigger guard. No other weapon appears on this sheet. THE RIFLES ARE NOT IDENTICAL COPIES: they differ in furniture, magazine and wear — orange-brown laminated wood handguards and stocks, black polymer furniture, plum-coloured polymer magazines, steel magazines, one with two magazines taped together, one with a folding stock, one with a stock repaired with wire and tape, one with a split handguard bound with cord, one with a rusted muzzle brake. Every one dull, scratched, hand-worn, bluing rubbed off the edges, dust in the seams. No optics, no rails, no lasers, no modern accessories, nothing new, nothing black-and-tactical.

DUST PASS — APPLIES TO ALL FIFTEEN: nothing anybody wears is clean or saturated. Every garment is DUSTY, SUN-BLEACHED AND DESATURATED — a fine pale layer of desert dust worked into the weave, heaviest at the hems, knees, cuffs and shoulders, so colours read chalky and greyed-down rather than bright. Clothes worn every day for years and washed in hard water: faded powdery earth tones, dye gone flat, sweat salt at the collars, old stains, mended seams, frayed hems, dust in the beards and on the sandals. VARIETY LOCK — THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS SHEET: fifteen unrelated men from fifteen different villages, NOT one man rendered fifteen times. DIFFERENT FACES: different face shapes — long and narrow, square, broad and flat-cheeked, angular, gaunt, high-cheekboned — different noses, eye shapes, brows, mouths and hairlines; a real range of Afghan colouring from pale olive through honey and ruddy sunburn to deep sun-darkened brown; DIFFERENT BEARDS on every man, no two the same length, shape or density, all of them young men's beards; individual marks: a scar, a broken nose, a missing tooth, an old burn, a crooked eyebrow. DIFFERENT HOSTILE EXPRESSIONS as specified — all hard, none identical, none performed. DIFFERENT LEAN BUILDS: whip-thin, wiry, sinewy, rangy, compactly athletic, broad-shouldered but flat-stomached — the variation is in frame and bone, never in fat. DIFFERENT HEIGHTS AND NOT A STAIRCASE — the height order is uneven and random, the tallest is not at either end, no two men are the same height, and the spread between tallest and shortest is obvious at a glance. DIFFERENT CLOTHES, HEADS AND SCARVES: no two turbans wound alike, no two garments the same faded colour, no two checked scarves the same pattern or worn the same way, no two pairs of shoes alike. SAME WEAPON, DIFFERENT RIFLES: all fifteen on the AK-74, every rifle different in furniture, magazine and wear.

PROPORTION LOCK: all fifteen stand at the same distance from the camera on one line, shot from far enough back on a normal lens that NOBODY is stretched, widened or bent — the figures at the ends of the frame have exactly the same true proportions as the figures in the middle. Every man anatomically normal: correct hands with five fingers, correct arms and necks, the rifle the correct size relative to the body, both hands correctly placed on it.

MATERIALS AND CASTING TRUTH: real Afghan faces, fifteen clearly different individuals, none of them models or actors in costume — sun-ruined skin, cracked lips, dust in the beards and eyebrows, dirt under the nails, hard working hands, mended seams, thin faded fabric. Fine photographic detail: skin texture, cloth weave, the woven grid of the scarves, worn wood, dull scratched steel.

no Arab, Persian, Turkish, Indian, Turkic or Hazara facial types, no epicanthic folds, no smooth modern city faces, no western actors in false beards; no camouflage uniforms, no plate carriers, no helmets, no ballistic goggles, no night-vision, no radios, no modern optics, rails, lasers or western tactical gear; Photorealistic full-length CASTING AND WARDROBE REFERENCE SHEET for a war film, shot in a photographic studio against a seamless DARK GREY backdrop, identical in look, lighting and background to a professional character reference plate: FIFTEEN young Afghan irregular fighters, ALL AGED BETWEEN TWENTY AND THIRTY, standing in ONE SINGLE STRAIGHT ROW, evenly spaced across the frame, never overlapping, ALL FIFTEEN FACING THE CAMERA DEAD-ON, FRONT VIEW ONLY. Every figure is FULL LENGTH — the whole body in frame from the top of the head to the shoes, feet flat on a plain dark grey floor of the same tone as the backdrop, nothing cropped, nobody cut by the frame edge. Soft even studio light from the front, gentle falloff, no hard shadows on the backdrop, no rim light, no coloured light, all fifteen lit exactly the same and rendered at exactly the same scale and the same true human proportion.

BODY RULE — ABSOLUTE: these are young fighters who walk twenty kilometres a day and eat badly. EVERY MAN IS LEAN AND HARD WITH A FLAT STOMACH — whip-thin, wiry, sinewy, rangy or compactly athletic. Visible collarbones, tendons in the forearms, hollow under the cheekbone, narrow waists, dense flat muscle without bulk. ABSOLUTELY NOBODY IS FAT: no bellies, no paunch, no gut, no soft middle, no double chin, no jowls, no heavy hips, nobody overweight, and equally nobody bodybuilt or gym-inflated. Nobody looks older than thirty — no grey beards, no white beards, no old men, no lined elderly faces, no stooped posture.

FACES — HARD AND HOSTILE, THIS IS THE MOOD OF THE WHOLE SHEET: nobody smiles, nobody is blank or neutral, nobody is friendly. Every man looks straight down the lens with a hard, cold, unwelcoming stare — jaw set, mouth closed and tight, brow low, eyes direct and unblinking, the look of men who have already decided about you. The hostility is DIFFERENT ON EVERY FACE and never a mask: one openly furious with the nostrils flared, one flat and dead-eyed, one coldly contemptuous with the chin lifted, one stony and patient, one seething with the jaw muscle showing, one bored and dangerous, one narrow-eyed and calculating, one hollow and burnt-out, one glaring from under the brow, one grimly amused with no warmth in it, one sullen, one appraising and unimpressed. Real human faces holding a real look, not actors pulling a face — no grimacing, no snarling, no bared teeth, no open mouths, no shouting, no theatrics.

BEARD RULE — ABSOLUTE: EVERY SINGLE MAN HAS A BEARD, without exception, and they are all young men's beards — black or dark brown, none grey, none white. No two are alike: full and long, thick and short, dense and squared off at the bottom, wiry and unkempt, curly, patchy and joined only along the jaw, thin and sparse, a heavy beard with a shaved upper lip, a beard dyed with henna to a dull rust, a soft young beard that has never been cut. Nobody clean-shaven, nobody with stubble only, nobody with a moustache alone.

ETHNIC AND REGIONAL FACE TYPE — WRITTEN PLAINLY: these are TALIBAN FIGHTERS. They are rural southern Afghan PASHTUN men out of Kandahar and Helmand, and the faces have to read as that specific type at a glance, not as generic extras. Strong heavy brow ridges with the eyes set deep underneath, hard high cheekbones, long narrow faces, long jaws, thin mouths, aquiline and hooked noses with high bridges, big ears, prominent Adam's apples on the thin ones. Skin ruined by wind, altitude and sun — weathered, dry, coarse-pored, sun lines fanning from the outer corner of the eye even on the twenty-year-olds, cracked lips, dust in the creases. Hair and beards black or very dark brown, eyebrows thick, straight and dark, often nearly meeting. Eyes mostly dark brown, but two or three men have the pale grey-green or light hazel eyes that genuinely occur among Pashtuns, and on those faces it reads colder. SEVERAL OF THEM WEAR SURMA: a thin smudged line of black kohl along the upper and lower lash line, an ordinary practice among Pashtun men and a signature look on Taliban fighters — it makes the eyes read harder, blacker and more direct, and it should be clearly visible on four or five of the fifteen and absent on the rest. NOT Arab faces, NOT urban Persian or Iranian faces, NOT Turkish, NOT Indian, NOT Central Asian or Turkic or Hazara faces with epicanthic folds and flat features, NOT smooth modern city faces, NOT western actors in beards — southern Pashtun village men.

SCARF RULE — NOT EVERYONE, AND THAT IS THE POINT: only SOME of them wear a large CHECKED COTTON SCARF — a shemagh / keffiyeh-type cloth with a woven grid or crosshatch check and knotted fringe at the ends — wound round the NECK and shoulders. All of them DARK, dusty and low-saturation: black-and-charcoal check, black-and-deep-grey check, dark umber-brown check, near-black olive check, dark oxblood-and-black check, a very dark check so dusty the pattern barely reads. No white in any scarf — where a check would normally be white it is dirty dark grey. NO TWO SCARVES SHARE A PATTERN, A COLOUR OR A WAY OF BEING WORN: loose round the neck with both fringed ends down the chest; wound twice tight to the throat; one end thrown back over a shoulder; bunched up under the chin; hanging open like a towel; tucked into the collar of a waistcoat; and exactly ONE man wears it pulled up over the chin and mouth with his eyes and the rest of his face completely clear.
WHO GETS A SCARF AND WHO DOES NOT — THIS OVERRIDES THE SCARF NAMED IN ANY ROSTER LINE BELOW: only men 2, 5, 9, 11 and 14 wear the CHECKED scarf. Men 4, 8 and 13 wear instead a PLAIN DARK CLOTH — no check, no pattern — wound loosely round the neck, one of them a strip torn off a blanket. Men 1, 3, 6, 7, 10, 12 and 15 wear NOTHING ON THE NECK AT ALL: bare open collar, throat and collarbones showing, dust on the skin. Nobody outside the five named men has a checked scarf anywhere on his body.

WEAPON RULE — ABSOLUTE, THE SAME WEAPON FOR ALL FIFTEEN: every man holds an AK-74 assault rifle IN HIS HANDS — the AK-74 specifically, with its slotted muzzle brake and curved magazine. He holds it with BOTH HANDS across the front of his body at waist height, one hand at the handguard and one at the grip, the MUZZLE ANGLED DOWN TOWARD THE FLOOR and clear of everyone. Nobody has it shouldered, nobody aims, nobody points it at the camera or at another figure, no finger inside a trigger guard. No other weapon appears on this sheet. THE RIFLES ARE NOT IDENTICAL COPIES: they differ in furniture, magazine and wear — orange-brown laminated wood handguards and stocks, black polymer furniture, plum-coloured polymer magazines, steel magazines, one with two magazines taped together, one with a folding stock, one with a stock repaired with wire and tape, one with a split handguard bound with cord, one with a rusted muzzle brake. Every one dull, scratched, hand-worn, bluing rubbed off the edges, dust in the seams. No optics, no rails, no lasers, no modern accessories, nothing new, nothing black-and-tactical.

DUST PASS — APPLIES TO ALL FIFTEEN: nothing anybody wears is clean or saturated. Every garment is DUSTY, SUN-BLEACHED AND DESATURATED — a fine pale layer of desert dust worked into the weave, heaviest at the hems, knees, cuffs and shoulders, so colours read chalky and greyed-down rather than bright. Clothes worn every day for years and washed in hard water: faded powdery earth tones, dye gone flat, sweat salt at the collars, old stains, mended seams, frayed hems, dust in the beards and on the sandals. DARK VALUE RULE — OVERRIDES EVERY COLOUR NAMED ANYWHERE BELOW: the whole sheet sits in the DARK half of the scale. Every garment, every turban, every scarf, every waistcoat and every blanket is a DEEP, DARK, DUSTY tone — charcoal, near-black, dark slate, deep grey-brown, dark olive gone almost black, deep umber, dark ash, dust-blackened indigo. The dust on them reads as a pale grey film ON TOP of a dark cloth, never as a pale cloth. Wherever a garment is named below as cream, grey, olive, brown or slate, render it as the DARK version of that tone, several stops down — dark dusty cream is a dirty deep sand-brown, dust-grey is charcoal grey, olive is near-black olive, mud brown is deep umber, slate is dark blue-black. NOTHING PALE, NOTHING LIGHT, NOTHING WHITE, no bright fabric, nothing lighter than a mid-dark tone anywhere on the sheet; the lightest thing in the frame is the dust film and the men's skin. Overall the row reads DARK against the dark grey backdrop, held apart from it only by the dust, the texture and the front light.

WARDROBE WORLD: long shalwar kameez in charcoal, near-black, dark slate blue-black, deep umber brown, dark olive gone almost black, dirty deep sand-brown, hanging loose on lean bodies; thin dark wool waistcoats; a rough patu wool blanket over one shoulder; heads varied — black, white or dust-brown turbans wound differently on every man, embroidered skullcaps, one flat woollen pakol cap only, several men bare-headed; footwear varied — cracked leather sandals, plastic sandals, cheap trainers, scuffed boots, one man in odd mismatched shoes. GEAR AND LOAD-BEARING — THIS IS THE SECOND MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THE SHEET AFTER THE FACES, AND IT MUST BE VISIBLY DIFFERENT MAN TO MAN. Everybody carries spare magazines and everybody carries them differently, all of it home-assembled, canvas and leather, all of it DARK and dust-worn. The types available, all period-correct and none of them western-issue:
— A CANVAS AK CHEST RIG worn over the shalwar kameez: a dark olive or charcoal canvas vest-front with three large square magazine pockets across the chest, two smaller grenade pockets, buckled canvas straps over the shoulders and round the waist, flaps closed with a strip of webbing and a tab, the canvas gone soft and pale at the fold lines.
— A HEAVIER FOUR-POCKET CANVAS CHEST RIG of the same family, taller on the chest, one flap missing, replaced with a strip of cloth.
— A DARK WOOL WAISTCOAT USED AS THE RIG ITSELF: an ordinary sleeveless waistcoat with curved magazines shoved straight into the inside chest pockets so the shape of them prints through the cloth, one magazine sticking out at the top, pockets sagging and stretched out of shape.
— A LEATHER BANDOLIER over one shoulder and across the chest, hand-stitched, with loops and small closed pouches, the leather cracked and grey with dust.
— A LEATHER BELT AROUND THE WAIST with two or three canvas pouches on it, plus a knife in a leather sheath.
— A CLOTH SHOULDER BAG on a long strap hanging at the hip with the corners of magazines showing through the fabric.
— A LENGTH OF CLOTH WOUND ROUND THE WAIST as a sash with a spare magazine pushed into it and nothing else.
HOW IT IS SPREAD ACROSS THIS ROW — assign exactly like this, and note it is a DIFFERENT spread from the other sheet: men 2, 6 and 13 wear the three-pocket canvas chest rig, each a different dark colour and a different state of wear; men 4 and 11 wear the heavier four-pocket rig; men 1, 9 and 12 use the dark wool waistcoat as the rig with magazines printing through the pockets; men 5, 7 and 14 wear the leather bandolier across the chest; men 3 and 15 have only the belt with canvas pouches; man 8 has the cloth shoulder bag; man 10 has just the cloth sash at the waist with one magazine in it. Extras scattered so no two men are kitted the same: a dented water bottle on a strap on one man, a small canvas satchel on another, a cheap plastic wristwatch, a coil of rope, a folded blanket strap.
NOTHING WESTERN OR MILITARY-ISSUE: no plate carriers, no modern nylon or MOLLE webbing, no plastic buckles, no camouflage uniforms, no helmets, no ballistic goggles, no night-vision, no radios with antennas, no pouches with velcro, no branded tactical gear — everything is canvas, leather, cloth, metal buckles and hand stitching.

【阵营,必须清晰区分】
杰克与他的战友是一队美军士兵:统一的美军沙漠迷彩、头盔、防弹背心,他们是一起的,彼此掩护,朝同一个方向——巷子外——射击。
敌人是伏击的武装分子:便装、缠头巾、无制服无头盔,躲在土墙后、屋顶与巷口,从另一个方向朝美军射击。
杰克与美军战友从不互相射击——他们是并肩的一队,共同对抗那些便装武装分子。方向必须清晰:美军在掩体这侧,武装分子在巷子另一侧。

【SCENE / 场景】
战争闪回,阿富汗白天。一支美军小队在土坯村庄突遭武装分子伏击。烈日、尘土、硝烟、土墙、窄巷。整段是被创伤扭曲的记忆:模糊、抽格、耳鸣。由当下的四声枪响引爆。

【ACTION / 动作】22秒,动作语法,机枪般急切
引爆(0–2秒):快特写——杰克(美军军服头盔),向前射击,枪口频闪照亮沾尘的脸。四声急促枪响,每次闪光撕开一格过去:白色天空/奔跑军靴/无声张嘴/——第四声,声音塌成耳鸣,已在战争里。
伏击(2–6秒):爆炸性混乱,每格0.4至0.6秒,全带失焦色差晕影:缠头巾的便装武装分子从巷子另一侧的土墙后与屋顶开火,枪口火光在对面频闪;这一侧,杰克和几名美军战友贴着掩体一起回击,朝武装分子那个方向射击,弹壳旋出。清晰的两侧对抗。
战友中弹与拖救(6–11秒):杰克身旁一名美军战友被对面的火力打得猛地一顿、瘫向墙根。杰克一把抓住这名战友的背心,一边朝武装分子方向短点射压制,一边把战友向掩体后拖拽——这名中弹的战友是一个宽肩的黑人士兵,但此刻在尘烟、动作模糊与失焦色差晕影里看不清脸,只是一个被杰克死死拖住、不肯松手的沉重身影。杰克拖着他退到土墙后,尘土在两人身下犁开。(观众此刻认不出这名战友是谁。)
交火与推进(11–15秒):把战友放到掩体后,杰克压低冲过街口,朝巷子尽头的武装分子持续开火;一个武装分子的身影在火光里旋身撞墙滑下(不给特写,只在动作中一闪)。杰克继续推进,呼吸粗重,眼睛冷硬,纯粹的战斗机器。
孩子(15–20秒,  <<<image_2>>> <<<image_3>>> 核心,骤然切入慢镜):就在他持续的火线前方——几个阿富汗孩子突然从横巷冲出,穿过战场奔逃,慢动作,尘埃在他们周围悬浮,惊恐的小脸、飞扬的衣角;杰克猛地看见他们——时间凝滞——他的眼睛在照门之上骤然睁大,那副战斗机器的冷硬一瞬碎裂。定格在孩子奔跑的慢镜与他震裂的眼睛之间。这一刻是伤口:二十年后他会在窗前再次僵住。
爆炸(20–22秒):慢镜猛地弹回实时——一团巨大爆炸在巷子里炸开,白光与尘土扑向镜头,冲击波掀翻画面——一记巨大次声波撞击穿透耳鸣——画面在撞击瞬间炸成全黑。保持黑。

【CAMERA / 摄影】
动作语法:超广角,贴身手持,机位随身体加速与落定,荷兰角逐镜换向。伏击与交火最急最抖;拖救段跟着杰克后退的重心;孩子段切入慢动作、机位略稳但晕影色差不减;爆炸回实时。全段地平线持续倾斜。

【ACTING TASK — 杰克】
终身动机:训练把他磨成执行程序的战斗机器,不许迟疑。
本场目标:打退伏击,守住战友,把中弹的兄弟拖回掩体,清掉火力点。
障碍:火线前方突然出现的孩子——不该在战场上的东西。
战术:整场他是冷硬的机器,眼睛只做测距、掩护、拖拽、推进;拖战友时他一秒都不松手——守住兄弟是他唯一没有变冷的地方;直到看见孩子,机器第一次卡死——这次卡死和二十年后窗前那次是同一双眼睛。

7-10s | THE WINDOW. WIDE, LOW, FROM INSIDE THE GROUND-FLOOR ROOM looking out through a sandbagged window hole: a SEAL is standing at the window hole firing his carbine out into the lane, helmet on, goggles down, brass flicking off to one side, sandbags bursting and pouring beside him as rounds come in. AND HE IS HIT. He stops firing mid-burst, comes off the weapon, and goes straight down out of the frame below the sill — the carbine dropping with him. THAT IS THE WHOLE BEAT. Nobody runs to him, nobody drags him, nobody shouts, the camera does not follow him down, and he is not shown on the floor. The window hole he was standing in is simply empty and the dust keeps pouring off the sandbags.

10-14s | SLOW MOTION — JACK IS HIT. Tight, close, low behind the parapet, EXTREME SLOW MOTION, all of it read on him and his kit: <<<93edeb87-e0e7-4ded-9569-527aca55e457>>> is up on his elbows on the rifle when the round arrives in his RIGHT SHOULDER. The impact goes through his body before his face knows about it — the shoulder is driven violently backwards and down, dust and a small burst of torn cloth fibres puff off the top of the shoulder where it strikes, the plate carrier strap snaps taut and jumps, his helmet whips over with the rotation of the torso and the goggle strap pulls tight across the cover. The rifle comes off the bipod and out of his hands, the bolt handle catching the concrete. His right arm goes dead and swings loose. He lands on his side against the parapet with his cheek on the grit, mouth open, breath driven out of him, and for a full beat he does nothing at all — the blankness of a body switched off and switched back on. His eyes stay visible behind the dusty scratched lens. No blood, no wound, no hole. Empty brass and grit float and turn in the slowed air around him.

14-16s | NORMAL SPEED SNAPS BACK — CLOSE ON TERRENCE: <<<4f969abd-60d2-4e34-9da2-d933f91e3688>>>'s head comes off his scope and round, goggles down over his eyes, and everything professional goes out of his face in one frame. He does not shout an order and does not reach for a dressing — he says the man's name once and starts to move toward him.
TERRENCE: "JACK!"

16-30s | ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN SHOT TO THE END OF THE SCENE — NO CUT ANYWHERE INSIDE THESE FOURTEEN SECONDS. One camera, one setup, one continuous take: a tight close-up, slightly low, <<<93edeb87-e0e7-4ded-9569-527aca55e457>>> propped against the base of the parapet on his good left side, the dead right arm hanging, his rifle on the concrete beside him, dust grey on his face and on the goggle lens, rounds cracking off the wall above his helmet. THE CAMERA NEVER CUTS, NEVER CHANGES ANGLE AND NEVER RE-FRAMES TO A NEW SETUP — it only breathes and drifts with him, handheld. HIS POSITION AGAINST THE PARAPET DOES NOT CHANGE FROM THE FIRST FRAME OF THIS SHOT TO THE LAST: he does not sit up, does not stand, does not roll over, does not move to another part of the roof, and he is never discovered already holding a radio in a new position. Everything below happens inside this one frame, in this order.

FIRST — HE LOOKS (about two seconds). His head comes down and he LOOKS AT HIS OWN RIGHT SHOULDER, at the torn dusty fabric where the round went in. He does not look at Terrence, not at the lane, not at the lens. He examines it the way you examine something that belongs to someone else.

SECOND — THE REACTION ARRIVES IN HIS BODY (about two seconds, no words at all), involuntary and physical, not acted: a sharp shallow catch of breath sucked in through the teeth; the head tips BACK against the concrete and the eyes screw shut hard behind the lens; the jaw clamps; HIS LEFT HAND COMES ACROSS AND PRESSES FLAT OVER THE SHOULDER AND STAYS THERE; his breathing goes short, fast and shallow through the nose, chest lifting; a shudder runs through him once. He rides it out.

THIRD — THE WORD (about one and a half seconds). The worst of it passes through him, his head comes back down off the wall, his eyes open, and he says it — flat, quiet, tired, disgusted, half under his breath, not a shout:
JACK: "Shit!"

FOURTH — THE HAND MOVES, STILL THE SAME SHOT AND THE SAME POSITION, AND THIS IS THE HINGE OF THE TAKE: the LEFT hand — the same hand that has been pressing his shoulder — LIFTS OFF THE WOUND and travels up to the shoulder mic clipped on the left strap of his plate carrier. We see it leave the shoulder and we see it close on the mic. He does not use the right arm, which stays dead and hanging. He does not change how he is lying. The camera stays exactly where it is and simply lets his hand come up into frame. Half a second of him squeezing the transmit key and drawing one breath before he speaks.

FIFTH — THE RADIO CALL (six full seconds for eighteen words, same unbroken shot, same position, left hand on the mic at his collarbone the whole time). HE IS SHOUTING. Loud, raised, forced, hoarse, straining over the volume of the firefight — a man who knows help is minutes away and that forty of them are closing. Real emotion: fury and urgency, teeth showing, the cords standing out in his neck, the words torn out of him, his voice cracking on the loudest ones. BUT HE DOES NOT GABBLE, DOES NOT RUSH AND DOES NOT RUN THE PHRASES TOGETHER. He shouts in SHORT HARD SEPARATE BURSTS — one phrase hammered out at full volume, then he STOPS, DRAGS IN A BREATH THROUGH HIS TEETH, and hammers out the next. The audible breath between phrases is part of the performance. Every word fully formed and hit hard, nothing swallowed, nothing crammed. Loud and slow at the same time.
JACK (shouting into the radio, hoarse, one short phrase at a time, breathing between each):
"All stations! — this is Reaper! — We are SURROUNDED! — I say again — SURROUNDED! — We need air support — NOW!"
Behind him, out of focus in the same frame, <<<4f969abd-60d2-4e34-9da2-d933f91e3688>>> is back down on his rifle and firing.

SIXTH — THE ANSWER (the last two and a half seconds, still the same unbroken shot, same position, left hand still on the mic): hold on his face, chest heaving from shouting, as the radio comes back — thin, compressed and crackling out of a speaker, and by contrast completely calm, unhurried and clearly enunciated:
RADIO (male, calm, American): "Copy, Reaper. Hawk is inbound. Hang tight, boys."
His hand comes off the mic and drops back onto the shoulder. He closes his eyes for half a second behind the lens and that is the only thing his face does. Hold. Last frame.

ACTING TASK — JACK: he is triaging, not suffering. When he looks at the shoulder he is checking a piece of equipment. The reaction that follows is his body overruling him for two seconds, and he lets it pass through rather than fighting it or performing it. "Shit" is irritation at a tool that broke, said quietly because there is nobody he wants to say it to. THEN THE RADIO CALL IS THE OPPOSITE — this is the one moment in the film where he loses his temper, because he has one arm, a man down at the window and forty men closing, and the only thing left that can change the outcome is at the other end of that radio. He is not asking, he is DEMANDING, at full volume — and he still forces himself to break it into separate hammered phrases, because a man who cannot be understood gets nothing. Note that to make the call he takes the pressure off his own wound, and he does not hesitate about that for a moment.
ACTING TASK — TERRENCE: for two seconds he stops being a soldier entirely. He is not assessing a casualty, he is looking at Jack. Then he puts himself back together and goes back on the gun, and the effort of doing it is visible on him.
ACTING TASK — THE FIGHTERS: not suicidal and not extras. Every man is trying to get thirty metres closer without being the next one down — zigzag rushes, proper cover, heads up at the roofline at every stop; when the man beside them goes down they do not stop, they change their line.

SOUND: two bolt-actions and carbines working, AK fire from four directions cracking off concrete, rounds hitting sandbags and stone, brass on the deck, Pashto passed lane to lane. Under the SLOW MOTION beat the mix drops to a muffled underwater roar with the impact itself almost dry and small, then a thin ringing. Normal speed returns with Terrence's shout. Through Jack's reaction: only his breath — the sharp catch, then short shallow breathing — under the battle. Through the radio call his shouting is the loudest thing in the mix and the ragged breath between phrases is audible. The radio reply is thin, compressed and crackling out of a speaker, calm and perfectly intelligible against him. No music.

FORBIDDEN: NO CUT, no edit point, no new angle, no reframe to a different setup and no change of camera position anywhere between 16s and the last frame — it is ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE; his body position against the parapet is identical from the first frame of that take to the last, he never sits up, never stands, never rolls over, never relocates on the roof, and he is never discovered already holding a radio in a new position; the hand that goes to the mic is the LEFT hand and it is the same hand that was pressing the shoulder, and we see it leave the wound and travel up into frame; the dead right arm never moves, never lifts, never holds anything; <<<93edeb87-e0e7-4ded-9569-527aca55e457>>>: helmet on his head, goggles down over his eyes. <<<4f969abd-60d2-4e34-9da2-d933f91e3688>>>: helmet on his head, goggles down over his eyes. Every other American in frame: helmet on his head, goggles down over his eyes. IN EVERY BEAT AND EVERY CLOSE-UP, including both men down behind their rifle scopes, including Terrence coming off the scope, including Jack looking down at his own shoulder, and including the entire unbroken take on the radio.
Nobody is bare-headed at any point, nobody removes a helmet, nobody pushes the goggles up onto the shell or onto the forehead, nobody wears them round the neck, and no helmet or goggles are ever lying on the ground.
THE REST OF THE KIT: tan plate carriers with three stacked magazine pouches and a shoulder radio with a whip antenna on the left strap, tan gloves, arid camo combat shirts with the sleeves rolled above the elbow and a subdued US flag patch on the right sleeve, trousers with built-in knee pads, a black pistol in a tan drop-leg holster on the right thigh, tan suede boots — everything dusty, sweat-stained, worn, never clean, never costume.

FIGHTER MOVEMENT — ZIGZAGS AND COVER, THIS GOVERNS EVERY FIGHTER IN EVERY BEAT: nobody runs at the building and nobody runs in a straight line. Every rush is THREE TO FIVE PACES, bent low, CHANGING DIRECTION TWO OR THREE TIMES INSIDE THAT SINGLE RUSH — cutting left, then right, then left again — and ending with the man going DOWN hard behind the next piece of cover, flat or on one knee, weapon coming up over it. They come OUT OF THE ALLEY MOUTHS ONE AT A TIME, and the first thing each man does on breaking cover is cut diagonally instead of running up the lane. They stop behind the ENGINE BLOCK AND WHEELS of the wrecked cars, never the doors. They CUT THE CORNERS OF THE BUILDINGS TIGHT, shoulder almost scraping the render, muzzle leading, one fast look and gone. They hug the base of walls in the shadow. They go through the gap in the low wall on their bellies one at a time and move along the drainage ditch on elbows and knees. They cross open ground ONE MAN AT A TIME on the diagonal. They move IN PAIRS, BOUNDING — one up and moving while the other is down covering, then swapping, never both moving at once. AND AT EVERY STOP AT LEAST ONE OF THEM SNAPS HIS HEAD UP AT THE ROOFLINE of the corner house, because they know there are snipers on it and it visibly decides where they choose to stop. Weapons in the shoulder or held high across the body while moving, never dangling.

HOW HITS ARE SHOWN: a man who is hit STOPS WORKING AND GOES DOWN — the read is the sudden loss of intention, a rush that ends mid-stride, a body that drops instead of falls, a weapon released. Dust and torn cloth fibres puff off the impact point, the body twists away from it, and there is no next move. NO BLOOD, NO WOUNDS, NO GORE, NO RED MIST. Enemy casualties always at DISTANCE and small in frame.

0-3s | ROOF, MEDIUM ON THE TWO OF THEM: <<<93edeb87-e0e7-4ded-9569-527aca55e457>>> breaks a shot and cycles the bolt, <<<4f969abd-60d2-4e34-9da2-d933f91e3688>>> fires beside him, brass turning on the concrete. CUT TO A LONG LENS DOWN THE LANE: a fighter from <<<image_1>>> mid-zigzag between a wrecked car and a rubble mound stops dead in stride, dust puffing off his chest rig, and goes straight down onto the stones, small and far away. His partner does not go to him and keeps moving.

3-7s | THE LANE, GROUND LEVEL, LOW AND WIDE — the movement beat: a fighter from <<<image_2>>> breaks out of the alley mouth, cuts hard right, then left, then right again across four paces and DROPS behind the front wheel of a wrecked car, rifle up over the bonnet, head snapping up at the roofline. A second man comes out a beat later on a completely different line, zigzags twice and puts himself behind the burnt-out minibus. A third slices round the corner of a courtyard wall with his shoulder against the render, muzzle leading, one look, gone. Two more bound forward in a pair — one rushes and drops behind the rubble mound, the other passes him at a sprint, changes direction twice and goes down behind the stacked breeze blocks. One is hit as he clears the alley mouth and drops flat two paces out, sliding in the dirt. The rest keep coming, lower, shorter rushes, tighter to the walls.

7-10s | THE WINDOW. WIDE, LOW, FROM INSIDE THE GROUND-FLOOR ROOM looking out through a sandbagged window hole: a SEAL is standing at the window hole firing his carbine out into the lane, helmet on, goggles down over his eyes, brass flicking off to one side, sandbags bursting and pouring beside him as rounds come in. AND HE IS HIT. He stops firing mid-burst, comes off the weapon, and goes straight down out of the frame below the sill — the carbine dropping with him. THAT IS THE WHOLE BEAT. Nobody runs to him, nobody drags him, nobody shouts, the camera does not follow him down, and he is not shown on the floor. The window hole he was standing in is simply empty and the dust keeps pouring off the sandbags.

10-14s | SLOW MOTION — JACK IS HIT. Tight, close, low behind the parapet, EXTREME SLOW MOTION, all of it read on him and his kit: <<<93edeb87-e0e7-4ded-9569-527aca55e457>>> is up on his elbows on the rifle when the round arrives in his RIGHT SHOULDER. The impact goes through his body before his face knows about it — the shoulder is driven violently backwards and down, dust and a small burst of torn cloth fibres puff off the top of the shoulder where it strikes, the plate carrier strap snaps taut and jumps, his helmet whips over with the rotation of the torso and the goggle strap pulls tight across the cover. The rifle comes off the bipod and out of his hands, the bolt handle catching the concrete. His right arm goes dead and swings loose. He lands on his side against the parapet with his cheek on the grit, mouth open, breath driven out of him, and for a full beat he does nothing at all — the blankness of a body switched off and switched back on. His eyes stay visible behind the dusty scratched lens the whole time. No blood, no wound, no hole. Empty brass and grit float and turn in the slowed air around him.

14-16s | NORMAL SPEED SNAPS BACK — CLOSE ON TERRENCE: <<<4f969abd-60d2-4e34-9da2-d933f91e3688>>>'s head comes off his scope and round, helmet on, goggles down over his eyes, and everything professional goes out of his face in one frame. He does not shout an order and does not reach for a dressing — he says the man's name once and starts to move toward him.
TERRENCE: "JACK!"

16-30s | ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN SHOT TO THE END OF THE SCENE — NO CUT ANYWHERE INSIDE THESE FOURTEEN SECONDS. One camera, one setup, one continuous take: a tight close-up, slightly low, <<<93edeb87-e0e7-4ded-9569-527aca55e457>>> propped against the base of the parapet on his good left side, the dead right arm hanging, his rifle on the concrete beside him, dust grey on his face and on the goggle lens, rounds cracking off the wall above his helmet. THE CAMERA NEVER CUTS, NEVER CHANGES ANGLE AND NEVER RE-FRAMES TO A NEW SETUP — it only breathes and drifts with him, handheld. HIS POSITION AGAINST THE PARAPET DOES NOT CHANGE FROM THE FIRST FRAME OF THIS SHOT TO THE LAST: he does not sit up, does not stand, does not roll over, does not move to another part of the roof, and he is never discovered already holding a radio in a new position. Helmet on, goggles down over his eyes, eyes readable through the lens throughout. Everything below happens inside this one frame, in this order.

FIRST — HE LOOKS (about two seconds). His head comes down and he LOOKS AT HIS OWN RIGHT SHOULDER, at the torn dusty fabric where the round went in. He does not look at Terrence, not at the lane, not at the lens. He examines it the way you examine something that belongs to someone else.

SECOND — THE REACTION ARRIVES IN HIS BODY (about two seconds, no words at all), involuntary and physical, not acted: a sharp shallow catch of breath sucked in through the teeth; the head tips BACK against the concrete and the eyes screw shut hard behind the lens; the jaw clamps; HIS LEFT HAND COMES ACROSS AND PRESSES FLAT OVER THE SHOULDER AND STAYS THERE; his breathing goes short, fast and shallow through the nose, chest lifting; a shudder runs through him once. He rides it out.

THIRD — THE WORD (about one and a half seconds). The worst of it passes through him, his head comes back down off the wall, his eyes open behind the lens, and he says it — flat, quiet, tired, disgusted, half under his breath, not a shout:
JACK: "Shit!"

FOURTH — THE HAND MOVES, STILL THE SAME SHOT AND THE SAME POSITION, AND THIS IS THE HINGE OF THE TAKE: the LEFT hand — the same hand that has been pressing his shoulder — LIFTS OFF THE WOUND and travels up to the shoulder mic clipped on the left strap of his plate carrier. We see it leave the shoulder and we see it close on the mic. He does not use the right arm, which stays dead and hanging. He does not change how he is lying. The camera stays exactly where it is and simply lets his hand come up into frame. Half a second of him squeezing the transmit key and drawing one breath before he speaks.

FIFTH — THE RADIO CALL (six full seconds for eighteen words, same unbroken shot, same position, left hand on the mic at his collarbone the whole time). HE IS SHOUTING. Loud, raised, forced, hoarse, straining over the volume of the firefight — a man who knows help is minutes away and that forty of them are closing. Real emotion: fury and urgency, teeth showing, the cords standing out in his neck, the words torn out of him, his voice cracking on the loudest ones. BUT HE DOES NOT GABBLE, DOES NOT RUSH AND DOES NOT RUN THE PHRASES TOGETHER. He shouts in SHORT HARD SEPARATE BURSTS — one phrase hammered out at full volume, then he STOPS, DRAGS IN A BREATH THROUGH HIS TEETH, and hammers out the next. The audible breath between phrases is part of the performance. Every word fully formed and hit hard, nothing swallowed, nothing crammed. Loud and slow at the same time.
JACK (shouting into the radio, hoarse, one short phrase at a time, breathing between each):
"All stations! — this is Reaper! — We are SURROUNDED! — I say again — SURROUNDED! — We need air support — NOW!"
Behind him, out of focus in the same frame, <<<4f969abd-60d2-4e34-9da2-d933f91e3688>>> is back down on his rifle and firing.

SIXTH — THE ANSWER (the last two and a half seconds, still the same unbroken shot, same position, left hand still on the mic): hold on his face, chest heaving from shouting, as the radio comes back — thin, compressed and crackling out of a speaker, and by contrast completely calm, unhurried and clearly enunciated:
RADIO (male, calm, American): "Copy, Reaper. Hawk is inbound. Hang tight, boys."
His hand comes off the mic and drops back onto the shoulder. He closes his eyes for half a second behind the lens and that is the only thing his face does. Hold. Last frame.

ACTING TASK — JACK: he is triaging, not suffering. When he looks at the shoulder he is checking a piece of equipment. The reaction that follows is his body overruling him for two seconds, and he lets it pass through rather than fighting it or performing it. "Shit" is irritation at a tool that broke, said quietly because there is nobody he wants to say it to. THEN THE RADIO CALL IS THE OPPOSITE — this is the one moment in the film where he loses his temper, because he has one arm, a man down at the window and forty men closing, and the only thing left that can change the outcome is at the other end of that radio. He is not asking, he is DEMANDING, at full volume — and he still forces himself to break it into separate hammered phrases, because a man who cannot be understood gets nothing. Note that to make the call he takes the pressure off his own wound, and he does not hesitate about that for a moment.
ACTING TASK — TERRENCE: for two seconds he stops being a soldier entirely. He is not assessing a casualty, he is looking at Jack. Then he puts himself back together and goes back on the gun, and the effort of doing it is visible on him.
ACTING TASK — THE FIGHTERS: not suicidal and not extras. Every man is trying to get thirty metres closer without being the next one down — zigzag rushes, proper cover, heads up at the roofline at every stop; when the man beside them goes down they do not stop, they change their line.

SOUND: two bolt-actions and carbines working, AK fire from four directions cracking off concrete, rounds hitting sandbags and stone, brass on the deck, Pashto passed lane to lane. Under the SLOW MOTION beat the mix drops to a muffled underwater roar with the impact itself almost dry and small, then a thin ringing. Normal speed returns with Terrence's shout. Through Jack's reaction: only his breath — the sharp catch, then short shallow breathing — under the battle. Through the radio call his shouting is the loudest thing in the mix and the ragged breath between phrases is audible. The radio reply is thin, compressed and crackling out of a speaker, calm and perfectly intelligible against him. No music.

FORBIDDEN: no helmet or goggles lying on the ground, on a wall or set down anywhere — they are worn; no helmet without goggles and no goggles without a helmet; no American without a helmet; no American without ballistic goggles worn DOWN OVER THE EYES; "Shit" is quiet and under his breath — it is never shouted; THE RADIO CALL IS SHOUTED AND EMOTIONAL BUT NEVER FAST — never gabbled, never rushed, never crammed, never with the phrases running into each other, never mumbled, never swallowed, never overlapping the radio reply; 【FILM STYLE — 全片固定】
■ 比例与同一性（最高优先，压倒一切）
2.39:1，比例正确。人物脸与身体是真实人体比例,与角色参考图完全一致:骨相、眉眼间距、鼻梁、下颌线、肤色。若任何构图或风格指令会让脸偏离参考图,放弃那条指令,保住脸。此段是几年前的杰克,成熟、饱经战斗的男人,不是 年轻新兵。
■ 摄影机·胶片·镜头
RED Gemini 双原生高感,Leica 定制镜头,复古2倍变形宽银幕:竖椭圆焦外、边缘猫眼、失焦高光横向抹长、明显色差、柔和暗角。镀膜洁净:无镜头耀光、无横向光条、无星芒、无光晕。
■ 调色(《泰坦》与《搏击俱乐部》双温度沼泽)
阴影沉入深青蓝绿,受光面是烈日晒白的赭黄与硫磺色;低饱和,黑位深沉但保留质感,重胶片颗粒。全画面无干净的白。
■ 创伤纹理(本段签名,贯穿全段)
一切被重运动模糊涂抹;每条边缘有强烈色差镶边;一圈柔和失焦晕影在四周游动,四角融化成模糊带色差的焦外,只一个不稳定的小中心勉强清晰;时间抽格、掉帧、地平线永不水平;高频耳鸣时时吞掉声音。
■ 表演
不演情绪,演贯彻战术的过程,戏在眼睛里。安全线:视线始终执行任务,绝不呆滞空洞;自然眨眼。
■ 全片禁止
动漫、漫画、赛璐璐、速度线、拖影线条、smear帧、插画平涂、游戏CG、塑料皮肤、过度锐化HDR;换脸、通用AI面孔;镜头耀光、横向光条、水平蓝白亮线、星芒、放射光、鬼影、光晕溢出、太阳直拍入画;文字、字幕、Logo、UI、边框、水印;音乐、配乐、旁白。
本段无血、无伤口特写、无尸体——画面只呈现动作、位置、重心与掩护的变化,这是电影化的战争记忆。

Duration: 30s. AFGHANISTAN, KABUL, DAY — the house is surrounded and Jack takes a round through the right shoulder. GRADE: warm GOLDEN Afghan daylight — honey-and-sand, creamy gold sun, dusty tan and khaki, 16mm grain, gentle halation, gold and dust. NORMAL SPEED EVERYWHERE except the one beat marked SLOW MOTION.

THE HELMET IS ON HIS HEAD: a modern military combat helmet in DESERT TAN with a dusty tan cloth cover, a night-vision mounting shroud and bracket on the front plate, accessory rails down both sides, a bungee cord across the top of the shell, an adjustable chinstrap FASTENED UNDER THE JAW with the cheek pads visible, the whole shell scuffed and grey with dust.
