FIRST FRAME <<<image_1>>> = <<<image_1>>> — the attached plate is the exact first frame. Start on it exactly as it is: same layout of the city, same mountains, same flat dusty light. Do not re-frame it, do not re-light it, do not warm it up, do not change the architecture, do not cut at the start. All motion grows out of this frame.

ALTITUDE LAW — WE ARE VERY HIGH: the drone sits at around eight hundred metres above the ground, higher than any building, higher than any helicopter would fly, looking out and down at roughly forty-five degrees. The whole city, the desert plain, the foothills and the mountain ridges are all in one frame at once. Individual buildings are small blocks, whole districts read as patches of texture, the main road is a thin line, vehicles are single specks, people are barely detectable dots. Nothing ever comes close enough to become a detail. Never a rooftop-level view, never a straight-down map view — the horizon and the mountains stay visible in the upper part of frame the whole time.

CAMERA — ONE SLOW PUSH IN, RUNNING THE WHOLE 15 SECONDS: the drone advances FORWARD towards the city at one slow, steady, even speed, holding its altitude and its downward angle from the first frame to the last. It is already moving in frame one and it is still moving in the last frame — no static opening, no hold, no acceleration, no deceleration, no stop, no arrival. Over the fifteen seconds the city comes towards us and grows a little in frame, the near districts drifting down and out under the bottom edge, while the mountains on the horizon barely change size at all — that difference is what sells the height and the distance. It is a PHYSICAL MOVE, not an optical one: no zoom, no focal length change, no punch-in, no tilt, no roll, no yaw, no orbit, no crane, no whip, no rise or descent, no handheld shake, no cut, no dissolve.

THE CITY IS SHUT AND ALMOST EMPTY — THIS IS A CITY AT WAR: the bazaar along the main road is closed, shutters down, stalls folded, awnings torn or rolled away. Almost no traffic — one lorry, one motorbike, a handcart pushed by a single figure, long stretches of empty tarmac between them. The alleys are deserted. A few stray dogs. Only a handful of tiny distant figures anywhere — no crowds, no market throng, no groups, no busy pavements, no children playing. The war sits in the fabric and does not move: sandbagged positions and stacked blast walls at a couple of junctions, razor wire, a street barricaded with rubble and oil drums, a burnt car husk on a verge, buildings with roofs fallen in and blackened window holes, one block collapsed into broken slabs, craters in the tarmac, spoil heaps everywhere. Two thin columns of grey smoke stand across the city and drift flat in the wind. No soldiers, no military vehicles, no fighting, no bodies.
GROUND MOVEMENT LAW: everything on the ground moves forwards, nose first, at a normal steady speed. The lorry drives AWAY from camera down the main road with its rear towards us; the motorbike comes TOWARDS camera, front wheel first; the handcart is pushed forwards; the dogs trot forwards. Nothing reverses, nothing rolls backwards, nothing drifts against its own direction.

GRADE — BLEAK AND HEAVY: hot daylight with the sun buried behind a lid of dust, so the light is flat, hard and colourless rather than golden. Bleached grey-tan and ash palette, warmth almost drained out, everything dulled by dust; the tiled domes and torn awnings barely tinted, never bright. Shadows soft and murky, sky pale and lifeless with no blue in it. Thick dust and smoke haze deepening with distance until the far districts and the mountains dissolve into dirty pale nothing. 16mm film texture, fine grain, slight halation, low saturation, soft falloff. Anamorphic 2.39:1.

SOUND — THE ATMOSPHERE IS THE POINT: at this height the world arrives thin, flattened and delayed. The bed is high-altitude air — a steady dry wind with a faint pressure hiss, gusting now and then, and nothing else close to us. Underneath it the city seeps up from far below, quiet and smeared by distance: one lone engine labouring somewhere, a single horn a long way off, a dog barking and another answering, a metal shutter banging in the wind, a hammer striking twice and stopping, sheet metal creaking as it heats. A thin distorted call to prayer drifts up from one of the minarets with nothing else under it and no crowd noise around it. Every few seconds a dull far-off thump rolls in from beyond the city and fades — too distant to place, never sharp, never a bang. Nothing ever comes close, nothing is ever loud, and the silences between the sounds are longer than the sounds themselves. No music, no score, no drone whine, no rotor, no whoosh, no stinger, no rising tension bed.

【FILM STYLE — fixed】
■ FRAME & IDENTITY (highest priority, overrides everything else)
2.39:1, correct proportions, no stretch, no squeeze. True human proportion, identical to the character reference; the generated face is the SAME PERSON — bone structure, eye spacing, nose bridge, jawline, skin tone, age, hair. If any instruction pushes the face off the reference, drop that instruction and keep the face.
■ CAMERA · LENS
RED Gemini dual native ISO, built for extreme low light | vintage 2x ANAMORPHIC widescreen, wide open | Leica-tuned glass with a low-contrast filter. Oval stretched bokeh, cat-eye at the frame edges, defocused highlights smeared into horizontal ovals, subtle chromatic aberration, desaturated restrained colour. Newly multi-coated, no internal reflection, straight lines at the frame edge stay straight. 135mm. Razor-shallow depth of field: BOTH his eyes hold the focal plane and are the sharpest thing in frame; the metal in the foreground is thrown completely out of focus into a soft black mass.
■ GRAMMAR — CHAMBER
Frame absolutely level, Dutch zero, camera locked on its axis. One scripted move only: a very slow, steady, continuous mechanical push-in running the entire take — it never stops, never speeds up, never pulls back. No handheld, no zoom, no slow motion, no speed ramping, no aerial.
■ GRADE
Fight Club, Fincher and Cronenweth — grimy green-teal shadows, sickly sodium tint, crushed murky blacks, desaturated, pale greenish skin, fine grain.

【SCENE】
Duration 10s. Night, present-day New York. A third-floor apartment under renovation. One continuous shot, no cuts.

【GEOMETRY & FRAMING — match this exactly】
Camera directly in front of him, head-on, slightly above his eye line, close enough that his face fills the frame from hairline to just below the mouth. He is prone and low, already OFF the eyepiece: his head is lifted just enough that he is looking OVER the top of the scope, straight down the lens, not through the optic.
BOTH EYES ARE OPEN, BOTH FULLY VISIBLE, BOTH IN SHARP FOCUS, and they sit just above the centre of the frame. Neither eye is squinted, closed, covered, or hidden behind the optic.
The rifle's optic is a large, completely defocused black mass rising from the bottom edge of frame, sitting BELOW the eye line and passing between and beneath his eyes — it partially covers his nose and mouth but NEVER crosses either eye. Symmetrical composition: the dark mass centred, one cheek to the left of it, one cheek to the right.
His hooded shoulders read as two soft black shapes at the far left and far right edges, out of focus.
END FRAME: the push-in has tightened to brow, eyes and the top of the dark mass only.
Nothing else is visible: no window, no sill, no wall, no ceiling — black on all sides.

【LIGHT — hardest rule of the shot】
NO light source inside the room: no lamp, no practical, no work light. The room is a black hole, exposed far below what looks normal: the surrounding frame is pure black with zero detail, and only his face carries information.
The single source is a weak, soft, cold-neutral light coming from HIGH IN FRONT of him, above and slightly behind the camera, out of frame. It falls on the UPPER PLANES ONLY — forehead, brow ridges, the bridge and tip of the nose, both cheekbones, the upper lip — and leaves the EYE SOCKETS DEEP IN SHADOW, so the eyes sit inside dark hollows while the bone above them is lit. Jaw, chin and throat fall away to black. No fill, no bounce, no rim from behind, no top light directly overhead.
Inside those dark sockets both eyes stay clearly readable, with a small sharp specular glint on the wet surface of each — these glints are the brightest points in the entire frame. Skin is pale, greenish, with visible pores, stubble and slight sheen; bright but never blown out, always holding texture.

【ACTION — one continuous 10s take】
0.0–10.0 | The push-in runs the entire take, very slow and perfectly even.
He does not move. He is already off the eyepiece and stays exactly where he is — head at the same height, body low, shoulders down, elbows planted, nothing rising, nothing turning, nothing reaching. The hands stay on the rifle, out of frame at the bottom.
All movement is micro: shallow breathing that barely disturbs the frame; one held breath around 4.0–5.5 where everything stops; irregular blinking, never in a rhythm; tiny involuntary shifts of the eyes as he keeps reading something past the camera; the faintest movement of the jaw once, around 7.0, as he swallows.
His gaze stays level and directed past the lens throughout — he is looking at something specific in the distance, never at the camera, never at nothing.
Hold to the last frame.

【ACTING TASK — no visual language; he is fully invested in his tactic】
MOTIVE (life-long, set once for the film): he does not carry people. Long ago he cut everyone loose on purpose, because a man with nobody in his life has nothing that can be used against him and nothing that argues with him at work. He is not haunted and he is not lonely — he is clean.
SCENE DIRECTION (unspoken): finish this the way the last hundred were finished.
GOAL: keep the figure across the street a shape, a distance and a time.
OBSTACLE: there is a second body in that room, small and unpredictable, and it will not stay out of the geometry.
TACTIC: he is not weighing whether to do it — that was never on the table. He is solving a technical problem: the second body degrades the shot. It moves without pattern, it will be in the room when the shot is taken, and a witness at that range means a longer exit. He has taken his eye off the glass to reset and is now watching the building with his own eyes, running the problem — angle, timing, whether it leaves the room, whether the target comes back to the window alone. He does not feel sorry for it; he resents it the way he would resent bad weather or a jammed window, because it costs him time and time is the only thing that can get him caught. What he arrives at is not mercy. It is that he will wait, and then he will do it anyway.
SAFETY LINE: the gaze is always engaged in the task, never a dead glassy stare, never soft, never sad, never warm; natural irregular blink cadence. PLAY IT SMALL — no wide staring eyes, no open mouth, no head shake, no grimace, no tears, no trembling, no clenched teeth, no theatrics, no visible sympathy or compassion of any kind. Everything lives in the eyes and in one held breath.

【SOUND】
Sync sound only, and only what exists inside the nest. His breathing — shallow, then held, then back on a new count — is by far the loudest thing in the mix and carries the whole shot. Under it, very quiet and very close: nylon shell creasing, glove leather shifting on steel, the board taking his weight, torn plastic sheeting stirring, a low draught moving through the empty floor. Nothing from outside: no street, no traffic, no voices, no city. No music, no dialogue, no narration.

场景背景

记忆闪回。白天,一家老式美式咖啡馆。杰克坐在窗边卡座看手表——女服务员走近,他把手放下。她微笑着问要点什么,他说"老样子",她说得说具体点,他呼出一口气,报出:咖啡、苹果派、账单一起上。东西端上来,黑色账单夹和食物一起落桌。他盯着合着的夹子看了一会儿,才打开。热敏纸上,他点的两行之下,虚线之外,是点阵打印的另一份订单——一个地址,一个人的体貌,没有名字。他合上夹子,压下钞票,起身离开。桌上留着完整未动的苹果派。

杰克——

动机:这套仪式是这份工作里他唯一没得选的部分;它早就不再意味着什么,只是每次都要重新排一遍的队。

场景背景
夜,大雨。城市边缘一家二十四小时快餐店的免下车取餐道。目标独自开着灰色轿车排队取餐。杰克在雨里跟着他,不紧不慢;当目标探身去接窗口递出的纸袋时,杰克拉开后车门坐了进去。车开走,后座一片漆黑。全片无台词。

风格
记忆的语法:梦境般浓重柔焦——边缘融化、高光晕成椭圆、动作带极轻拖影。浓烈芬奇之夜:快餐店招牌的脏黄与刺目红、尾灯的红、湿沥青上化开的倒影,在雨里互相渗透;整体欠曝一档半,画面活在阴影上部;黑位深沉但保留质感;肤色始终自然温暖。

摄影机与镜头
RED Gemini双原生高感光度,Leica定制镜头加低反差滤镜,无刺眼高光。复古2倍变形宽银幕,2.39:1,大光圈全开:椭圆拉伸焦外,画面边缘猫眼光斑,失焦高光抹成水平长椭圆,轻微色差,低饱和克制色彩。运动一律为电动机械运动——滑轨横移与极缓推近,匀速精确,绝不手持抖动。无镜头眩光,无光线拉丝,画面边缘直线保持笔直。

目标:五十岁上下的白人男子,体格臃肿厚重,深褐色头发浓密但两侧额角明显后退,脸圆、下颌松弛,穿一件厚重的深褐色长大衣。他与杰克的体型、发色、衣着完全不同,任何时候都不会混淆。
车辆:一辆灰色四门轿车,车龄不新,后车窗贴着深色膜,从外面看不见后座。

首帧与空间调度
大全景,机位在取餐道外侧的停车场边缘,与人齐高,滑轨缓慢横移。雨在钠黄的灯光里成线落下,地面积水映着快餐店招牌化开的红与黄。取餐道上排着三辆车,灰色轿车是中间那辆,尾灯亮着两团红色椭圆。画面近处,一个黑色帽兜的身影背对镜头站在候车棚下,一动不动。

格式模式
五个镜头,共15秒。全程记忆柔焦。无台词。

动作时间轴
镜头1——0.0至3.5秒——大全景,滑轨横移:雨、取餐道、三辆排队的车。灰色轿车向前挪了一个车位,刹车灯亮了一下又暗下去。候车棚下那个黑色帽兜的身影没有看那些车——他面朝街道,雨水从棚檐连成一条线落在他身前。
3.5秒切
镜头2——3.5至6.0秒——车内侧面近景,隔着雨水流淌的侧窗玻璃向内看:目标独自坐在驾驶座上,厚重的深褐色大衣把他填满整个座位;他一手搭方向盘,一手在中控台上翻找零钱,收音机的微光照着他的下巴。副驾驶座空着,后座隐在深色车窗膜后面看不见。
6.0秒切
镜头3——6.0至8.5秒——低角度中景,机位贴近湿地面:黑色的靴子从画面右侧走进来,不急不缓地穿过积水,踩碎地面上招牌的红色倒影,朝停在取餐窗口前的灰色轿车走去。步幅平稳,速度和车队向前挪动的速度差不多。
8.5秒切
镜头4——8.5至12.5秒——【核心镜头】侧后方中景,机位固定,一镜到底。灰色轿车停在取餐窗口前,车身把窗口和驾驶座之间的空间挡住。目标降下车窗，上半身探出去,两只手一起去接窗口递出的纸袋,整个人朝画面外侧扭过去。就在这两秒里,杰克从画面右侧走到车的另一侧,拉开后车门,一个动作坐了进去,把门轻轻带上——动作平稳、经济，没有一丝多余，没有回头看，没有加速。车门关上的同时,目标把纸袋收进车里,重新坐正,升起车窗。他没有察觉。
12.5秒切
镜头5——12.5至15.0秒——车后方中景,极缓推近:灰色轿车驶出取餐道,汇入雨夜的街道。透过后窗只能看见驾驶座上那个厚重的剪影;后座在深色车窗膜后面完全是黑的,什么也看不出来。红色尾灯在湿沥青上晕成两团椭圆,渐渐远去。定格一拍,切黑。

表演任务(功课在眼里,不演情绪)
杰克——
动机:这不是一场对抗,是一道工序;工序里没有对手,只有工件。
目标:在窗口时间内上车,不让任何人记住有人上过这辆车。
战术:他不跟、不追、不藏——他站在候车棚下等的不是这个人,是这个人自己空出来的那两秒;他看的是队伍还剩几辆车、窗口递出东西要多久、对方的手什么时候会同时离开方向盘;走向车的速度是刻意挑的,和车队挪动一样快,这样在任何人眼里他都只是个走路的人;拉门上车的动作和搭一辆网约车没有区别,因为犹豫才会被记住。
目标——
战术:他饿了,一整天了;他关心的是零钱够不够、袋子里有没有漏掉的东西、雨会不会打湿座椅。他今晚要处理的事情里没有一件是危险的。
(安全线:两人目光始终投入各自的任务,绝不僵死呆滞、绝不空洞发直;自然眨眼节奏。)

物理
雨在灯下成线落下,打在车顶与积水面上溅起细碎水花;雨水在侧窗玻璃上连续流下,使玻璃后的面孔轻微变形;车队向前挪动时刹车灯亮灭有真实的先后;厚重大衣的呢料在动作时有重量与惯性;车门开合有真实的行程、密封条的闷响与车身的轻微下沉;湿沥青上的霓虹倒影随水面扰动而碎开又合拢;尼龙风衣被雨打湿后反光变强。记忆段拖影严格跟随动作方向。

声音
雨:打在棚顶、车顶、积水面上,层次分明。快餐店的底噪隔着雨:对讲机里模糊的人声、油炸的滋滋声、一声电子提示音。近处清晰:靴子踩过积水、车门开合的闷响、车窗升降的电机声、雨刷的节拍。全程没有任何一声惊呼或异常——这是一次完全正常的取餐。无音乐,无台词。

夜。城市里一条安静的侧街。目标独自沿着街走,杰克跟在他后面,保持着距离。全片三秒,没有事件,没有台词——只有一个人走,和另一个人跟着。

风格
记忆的语法:梦境般浓重柔焦——边缘融化、高光晕成椭圆、动作带极轻拖影。片段以一帧近白闪光开场,像一段记忆被突然接上。浓烈芬奇之夜:钠黄的街灯与门廊灯、砖墙的暖褐、车漆上的橙色反光,浸在青绿的暗部里;整体欠曝一档半,画面活在阴影上部;黑位深沉但保留质感;肤色始终自然温暖。

摄影机与镜头
RED Gemini双原生高感光度,Leica定制镜头加低反差滤镜,无刺眼高光。复古2倍变形宽银幕,2.39:1,大光圈全开:极浅景深,椭圆拉伸焦外,画面边缘猫眼光斑,失焦高光抹成水平长椭圆,轻微色差,低饱和克制色彩。机位固定,或极缓的机械横移跟随;绝不手持抖动,绝不变焦。无镜头眩光,无光线拉丝,画面边缘直线保持笔直。

AFGHANISTAN, KABUL, DAY. 5s. THE GUNNER IN THE WINDOW IS HIT.

FRAME — REPEAT THIS COMPOSITION EXACTLY: camera stands INSIDE a dark room and looks OUT through a rectangular window opening. The whole surround of frame is the unlit interior wall — pure black, no detail, filling the outer two thirds of the picture on every side — and the bright hazy exterior sits in that black rectangle in the middle. On the sill, a row of dusty sandbags stacked two deep across the bottom of the opening. Beyond them, on the flat roof outside, ONE American MACHINE GUNNER stands behind his weapon, side-on to us, firing away to the right of frame. Behind him the city falls away into a pale bleached golden haze — flat roofs, a low block, a distant vehicle, everything washed out and out of focus. Anamorphic 2.39:1, long lens, shallow focus: the sandbags and the gunner sharp, the city soft. Handheld with only a small unsteady drift and a couple of impact jolts — no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no cut.

THE GUNNER: tan combat helmet on his head with a dusty cloth cover, a night-vision mount on the front plate, side rails, chinstrap fastened, and ballistic goggles worn DOWN OVER HIS EYES — one wide scratched dusty lens with a broad tan strap round the helmet shell. Arid camo combat shirt, sleeves rolled above the elbow, tan plate carrier with stacked magazine pouches and a shoulder radio, tan gloves. Everything dust-caked and sweat-stained, never clean, never costume.

THE WEAPON AND THE AMMUNITION BELT — THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE RIGHT: a belt-fed light machine gun, dark receiver, tan furniture, resting across the sandbags. THERE IS EXACTLY ONE AMMUNITION BELT AND IT ENTERS THE GUN ON ONE SIDE ONLY — the LEFT side of the receiver, the feed side. That belt is a single linked run of brass cartridges that comes up out of the pouch hanging under the gun, curves once and goes into the feed tray, and it slowly shortens and jumps as the gun fires. THE OTHER SIDE OF THE RECEIVER IS THE EJECTION SIDE AND IT HAS NO BELT AT ALL — only empty cases and short lengths of empty steel link spitting out of it and falling away. NO belt on both sides, no second belt, no loop of cartridges hanging out of the right side, no cartridges coming out of the ejection port, no belt crossing over the top of the gun, no belt around his neck or shoulder, no draped bandolier.

HOW THE HIT IS SHOWN: he simply STOPS WORKING. The read is the total, instant loss of intention — the firing cuts off mid-burst, the body loses its shape and drops instead of falling, the weapon released. NO BLOOD, no blood spray, no red mist, no wound, no hole, no gore, nothing of any injury shown at any point. His head and face are never lingered on after the impact — he is gone below the sandbags within a fraction of a second.

0-2.2s | He is firing in bursts, side-on to us, leaning into the gun. The receiver hammers, the belt on the left side jerks and shortens, empty brass and links fly out of the right side and tumble down the sandbags, the barrel shimmers with heat. His shoulders take the recoil in rhythm. Dust drifts across the bright opening. One brief jolt of the camera as something strikes the wall near us.
2.2-2.6s | The burst cuts off dead. His helmet snaps hard sideways and back, a small puff of dust jumps off the cover, and the whole body loses its shape at once — knees gone, weight collapsing straight down.
2.6-4s | He drops out of sight behind the sandbags, released hands leaving the gun. The machine gun tips over on the bags, muzzle swinging up and off target, and stops. One last empty case rolls down the sandbag and off the sill.
4-5s | The opening is empty except for the abandoned gun lying across the sandbags, its single belt hanging slack out of the feed side. Dust and haze move in the bright rectangle. The black interior fills the rest of the frame. Hold.

GRADE: warm GOLDEN Afghan daylight — honey-and-sand, creamy gold sun blowing out the exterior, dusty tan and khaki, the interior surround crushed to pure black. 16mm grain, gentle halation, gold dust in the air. No lens flare, no starbursts, no streaks.

SOUND: the flat hammering of the machine gun close and dry, links and brass ringing on concrete, rounds cracking off stone around the window, distant AK fire, shouting somewhere below. At the moment the firing stops, everything except the ambient fire drops away for a beat. No music, no stinger.

FORBIDDEN: no ammunition belt on both sides of the gun, no belt on the ejection side, no second belt, no loop of live cartridges hanging from the right of the receiver, no cartridges emerging from the ejection port, no belt over the shoulder or round the neck, no draped bandolier. NO BLOOD, no blood spray, no red mist, no wound, no bullet hole, no exit wound, no spatter on the sandbags or the wall, no gore, no body lingered on, no face of the dead, no death rattle, no screaming. He never staggers, never clutches his head, never turns to camera, never sinks slowly — the collapse is instant. Nobody else is in frame, no second soldier, no medic, nobody comes for him inside this shot. He is never without his helmet or his goggles, and the goggles are never pushed up or removed. No camera movement beyond the small drift and the impact jolts, no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no rack focus, no cut, no slow motion, no speed ramp. No explosions, no aircraft, no enemy visible in frame. No text, no subtitles. No clean uniform, no costume look, no cold grade. Not anime, not animated, not a video game, no CGI look.

FRAME: camera rides just outboard of the aircraft, level with the stub wing, looking along it — the near wing and its TWO nineteen-tube rocket pods fill the left half of frame, big, close and sharp, with the fuselage flank and the rotor disc edge above them. The rest of frame, beyond and BELOW the wing, is the city of <<<image_1>>> sliding past, soft and hazy. Buffeted, slightly unsteady, a little vibration in the airframe — no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no cut.

ATTITUDE LAW — THE AIRCRAFT IS NOSE-DOWN AND SO IS THE FIRE. <<<86c44cdf-61ea-4af1-9fed-111507f8fbb3>>> is in a shallow DIVING gun run, pitched NOSE-DOWN by about twenty degrees, banked slightly toward the target. Because of that attitude the whole frame is tipped down at the ground: the HORIZON SITS HIGH, in the upper quarter of frame, and the CITY FILLS EVERYTHING BELOW IT — rooftops, courtyards and lanes clearly seen from above and ahead, getting closer through the shot. The wing and pods are angled down with the aircraft, the tube mouths pointing DOWN AND FORWARD at the rooftops.
EVERY ROCKET FLIES DOWNWARD. Each one leaves its tube along the axis the pod is pointing — down and forward at a shallow descending angle — and its smoke trail runs DOWN toward the city and away from camera, converging on the block below. No rocket ever climbs, no rocket goes up into the sky, no trail rises above the horizon line, and no trail bends upward at any point.

ROCKET COUNT LAW — ONE FLASH, ONE ROCKET, ALWAYS. EXACTLY SIX ROCKETS ARE FIRED IN THIS SHOT, IN THREE PAIRS. For every single flash there is exactly one rocket that visibly leaves its tube and flies away down toward the city, and for every rocket there is exactly one flash. The count matches at every moment: three flashes means three rockets gone; six flashes means six rockets gone. There are NEVER more flashes than rockets, never a flash with nothing leaving the tube, never strobing or flickering light on the pod, never a burst of light with a single rocket in it, and never rockets appearing without a launch flash.
WHAT ONE LAUNCH LOOKS LIKE, and it happens six times: a hard white motor flare at ONE tube mouth; a thick jet of grey-white smoke blasting back along the pod from that same tube; the rocket body itself streaking out of frame down and forward as a fast bright point with a straight trail behind it; and that tube left DARK, EMPTY and smoking. THE EMPTIED TUBES ARE THE PROOF: the pod face visibly loses one loaded tube per rocket, and by the last frame exactly SIX tubes are dark and smoke-stained while the rest are still loaded.

AFGHANISTAN, KABUL, DAY. 5s. THE GUNNER IN THE WINDOW IS HIT.

FRAME — REPEAT THIS COMPOSITION EXACTLY: camera stands INSIDE a dark room and looks OUT through a rectangular window opening. The whole surround of frame is the unlit interior wall — pure black, no detail, filling the outer two thirds of the picture on every side — and the bright hazy exterior sits in that black rectangle in the middle. On the sill, a row of dusty sandbags stacked two deep across the bottom of the opening. Beyond them, on the flat roof outside, ONE American MACHINE GUNNER stands behind his weapon, side-on to us, firing away to the right of frame. Behind him the city falls away into a pale bleached golden haze — flat roofs, a low block, a distant vehicle, all washed out and out of focus. Anamorphic 2.39:1, long lens, shallow focus: the sandbags and the gunner sharp, the city soft. Handheld with only a small unsteady drift and a couple of impact jolts — no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no cut.

THE GUNNER: tan combat helmet on his head with a dusty cloth cover, night-vision mount on the front plate, side rails, chinstrap fastened, and ballistic goggles worn DOWN OVER HIS EYES — one wide scratched dusty lens with a broad tan strap round the helmet shell. Arid camo combat shirt, sleeves rolled above the elbow, tan plate carrier with stacked magazine pouches and a shoulder radio, tan gloves, everything dust-caked and sweat-stained.
NO INSIGNIA ANYWHERE: NO FLAG PATCH ON EITHER SLEEVE, no flag anywhere on him, on his helmet, on his plate carrier, on his pouches, on the sandbags or the wall. No unit patches, no name tapes, no rank, no badges, no lettering, no numbers, no symbols of any kind. Every sleeve and every panel of his kit is plain bare fabric.

THE WEAPON AND THE AMMUNITION BELT: a belt-fed light machine gun, dark receiver, tan furniture, resting across the sandbags. THERE IS EXACTLY ONE AMMUNITION BELT AND IT ENTERS THE GUN ON ONE SIDE ONLY — the LEFT side of the receiver, the feed side: a single linked run of brass cartridges that comes up out of the pouch hanging under the gun, curves once and goes into the feed tray, shortening and jumping as the gun fires. THE OTHER SIDE IS THE EJECTION SIDE AND HAS NO BELT AT ALL — only empty cases and short lengths of empty steel link spitting out and falling away. No belt on both sides, no second belt, no loop of cartridges hanging from the right side, no cartridges coming out of the ejection port, no belt over the top of the gun, no belt round his neck or shoulder, no draped bandolier.

HOW THE FALL WORKS — THIS IS DEAD WEIGHT, NOT AN ANIMATION. The instant he is hit he STOPS HOLDING HIMSELF UP and gravity does the rest. Nothing about it is even or symmetrical and no part of it looks chosen: the head goes first and the body follows it late; the weight comes off the gun unevenly so one shoulder drops before the other; one knee folds INWARD and sideways rather than straight down; his hip catches the sandbags on the way and turns him as he goes; one gloved hand drags across the top of a sandbag and slips off it; a boot scrapes and skids on the grit; the torso twists away from the impact and the plate carrier lags and thumps against him. He folds in the middle rather than toppling as one piece, arrives on the concrete heavy and lopsided, and there is no bracing, no catching himself, no attempt to control any of it. HE DOES NOT PAUSE, DOES NOT STIFFEN, DOES NOT SINK SLOWLY, DOES NOT ARCH BACKWARDS, DOES NOT DROP STRAIGHT DOWN LIKE A LIFT. All of it happens fast, in less than half a second, and the only thing that reads is that a working body stopped working.
NO BLOOD, no blood spray, no red mist, no wound, no hole, no gore, nothing of any injury shown at any point. His head and face are never lingered on after the impact — he is gone below the sandbags within a fraction of a second.

The receiver hammers, the belt on the left side jerks and shortens, empty brass and links fly out of the right side and tumble down the sandbags, the barrel shimmers with heat. Dust drifts across the bright opening. One brief jolt of the camera as something strikes the wall near us.
2.2-2.7s | The burst cuts off dead. His helmet snaps hard sideways and back with a small puff of dust off the cover, and the whole body lets go at once — head first, shoulders unevenly, one knee buckling inward, the hip catching the sandbags and turning him, a glove dragging off the bag, a boot skidding on grit.

表演任务——女服务员:

目标:平常一次结账,对面只是安静的常客。

战术:俯身、递夹、微笑、说完即直起身——她的眼睛没有停留;她的毫无察觉正是这段记忆的冰冷之处。

(安全线:目光始终投入任务,绝不僵死呆滞;自然眨眼节奏。)

咖啡液面随饮尽真实倾斜;账单夹人造革翻折带真实弧度与反光;热敏纸轻薄微颤;记忆碎片的拖影严格跟随动作方向;夜景白汽随风缓慢飘散。

声音

记忆碎片(1至8):一切闷、远、隔水——瓷杯轻碰、被吞尾音的"Your check."、人造革翻折、纸的脆响;每次闪切一声极短的低频撞击,节奏随碎片越来越密;镜头8上"447"的一拍,所有声音瞬间抽空——半秒真空。镜头9:声音骤然清晰真实——纽约深夜底噪、警笛、白汽嘶声、夜风。无音乐;唯一台词是镜头2的英语"Your check."。

夜。城市里一条安静的侧街,干燥无雨。目标独自沿着街走,杰克跟在他后面,保持着距离。全片三秒,没有事件,没有台词——只有一个人走,和另一个人跟着。

AFGHANISTAN, KABUL, DAY. 5s. THE GUNNER IN THE WINDOW IS HIT.

FRAME — REPEAT THIS COMPOSITION EXACTLY: camera stands INSIDE a dark room and looks OUT through a rectangular window opening. The whole surround of frame is the unlit interior wall — pure black, no detail, filling the outer two thirds of the picture on every side — and the bright hazy exterior sits in that black rectangle in the middle. On the sill, a row of dusty sandbags stacked two deep across the bottom of the opening. Beyond them, on the flat roof outside, ONE American MACHINE GUNNER stands behind his weapon, side-on to us, firing away to the right of frame. Behind him the city falls away into a pale bleached golden haze — flat roofs, a low block, a distant vehicle, all washed out and out of focus. Anamorphic 2.39:1, long lens, shallow focus: the sandbags and the gunner sharp, the city soft. Handheld with only a small unsteady drift and a couple of impact jolts — no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no cut.

THE GUNNER: tan combat helmet on his head with a dusty cloth cover, night-vision mount on the front plate, side rails, chinstrap fastened, and ballistic goggles worn DOWN OVER HIS EYES — one wide scratched dusty lens with a broad tan strap round the helmet shell. Arid camo combat shirt, sleeves rolled above the elbow, tan plate carrier with stacked magazine pouches and a shoulder radio, tan gloves, everything dust-caked and sweat-stained.
NO INSIGNIA ANYWHERE: NO FLAG PATCH ON EITHER SLEEVE, no flag anywhere on him, on his helmet, on his plate carrier, on his pouches, on the sandbags or the wall. No unit patches, no name tapes, no rank, no badges, no lettering, no numbers, no symbols of any kind. Every sleeve and every panel of his kit is plain bare fabric.

THE WEAPON AND THE AMMUNITION BELT: a belt-fed light machine gun, dark receiver, tan furniture, resting across the sandbags. THERE IS EXACTLY ONE AMMUNITION BELT AND IT ENTERS THE GUN ON ONE SIDE ONLY — the LEFT side of the receiver, the feed side: a single linked run of brass cartridges that comes up out of the pouch hanging under the gun, curves once and goes into the feed tray, shortening and jumping as the gun fires. THE OTHER SIDE IS THE EJECTION SIDE AND HAS NO BELT AT ALL — only empty cases and short lengths of empty steel link spitting out and falling away. No belt on both sides, no second belt, no loop of cartridges hanging from the right side, no cartridges coming out of the ejection port, no belt over the top of the gun, no belt round his neck or shoulder, no draped bandolier.

HOW THE FALL WORKS — THIS IS DEAD WEIGHT, NOT AN ANIMATION. The instant he is hit he STOPS HOLDING HIMSELF UP and gravity does the rest. Nothing about it is even or symmetrical and no part of it looks chosen: the head goes first and the body follows it late; the weight comes off the gun unevenly so one shoulder drops before the other; one knee folds INWARD and sideways rather than straight down; his hip catches the sandbags on the way and turns him as he goes; one gloved hand drags across the top of a sandbag and slips off it; a boot scrapes and skids on the grit; the torso twists away from the impact and the plate carrier lags and thumps against him. He folds in the middle rather than toppling as one piece, arrives on the concrete heavy and lopsided, and there is no bracing, no catching himself, no attempt to control any of it. HE DOES NOT PAUSE, DOES NOT STIFFEN, DOES NOT SINK SLOWLY, DOES NOT ARCH BACKWARDS, DOES NOT DROP STRAIGHT DOWN LIKE A LIFT. All of it happens fast, in less than half a second, and the only thing that reads is that a working body stopped working.
NO BLOOD, no blood spray, no red mist, no wound, no hole, no gore, nothing of any injury shown at any point. His head and face are never lingered on after the impact — he is gone below the sandbags within a fraction of a second.

0-2.2s | He is firing in bursts, side-on to us, leaning into the gun, weight shifting as he works it. The receiver hammers, the belt on the left side jerks and shortens, empty brass and links fly out of the right side and tumble down the sandbags, the barrel shimmers with heat. Dust drifts across the bright opening. One brief jolt of the camera as something strikes the wall near us.
2.2-2.7s | The burst cuts off dead. His helmet snaps hard sideways and back with a small puff of dust off the cover, and the whole body lets go at once — head first, shoulders unevenly, one knee buckling inward, the hip catching the sandbags and turning him, a glove dragging off the bag, a boot skidding on grit.
2.7-4s | He folds down out of sight behind the sandbags, hands leaving the gun. The machine gun is dragged a few centimetres by his falling weight, tips over on the bags with the muzzle swinging up and off target, and stops. One last empty case rolls down a sandbag and off the sill.
4-5s | The opening is empty except for the abandoned gun lying across the sandbags, its single belt hanging slack out of the feed side, a thread of smoke off the barrel. Dust and haze move in the bright rectangle. The black interior fills the rest of the frame. Hold.

GRADE: warm GOLDEN Afghan daylight — honey-and-sand, creamy gold sun blowing out the exterior, dusty tan and khaki, the interior surround crushed to pure black. 16mm grain, gentle halation, gold dust in the air. No lens flare, no starbursts, no streaks.

SOUND: the flat hammering of the machine gun close and dry, links and brass ringing on concrete, rounds cracking off stone around the window, distant AK fire, shouting somewhere below. At the moment the firing stops everything except the ambient fire drops away for a beat, then the heavy scrape and thud of his weight going down behind the bags and the gun shifting on them. No music, no stinger.

FORBIDDEN: no flag, no flag patch on any sleeve, no insignia, no unit patch, no name tape, no rank, no badge, no lettering or numbers anywhere on him or in frame. No robotic or mechanical fall, no symmetrical collapse, no straight-down drop, no stiffening, no pause before falling, no slow controlled sinking, no theatrical backward arch, no spin, no flying backwards, no mannequin or ragdoll physics, no floating, no bouncing on landing. He never staggers, never clutches his head, never turns to camera, never reaches for the gun as he goes. No ammunition belt on both sides of the gun, no belt on the ejection side, no second belt, no live cartridges from the ejection port. NO BLOOD, no spray, no red mist, no wound, no bullet hole, no spatter on the sandbags or wall, no gore, no body lingered on, no face of the dead, no screaming. Nobody else in frame, no second soldier, no medic, nobody comes for him in this shot. He is never without helmet or goggles, and the goggles are never pushed up or removed. No camera movement beyond the small drift and the impact jolts, no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no rack focus, no cut, no slow motion, no speed ramp. No explosions, no aircraft, no enemy visible. No text, no subtitles. No clean uniform, no costume look, no cold grade. Not anime, not animated, not a video game, no CGI look.

NO US FLAG PATCH ON EITHER SLEEVE. NO US FLAG ANYWHERE.

FRAME — REPEAT THIS COMPOSITION EXACTLY: camera stands INSIDE a dark room and looks OUT through a rectangular window opening. The whole surround of frame is the unlit interior wall — pure black, no detail, filling the outer two thirds of the picture on every side — and the bright hazy exterior sits in that black rectangle in the middle. On the sill, a row of dusty sandbags stacked two deep across the bottom of the opening. Beyond them, on the flat roof outside, ONE MACHINE GUNNER stands behind his weapon, side-on to us, firing away to the right of frame. Behind him the city falls away into a pale bleached golden haze — flat roofs, a low block, a distant vehicle, all washed out and out of focus. Anamorphic 2.39:1, long lens, shallow focus: the sandbags and the gunner sharp, the city soft. Handheld with only a small unsteady drift and a couple of impact jolts — no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no cut.

THE GUNNER: tan combat helmet on his head with a dusty cloth cover, night-vision mount on the front plate, side rails, chinstrap fastened, and ballistic goggles worn DOWN OVER HIS EYES — one wide scratched dusty lens with a broad tan strap round the helmet shell. Arid camo combat shirt, sleeves rolled above the elbow, tan plate carrier with stacked magazine pouches and a shoulder radio, tan gloves, everything dust-caked and sweat-stained.
NO INSIGNIA ANYWHERE: NO FLAG PATCH ON EITHER SLEEVE, no flag anywhere on him, on his helmet, on his plate carrier, on his pouches, on the sandbags or the wall. No unit patches, no name tapes, no rank, no badges, no lettering, no numbers, no symbols of any kind. Every sleeve and every panel of his kit is plain bare fabric.

THE WEAPON AND THE AMMUNITION BELT: a belt-fed light machine gun, dark receiver, tan furniture, resting across the sandbags. THERE IS EXACTLY ONE AMMUNITION BELT AND IT ENTERS THE GUN ON ONE SIDE ONLY — the LEFT side of the receiver, the feed side: a single linked run of brass cartridges that comes up out of the pouch hanging under the gun, curves once and goes into the feed tray, shortening and jumping as the gun fires. THE OTHER SIDE IS THE EJECTION SIDE AND HAS NO BELT AT ALL — only empty cases and short lengths of empty steel link spitting out and falling away. No belt on both sides, no second belt, no loop of cartridges hanging from the right side, no cartridges coming out of the ejection port, no belt over the top of the gun, no belt round his neck or shoulder, no draped bandolier.

HOW THE FALL WORKS — THIS IS DEAD WEIGHT, NOT AN ANIMATION. The instant he is hit he STOPS HOLDING HIMSELF UP and gravity does the rest. Nothing about it is even or symmetrical and no part of it looks chosen: the head goes first and the body follows it late; the weight comes off the gun unevenly so one shoulder drops before the other; one knee folds INWARD and sideways rather than straight down; his hip catches the sandbags on the way and turns him as he goes; one gloved hand drags across the top of a sandbag and slips off it; a boot scrapes and skids on the grit; the torso twists away from the impact and the plate carrier lags and thumps against him. He folds in the middle rather than toppling as one piece, arrives on the concrete heavy and lopsided, and there is no bracing, no catching himself, no attempt to control any of it. HE DOES NOT PAUSE, DOES NOT STIFFEN, DOES NOT SINK SLOWLY, DOES NOT ARCH BACKWARDS, DOES NOT DROP STRAIGHT DOWN LIKE A LIFT. All of it happens fast, in less than half a second, and the only thing that reads is that a working body stopped working.
NO wound, no hole, no gore, nothing of any injury shown at any point. His head and face are never lingered on after the impact — he is gone below the sandbags within a fraction of a second.

场景背景
夜。一场高级慈善晚宴——水晶吊灯,暖金烛光,香槟色,礼服与晚礼服的人群在大厅里谈笑。杰克今晚是端着托盘的侍者之一,面孔平凡、毫不起眼。一杯香槟里被放了东西;一个男人喝下它。杰克站在远处,看着那个人慢慢意识到不对劲。全片约15秒。几乎无台词(只有人群的环境声与最后的惊呼)。

风格
《杀手》式芬奇冷静:高级但浑浊的色调,暖金烛光与香槟色浮在克制的青绿暗部上;整体欠曝一档半,画面活在阴影上部;黑位深沉带质感;肤色自然温暖。轻微记忆柔焦——边缘微融、高光晕成椭圆,但比闪回段落清醒、稳定。

摄影机与镜头
RED Gemini,Leica定制镜头加低反差滤镜,无刺眼高光。复古2倍变形宽银幕,2.39:1:椭圆拉伸焦外,边缘猫眼光斑,失焦高光抹成水平长椭圆,轻微色差,低饱和克制色彩。运动为电动机械运动——微距细节镜头,以及缓慢精确的推近与横移;绝不手持抖动。无镜头眩光,无光线拉丝。

激活参考
<<<cd7d691a-d4f5-46ca-920c-00b72c36ebee>>>——杰克,四十五岁左右消瘦沧桑,灰白短发,浅灰眼睛;此场作侍者:白衬衫、黑色马甲、黑领结、白手套或黑手套,端一只银托盘,毫不起眼地融入侍者之中。目标:六十岁上下优雅银发男子,合身晚礼服,谈吐从容,今晚的贵宾之一。参考图只控制外貌,不控制画面亮度。

首帧与空间调度
中近景:水晶吊灯下的宴会厅,暖金烛光,香槟色的人群虚化在纵深里。前景是杰克端着的银托盘,盘上几只斟满的高脚香槟杯,气泡上升。

格式模式
单一场景,约15秒,数个连贯镜头,硬切不多。环境有声,几乎无台词。

动作时间轴

0.0-3.0秒 | 微距,那滴东西。极浅景深微距:杰克戴手套的手托着银盘,另一只手在盘沿的遮挡下,拇指与食指间一粒小小的白色药片(或一滴透明液体)极自然地落进最外侧那只香槟杯——气泡里一串极细的涟漪,药片在杯底融开、消失。整个动作藏在托盘边缘,快而不慌,像只是在整理杯子。周围的谈笑声、杯盏轻碰声不停。

3.0-6.0秒 | 递杯。杰克端盘走近人群,银发男子正与旁人谈笑,顺手从盘上取走那只最外侧的杯子——杰克的脸平淡无波,不多看他一眼,端着盘继续走开、退入人群。银发男子举杯,啜了一口,继续说话,毫无察觉。

6.0-9.0秒 | 远处的杰克在看。切到大厅另一侧:杰克已退到远处,端着空了几只的托盘,站在侍者该站的位置,浅灰的眼睛越过谈笑的人群,平静地、精准地锁在那个男人身上——像在核对一件事的进度。前景是流动的礼服人群,把他和目标隔开,他毫不起眼。

9.0-12.0秒 | 不对劲。切回银发男子:他说话的声音慢下来,笑容凝住,眉头困惑地皱起;他的手抬到喉咙上,像想清一清嗓子,又像被什么堵住——他扯了扯领结,呼吸变得费力,脸上是纯粹的不解:发生了什么?他扶住旁边的桌沿,身体晃了一下。旁边的人开始察觉,转过头来。

12.0-15.0秒 | 下沉与惊慌。银发男子撑不住,顺着桌沿缓缓滑坐、倒下,带响一两只杯子;周围的宾客惊呼、后退又围拢,有人蹲下去扶他、有人四处张望呼救——人群乱成一团。在这片慌乱的边缘、纵深的另一端,杰克端着托盘安静地转身,浅灰的眼睛最后掠过那片混乱一眼,然后平静地没入侍者通道的暗处。最后一帧落在他离开的背影上。切黑。

表演任务
杰克——动机:这不是对抗,是一道工序;工件是那只杯子,不是那个人。战术:放药的手法自然得像在整理托盘,眼睛扫的是谁在看他的手;递杯时不与目标对视、不多停一秒;退到远处后,他只做一件事——核对进度,确认那口酒下去、确认反应开始;人群的惊慌对他而言是画面里的天气,不是信息,他的脸毫无起伏,最后转身离开时也不快不慢。
目标——各阶段的真实:先是从容谈笑、毫无防备;喝下后一切如常;然后是那半秒"这解释不通"的困惑——他不知道是酒、不知道是谁,只知道身体不听使唤了;不解一直持续到下沉,他至死没明白。
宾客——真实的旁观者:先当他是喝多了或不舒服,愣一下,然后才反应过来事情不对,惊呼、围拢、呼救,乱而真实。
(安全线:活着的人眼睛自然投入、自然眨眼;不演夸张。)

物理
香槟气泡里药片融化的涟漪细小真实;高脚杯被取走时液面轻晃;男子扯领结、扶桌沿有真实的重量与失衡;下沉时带响桌上的杯子;人群围拢时的推挤与走动自然。轻微记忆柔焦跟随动作方向。

声音
晚宴环境声:弦乐四重奏的轻柔背景乐、人群谈笑、杯盏轻碰、脚步——一切优雅正常。目标出问题时,近处的谈笑先没注意,随后一声"你还好吗?"、椅子拖动、一片倒吸气的惊呼、"快叫医生!"的呼喊、慌乱的脚步——声音由优雅滑向混乱。杰克那一侧始终安静。无旁白。

时长：27秒。深夜——把黑夜锁死：深夜，无月，厚云密布，天空是黑的，没有日光、没有蓝调余晖。

亮度锁——比现在暗得多，这是最重要的一条：巢穴 内部几乎完全是黑的，画面绝大部分（约百分之九十）是没有细节的纯黑。巢穴内部没有任何光源——没有灯、没有实用光、没有补光、没有环境光。唯一的光是从他远离镜头那一侧的窗户射入的一道冰冷微弱的街灯（钠黄与钢蓝），这道光又低又弱，只够勾出他远侧的脸缘、肩线和枪管的一道细边。他靠近镜头的这半张脸——脸颊、眼窝——完全沉进纯黑里，看不见细节。房间、墙壁、桌子、他的身体大部分都是黑的，只在窗光扫到的边缘才浮出一点点冷色的轮廓。整体在正常曝光基础上再压暗两到三档。深沉压死的黑位，冷蓝绿色调绝对主导。调色：芬奇/克罗嫩威斯《搏击俱乐部》风格，去饱和，深度欠曝，细腻颗粒。绝不把巢穴照亮、绝不让他整张脸都看清、绝不出现均匀的补光。

镜头1（0-5秒）——巢穴 全景，几乎全黑： 卧在长边朝窗的长射击台上，步枪 <<<5cf041e3-3a8e-42ea-81ae-4c8bc52da795>>> 枪管朝玻璃伸出；他正盯着街对面那栋房子。房间陷在纯黑里，只有窗口那道冷光在他的肩线、后脑与枪管上勾出极细的边，其余全部沉入黑暗。塑料布在画面边缘的暗影里随风微动。
镜头2（5-9秒）——他贴在瞄准镜上的面部特写：脸颊紧贴枪托，一只眼睛贴着目镜；靠近镜头的左半张脸完全沉在纯黑里、看不见，只有远侧的脸缘挂着一道冰冷的细边，那只贴着目镜的眼睛在微光里反着一点湿光。只有眼睛在工作。没有任何雾气或白气。
镜头3（9-13秒）——他透过瞄准镜 <<<784c1df8-6501-430a-b08a-76ca5ab4ce6a>>> 的主观视角——圆形视野、分划线与暗角完全与 <<<784c1df8-6501-430a-b08a-76ca5ab4ce6a>>> 一致：街对面，<<<95dc4fe7-69b3-447f-90e4-b4dcc006575c>>> 的三楼——并排三扇高大的黑框窗户，全部漆黑，没有一盏灯，家里没人。这个镜头不是静止的：瞄准镜从左边那扇窗开始，缓慢连续地平移，经过中间那扇，一直摇到右边那扇，一次平滑的横摇，分划线依次滑过每一块漆黑的玻璃，运动之上叠加呼吸的晃动；不停在任何一扇窗上，也绝不变焦。
镜头4（13-22秒）——中景，从他的正前方拍摄，摄影机架在靠窗一侧回望他，略偏他的左侧、并且很低，位于他视线以下略微向上仰拍：整个画面依旧极暗，他大部分沉在黑里。他把眼睛从瞄准镜上移开，把手腕抬进窗口那道冷光里去看一只划痕累累的黑色军表——只有抬进那道光里的前臂下侧和表盘浮出黑暗，其余仍是黑的；他的眼睛向下瞥去——短短一瞥，手随即放回步枪上，手臂重新沉回黑暗。随后，在同一个不间断的镜头里，摄影机开始缓慢平稳地推近他的脸，在余下的几秒内从中景推成紧的特写——最终停在黑暗中他的眼睛上，半张脸被纯黑吞没，只有远侧一道冷边，他眨着眼，等待着。他在等某个人。没有白气、没有雾气。
镜头5（22-27秒）——同样是从他左前方、低位的正面角度，紧紧框住他的头与肩，画面仍旧极暗、大半是黑：街上传来闷闷的汽车引擎声；他抬起头，把目光转向左侧、朝着声音的方向、画外——停一拍，眨着眼——然后重新俯身贴上瞄准镜，把眼睛凑到目镜上，朝汽车将要出现的方向瞄去。远侧脸缘的冷边随他低头移动，近侧始终在黑里。

活人表演——他必须像一个真正呼吸的人，绝不是凝固的雕像：胸口与肩膀随缓慢真实的呼吸起伏，自然而不规律的眨眼，眼球细微的无意识移动，一次吞咽，下颌一丝轻微的抽动，双手在枪上细微地调整。不要用嘴里的白气或雾气来表现呼吸——通过肩膀起伏和眼睛的活来表现。
表演任务——：职业者的耐心——没有大动作，但他是活的：眼睛与手腕；看表不是无聊，而是他信任的时间表；引擎声传来时，头先于身体转动，重新贴上瞄准镜是一个经济的动作。

声音：只有巢穴——房间底噪、塑料布拍打、他缓慢平稳的呼吸、桌板在他重量下一声轻微的吱呀、远处闷闷的纽约夜；第22秒起，下方街道传来渐近的汽车引擎声，经过玻璃与距离的过滤。

禁止：任何白气、雾气、呼出的水汽、嘴边的哈气——完全不要；把巢穴照亮、让他整张脸都看清、均匀的补光、任何巢穴内部的光源（灯、屏幕、指示灯）；抬起的黑位、发灰发亮的暗部、朦胧的灰雾；日光、天光、蓝调；镜头眩光、光线拉丝、星芒；字幕、水印；音乐；非动画、非游戏CG、无塑料感皮肤。 <<<cd7d691a-d4f5-46ca-920c-00b72c36ebee>>>

END CREDIT SEQUENCE — THE WORK, WITH THE ORDERS OVER IT. 30s. Five killings, each carrying one printed slip superimposed in frame.

【TEXT LOCK — HIGHEST PRIORITY, READ FIRST】
Five slips appear, one per scene, in this order, each carrying EXACTLY this text and nothing else. All capitals, dot-matrix monospace, correctly spelled:

SLIP 1: "WRITTEN AND DIRECTED BY" / "ALDIYAR BAIRAKIMOV" / "ILIYAS BAKTYGUL"
SLIP 2: "SOUND DESIGN" / "DIAS BEKTAYEV"
SLIP 3: "COLORIST" / "DANIEL BAYANDIN"
SLIP 4: "SPECIAL THANKS" / "CHINGIZ ESELBAEV"
SLIP 5: "HIGGSFIELD ORIGINALS"

Spelled letter by letter so there is no doubt: A-L-D-I-Y-A-R B-A-I-R-A-K-I-M-O-V. I-L-I-Y-A-S B-A-K-T-Y-G-U-L. D-I-A-S B-E-K-T-A-Y-E-V. D-A-N-I-E-L B-A-Y-A-N-D-I-N. C-H-I-N-G-I-Z E-S-E-L-B-A-E-V. H-I-G-G-S-F-I-E-L-D O-R-I-G-I-N-A-L-S.
No other words exist anywhere in this sequence — no addresses, no target names, no descriptions, no priorities, no numbers, no dates, no logos, no marks, no symbols, no subtitles. While a slip is on screen its text is razor sharp and fully legible, and no letter blurs, wobbles, re-forms, swaps, disappears or changes spelling. Each scene carries only its own block; the blocks never mix and never appear together.

【HOW THE SLIPS SIT IN THE FRAME — NEVER A SEPARATE SHOT】
The slips are NOT cut to. They are SUPERIMPOSED INTO THE LIVE SCENE and the scene keeps playing behind and around them the whole time. Each slip is a warm grey-cream thermal paper strip, slightly curled, printed in black dot-matrix monospace with individual pin dots visible inside every character, characters fractionally off the baseline, a dotted tear line above the block. It sits to ONE SIDE of frame, occupying about a quarter of the picture width, in a clear area of the composition where it never covers the action. The paper itself is semi-transparent so the scene reads faintly through it; THE TEXT ITSELF IS FULLY OPAQUE AND PERFECTLY SHARP.
It appears as the killing lands — not before — with a fast one-frame arrival, holds still while it is read, and is gone before the cut. It never slides, never scrolls, never scales, never rotates, never animates: it is simply there and then not there. The side alternates scene to scene: left, right, left, right, then centred for the last one.
THE CAMERA NEVER CUTS AWAY TO THE PAPER, and there are no macro inserts of it anywhere in this sequence.

【REFERENCES】
<<<image_1>>> = JACK — his face, build and age decided by this asset alone. Dark overcoat and gloves, or a plain dark suit. His face is never brightly lit and never fills the frame; he is a presence, not a portrait. The five targets are strangers, ordinary faces, each on screen a couple of seconds only.

【THE LAW FOR ALL FIVE KILLINGS】
Each scene cuts in mid-action and cuts out before it finishes. Death reads as a working body that stops working, never as violence performed for the camera. NO BLOOD, no spray, no mist, no wounds, no bullet holes, no spatter, no gore, no bodies lingered on, no faces of the dead, nobody thrashing or screaming. The living blink naturally with their eyes engaged in what they are doing; the dead never blink and never breathe.
THE SUPPRESSOR IS THE SIGNATURE — AND IT IS ALWAYS ALREADY FITTED, IN FRAME, VISIBLE. Every time the pistol appears, the long suppressor is threaded onto the barrel and readable in the shot: it is why nobody in the building hears anything. When it fires, the muzzle points INTO THE DEPTH of frame at the target, the flash is one short flare into that depth, the body falls along the line the muzzle points, and the recoil kicks the frame out of focus and straight back. Never towards camera, never off to one side while the body falls elsewhere.

【GRADE, CAMERA, LENS】
Fincher night palette: sickly fluorescent green and steel blue, sodium amber only where a street lamp allows it, no clean whites, murky crushed blacks with texture, low exposure throughout, desaturated. RED Gemini, Leica primes with a low-contrast filter, vintage 2x anamorphic: oval stretched bokeh, cat-eye at the frame edges, defocused highlights smeared into horizontal ovals, mild chromatic aberration, soft vignette, fine 35mm grain. Slight Dutch tilt, eight to fifteen degrees, alternating direction scene to scene, levelling out only in the last scene. No lens flare, no light streaks, no starbursts. Environmental colour stains the environment and the edges of skin only and NEVER enters anyone's eyes.
THE CUTTING ACCELERATES: the first scenes breathe, the last are tighter, the cuts harder, a couple of them carrying one near-white frame. Then everything stops on the final card.

No dialogue. Everything muffled and distant, as if remembered. City hum far below the penthouse; fluorescent buzz and a far-off vacuum in the office; rain on a car roof and wipers beating in the street; polythene rustling and a conveyor motor in the dry cleaner; compressor hum in the freezer and then a beat of pure vacuum. Every suppressed shot is a flat compressed thump, small, never cinematic — mechanical action, not gunfire. 【FORBIDDEN】
No cut to a macro of the paper, no separate slip shot, no slip before the killing lands, no slip scrolling, sliding, rolling, scaling or animating, no slip covering the action, no two slips at once, no slip on the wrong scene. No misspelling of any name, no missing, doubled, mirrored or invented characters, no letters melting or re-forming, no extra credit lines, no target names or addresses, no logos or marks, no watermark, no borders, no UI, no subtitles.
NO BLOOD, no spray, no mist, no wounds, no bullet holes, no spatter, no gore, no bodies lingered on, no faces of the dead, nobody thrashing, choking or screaming. No pistol without its suppressor fitted, no pistol pointed at camera, no shot fired into empty frame, no shot where the muzzle points one way and the body falls another. No knives, no strangling, no drowning, no poison, no explosions, no fire. Nobody dies on a metro platform, nobody dies in water, no car wash, no shooting range — those places do not appear.
The dead never blink and never breathe. Environmental colour never enters anyone's eyes; no glowing or colour-changed eyes. No slow motion, no speed ramps, no bullet time, no zooms, no whip pans. No lens flare, no light streaks, no starbursts. No clean bright interiors, no daylight, no warm postcard grade. Not anime, not animated, not a video game, no CGI or game-engine look, no plastic skin.

SCENE: Evening, the open-air pool in the back yard of a luxury modern villa. The elderly master of the house swims alone; Jack pushes him under the water and holds him there. Jack is expressionless throughout, utterly without mercy.

STYLE — the grammar of memory: dreamlike heavy soft focus — edges melting, highlights blooming into ovals, a very light motion trail; the piece opens with one near-white flash frame, like a memory suddenly spliced in. Evening: the daylight has just died, one line of deep indigo left in the sky, the rest of the yard sunk in darkness; the only strong source is the pool's underwater lights — the whole pool is a sheet of glass glowing a sickly blue-green, the netted caustics from the water surface constantly crawling across the villa's white walls, the full-height glazing and the terrace ceiling; a few warm floor lamps glow inside the villa; an outdoor fire bowl burns on the terrace throwing orange-red; warm pool water raises a thin mist into the cool night. Underexposed about 1.5 stops, blacks deep but keeping texture; skin always natural and warm.

CAMERA & LENS: RED Gemini, custom Leica lenses with a low-contrast filter, no harsh highlights. Vintage 2x anamorphic, 2.39:1, wide open: oval-stretched bokeh, cat-eye edges, out-of-focus highlights smeared into horizontal ovals, subtle chromatic aberration, low-saturation restrained colour. No lens flare, no light streaks, straight edges stay straight. All movement is motorized mechanical movement — dolly, slow push-in, vertical descent, locked underwater positions, even and precise, never handheld. Normal speed, no slow motion.

REFERENCE: <<<cd7d691a-d4f5-46ca-920c-00b72c36ebee>>> — Jack, around fifty, lean and weathered, grey-brown hair swept back, grey-green eyes, stubble, a weathered face. This scene: black nylon hooded windbreaker, black gloves.
THE TARGET: a white man around seventy, bloated and slack, big belly, loose flesh piled on his shoulders and back, bald, only a ring of white hair left at the back and sides, slack skin covered in age spots, a broad heavy gold ring on his hand; dark swim trunks, no swim cap, no goggles. His expression carries the impatient arrogance of a man used to being waited on — a rich old man used to everyone revolving around him. The two are completely different in build, age and clothing, never confusable.

FIRST FRAME & STAGING: underwater position, locked deep at the bottom of the pool, the lens looking vertically up at the surface. The frame is almost all blue-green glowing water and the rippling surface above, the surface like a shifting silver ceiling; the tile lines of the pool walls converge toward the top of frame. For now there is no one above the surface.

FORMAT: five shots, about 17.5 seconds total. Memory soft focus throughout.

ACTION TIMELINE:
SHOT 1 — 0.0-3.5s — evening, villa back yard, wide, very slow push-in. Behind the full-height glass is the warm-lit interior, the fire bowl burning on the terrace, landscape lights edging the neatly trimmed hedges, the stone paving reflecting pool light; on a low table an ice bucket with sparkling wine, beside it a half-finished wine glass and an ashtray with a still-smoking cigar resting on the rim; a bathrobe thrown over a lounger, a gold watch left beside it. The pool is the only strong light source in the yard. The bloated old man is climbing slowly down the pool ladder into the water, his movements slow and laboured, the surface broken, the caustics scattering on the walls for a moment then slowly recovering. In the darkness at the far end of the pool, tight against the hedge, a black hooded figure crouches motionless.
CUT AT 3.5s
SHOT 2 — 3.5-7.5s — [GRAPHIC SHOT] locked underwater position, shooting up from the pool floor, the camera staying deep at the bottom, far from the surface. He swims slowly across above — a dark silhouette fully against the glowing surface, only a heavy body visible: round thick torso, short stubby limbs slowly doing a breaststroke pull, the rhythm mechanical and laboured, like completing the daily laps a doctor prescribed; his body casts a moving shadow on the pool floor, sweeping across the lens. Where the surface is parted fine bubbles and shimmering silver rise, the netted caustics crawling slowly across the floor. The whole shot quiet and restrained, only contour and light, detail lost in the backlit black shape.
CUT AT 7.5s
SHOT 3 — 7.5-12.5s — [CORE SHOT] mid-close from the pool edge, slightly above, locked camera. He swims to the pool wall, both hands gripping the coping, tilts his head up gasping for air, shoulders heaving — and in that instant he senses someone beside him, whips his head round, lets out a short hoarse cry. Jack has already stepped from the hedge shadow to the pool edge, drops onto one knee on the wet slick coping, both hands clamping the back of his head and his shoulder, driving the weight of his upper body down — the cry is cut off hard the instant his head goes under. His resistance is violent but formless: arms flailing up great sheets of spray, body thrashing and twisting in the water, fingers clawing at Jack's forearms, nails scraping a few marks; but his strength cannot last more than a few seconds, the more he struggles the less air he has. For Jack the hard part is not the man's strength but that heavy slick body: the slack flesh slips under the gloves, his grip won't hold, he has to re-adjust his hold twice; his knee slips on the wet tile, his body pitches forward, he drops his weight lower to steady it. Water slops over the coping again and again, knocking over the wine glass at the edge, his sleeves and trouser legs soaked through, the muscles of his shoulders and back taut, his breathing gone rough. Through all of it his face does not change at all — no gritted teeth, no frown, no disgust, his eyes simply cast down at the water below, like watching a stopwatch run out. The caustics on shore go wild across the villa's walls and glass with the violent spray.

GEOGRAPHY: seen from the side along the parapet, JACK NEARER CAMERA, TERRENCE JUST BEYOND. They never swap.
TERRENCE'S RIFLE IS SILENT AND STAYS SILENT: no report, no muzzle flash, no recoil, no smoke, no ejected case. His gloved index finger lies FLAT along the outside of the trigger guard and never returns to the trigger. The shot has already been fired by Jack, before this clip begins.

SHOT 1 — 0.0–4.0s | THE TWO OF THEM, FROM THE SIDE.
Slow motion, one held frame: a side-on two-shot along the parapet, both men close together, both in profile, both still in a crouch behind the capping.
JACK leans on the parapet, chest and left forearm taking his weight. IN HIS LEFT HAND, EXTENDED OVER THE CAPPING, IS HIS BLACK PISTOL, still out toward where the boy stood, arm not yet down, A THIN RIBBON OF SMOKE drifting off the muzzle. His right-thigh holster is EMPTY. His RIGHT SHOULDER IS HITCHED UP AND PULLED BACK, stained sleeve tight, RIGHT ARM CLAMPED against his ribs, gloved hand tucked to his side.
Beyond him TERRENCE is still on his knee on the long sand-coloured suppressed sniper rifle, cheek on the stock, eye at the scope, finger flat along the outside of the guard, muzzle clean and smokeless.
Neither speaks. THEN JACK TURNS HIS HEAD, inside the same frame, and LOOKS AT TERRENCE. The look holds to the cut.

SHOT 2 — 4.0–7.0s | THE LAST SHOT — HE GOES DOWN.
Cut across the gap to the boy's open second floor: a LOW, TIGHT ANGLE just above the dusty broken concrete, camera almost at floor level, stones and grit and gold light raking along them. Slow motion.
THE BOY COMES DOWN INTO FRAME AND LANDS. He arrives ALREADY COMPLETELY LIMP — dead weight, with no bracing of any kind: the arms do NOT come out to break the fall, the head does NOT tuck, the body does not try to catch itself at any point.
He lands on the shoulder and hip, the stones taking the whole weight at once. The head, out of frame, does not lift. ONE LEG FOLDS UNDER THE TORSO AT AN ANGLE A CONSCIOUS BODY WOULD NEVER HOLD, the boot turned over on its side. ONE ARM IS TRAPPED BENEATH HIM, dragged under by the fall. THE OTHER ARM FLINGS OUT ACROSS THE CONCRETE and comes to rest palm-up, the fingers slack and half-curled, the wrist bent back against the stones.
Dust bursts up and hangs. The clothing settles a moment after the body has already stopped.
AND THEN NOTHING — no roll, no settle, no shift of weight, no attempt to gather himself, not one twitch, not one breath. The body is entirely still from the instant it touches the ground, and stays that way.
The launcher comes down with him, clatters onto the stones and rolls a half turn TO A STOP RIGHT BESIDE HIS OPEN HAND, a hand's width apart.
The dust settles back over both. HIS HEAD AND FACE ARE TURNED AWAY FROM CAMERA AND ENTIRELY OUT OF FRAME — we see him from the shoulder down and no further. NO FACE, NO BLOOD, NO WOUND, NOTHING ELSE IN FRAME. Hold. Last frame.

ACTING TASK — JACK: he has just done it himself with the only hand he has, and it was arithmetic, not courage. He is not looking for agreement. The final look is not contempt — a man handing over a bill he has just paid for both of them.
ACTING TASK — TERRENCE: he refused, and the price has been paid without him. Hard, controlled, completely dry-eyed — nothing in the face, nothing in the body, the finger still flat along the guard. He does not flinch, does not turn, does not speak.

SOUND: dust falling, small fires far off, a long high ringing tone under everything. Jack's breath wet and hard. The mix is heavy and stretched throughout. Over the last shot: the heavy soft impact of a body onto concrete — a single dull sound with no second impact and no scrape after it — a burst of dust, then the harder clatter and dull roll of a steel tube on stone, then nothing. Terrence makes no vocal sound. No music, no dialogue.

FILM STYLE — Afghanistan war flashback, fixed for the whole film.

IDENTITY (top priority): 2.39:1, true human proportions, faces exactly match the reference images — bone structure, eye spacing, nose, jaw, skin tone. If any instruction pulls a face off the reference, drop the instruction and keep the face.

CAMERA: RED, custom Leica lenses, vintage 2x anamorphic — vertical oval bokeh, cat-eye edges, out-of-focus highlights smeared horizontally, subtle chromatic aberration, soft vignette. Clean coating: no flares, no light streaks, no starbursts. Handheld, alive, real war-documentary energy, close and kinetic.

GRADE: warm golden Afghan memory — honey-and-sand palette, creamy gold sunlight, dusty tan and khaki, warm sun-touched skin, 16mm texture, fine grain, gentle halation. Low saturation.

KIT LOCK (mandatory, taken from the references): every soldier in frame wears a tactical combat helmet with a fabric cover and an NVG bracket, and ballistic goggles or glasses over the eyes — no exceptions. Desert-tan coyote camo, plate carrier, gloves, caked in sweat and dust, worn not costume-like. Every surface of the uniform is PLAIN BARE FABRIC: sleeves, shoulders, chest and helmet cover unmarked — no patches, no insignia, no emblems, no writing, no symbols anywhere on clothing or gear. Jack's and Terrence's kit and weapons are exactly as in their reference images and never change. All long guns are sand-coloured, matching the references; the only black weapon is the pistol.

THE OTHER TWO SOLDIERS: two more soldiers climb with them in identical kit to the references — same helmets with fabric covers, same ballistic goggles, same desert-tan camo and plate carriers, same sand-coloured long guns, same plain unmarked fabric. Their faces stay behind goggles, helmet brims, shoulders and dust, kept in the background or cut by the frame, so they read as the same team and no new face is ever the subject of a frame.

【TACTICAL MOVEMENT LAW — HOW THEY MOVE, THIS IS THE POINT OF THE SHOT】
These are working professionals under threat, not men walking upstairs. Every body reads as a weapon system moving.
— The rifle is SHOULDERED, stock into the pocket, cheek near the stock, eyes over the sights. The muzzle leads wherever the man is looking; head and muzzle move together as one unit and never point in different directions.
— Knees bent, weight forward and low, centre of gravity dropped, back straight, elbows tucked in tight to clear the narrow shaft. No upright strolling, no swinging arms, no waddling, no bouncing shoulders, no rifle hanging slack from one hand.
— Feet roll heel to toe in short deliberate steps, each foot tested on the mud step before the weight goes onto it, one hand off the wall for balance. Quiet, economical, no stamping.
— They move by SECTORS: the lead man's muzzle covers the top of the stairwell and the landing above; the second man's muzzle covers the turn of the stairs; the last man turns his upper body and covers back DOWN the shaft behind them. Someone is always looking at the danger the others cannot see.
— At the turn of the staircase the lead man SLICES THE PIE: he steps out in small arcs around the corner, muzzle first, exposing only a sliver of himself, clearing the angle a piece at a time before committing his body past it.
— They move in bounds, not in a continuous stream: one man moves while the others hold and cover, then the next moves. Short bursts, then a held beat with weapons up, then the next bound.
— Hand signals only — a raised fist to hold, two fingers to move. Nobody speaks.
— Contact readiness at all times: chins slightly down, shoulders forward, ready to drop or fire in the same instant. The lead man's stance says he expects someone to come around the corner at him right now.

ACTING: don't play emotion, play the execution of tactics; the work is in the eyes. Safety line: gaze always engaged, natural blinking.

SCENE: war flashback, Afghanistan, harsh gold daylight outside. Inside a two-storey mud building the team goes UP the inner staircase to take the rooftop position. Nothing else happens in this shot.

ACTION (10s):
0–2.5s | Ground floor, bare mud walls, dust hanging in shafts of gold light from the window openings. The four stack tight at the foot of a narrow mud staircase, weapons shouldered, muzzles already covering the top of the shaft. A raised fist holds them, then two fingers, and the lead man bounds up the first steps low and quiet while the others cover.
2.5–6s | Handheld, close, riding the climb: knees bent, elbows in, boots rolling heel to toe on worn mud steps, sand-coloured rifles up and tight in the narrow shaft, plate carriers brushing the wall, grit sifting down through the gold light. They move in bounds — one man up, a held beat with muzzles covering, the next man up. The last man's upper body is turned, muzzle covering back down the stairs behind them.
6–8.5s | The turn of the staircase. <<<d0095f26-63a3-4c38-974d-89208cb6546f>>> slices the pie around the corner — small arcs, muzzle first, only a sliver of him exposed — goggles catching the gold light for a second, eyes and muzzle moving together up the shaft, reading the top before he gets there. He holds the angle while the man behind him moves.
8.5–10s | <<<36b8fb78-402b-464b-8cc4-1b1898c1f0b2>>> on the last steps, still low, rifle up and leading: the hard white-gold daylight of the roof opening washes down over his helmet and goggles as his muzzle, then his head and shoulders, rise into it. He pauses one beat under the opening, weapon covering the gap, then commits. Hold on him entering the light. End.

Terrence — motive: cover his partner. Goal: hold the angle nobody else can see. Tactic: he takes the corner and the top of the shaft — he is the one who sees things coming.
Safety line: gazes engaged in the task, natural blinking.

影片开场的最后一个镜头。白天,一家老式美式咖啡馆。杰克双手捧着已经翻开的黑色人造革账单夹,低头在读夹子里那张热敏纸上印着的订单。这是全片第一次给到他的脸。他一句话都不说;只有男性英语画外旁白的最后一句。

旁白声音(最高优先级)
声音属于一个四十五岁上下的男人。音高极低,男低音区,重心完全压在胸腔里,共鸣厚重发闷。质地非常沙哑粗粝,带砂砾与低频毛刺,喉咙深处带一点近似低吼的摩擦音,句尾破音带气。咬字含混、往回吞,像在自言自语地嘟囔,词尾常被吞掉,辅音软化模糊,音与音之间黏连,绝不字正腔圆。音量不大,压着嗓子说,几乎是低声咕哝,但密度很高,像贴着耳朵。节奏紧凑往前推,句尾干脆收掉。情绪平直,不加重任何词。绝不清亮、绝不年轻、绝不圆润、绝不明亮、绝不播音腔、绝不温和,也绝不是老人的颤抖声。

《杀手》式浑浊橄榄绿与硫磺黄,整体欠曝一档半,画面活在阴影上部;黑位深沉但保留质感;肤色始终自然温暖。空气里有缓慢浮动的尘埃,被窗光照成一层薄薄的雾。画面沉稳克制,不带柔焦。

摄影机与镜头
RED Gemini,Leica定制镜头加低反差滤镜,无刺眼高光。复古2倍变形宽银幕,2.39:1,大光圈全开:椭圆拉伸焦外,边缘猫眼光斑,失焦高光抹成水平长椭圆,轻微色差,低饱和克制色彩。无镜头眩光,无光线拉丝,画面边缘直线保持笔直。运动为电动推轨,匀速极缓,起停带轻缓冲。

道具(本镜头关键,严格照此)
他手里的是一只已经完全翻开的黑色人造革账单夹:封面向外翻开、朝下,夹子的远端向他这一侧抬起,里面那张白色热敏纸完整露出来、正对着他的视线。纸上有等宽点阵打印的字迹,在画面里可见但因景深而不可辨读。这不是菜单、不是合着的夹子、不是空的夹子——它是打开的,他读的是里面的那张纸。
他双手捧着夹子的两侧下缘,两个拇指压在人造革的边上;肘部搭在桌沿上。

首帧与空间调度(本镜头的核心,严格照此)
这是他背影镜头的反打:摄影机在窗与桌子之间,背对着窗,朝向店内看他。
机位:明显低于桌面,几乎贴着浅色斑点纹台面的高度向上仰拍,镜头轴线自下而上——观众是从下往上看他的。桌面前缘作为一条模糊的亮色带横过画框最下方。
构图与力量:他的头与肩占据画框中下部,占比稳固但不塞满;头顶之上留出明显的空间——那是咖啡馆室内的深暗纵深,完全失焦。他在画框里舒展、有余地,绝不被四边挤压。翻开的账单夹在画面下缘、他胸前偏低的位置,失焦但形状清楚。
荷兰角:轻微倾斜,约8至10度,从入画第一帧起锁死,全程不变、绝不旋转、绝不回正。
背景:他身后是店内纵深——棕褐色皮革卡座靠背的边缘、过道、更深处的黑暗,全部化成柔软的深色块面与几团水平拉伸的椭圆光斑。绝不出现天花板、吊灯、横梁或任何位于他头顶上方的实体结构。
光线:唯一光源是他正对着的那扇临街大窗,此刻位于摄影机背后、画面之外。日光大而柔地从镜头方向偏一侧打在他脸上——额头、鼻梁、一侧颧骨被托亮,另一侧脸颊落进柔和的阴影。此外,他手里那张白色热敏纸把窗光反射上来,在他的下颌与鼻底形成一小片极柔和的补光,并在虹膜下缘留下一点细小的反射。眼窝微陷,眼睛清晰可读。亮但不过曝,最亮处仍能看清皮肤纹理与纸的质感。

格式模式
单镜头一镜到底,共4秒。无实拍台词,只有一句画外旁白。

动作时间轴
0.0-1.0秒——极缓匀速推近开始。他双手捧着翻开的夹子,视线落在纸面上,眼球沿着一行一行极小幅度地移动——他在读。肩背放松,呼吸平缓。
1.0-2.2秒——他读完了。目光从纸面上缓缓抬起,不急不慌,越过镜头上缘落到远处——他看的是很远的地方,焦点不在这个房间里的任何东西上,也不在镜头上。手没有动,夹子仍然翻开着捧在手里。下颌不抬、脖子不伸、肩膀不动,整个动作只发生在眼睛和眉骨上。
2.2-4.0秒——他停在那里,什么也没有发生:不点头,不皱眉,不吞咽,不合上夹子,嘴唇完全静止,呼吸平稳而缓慢。推近走完最后半步停住,倾斜角度全程锁死。
1.4秒——画外旁白,音量更轻、位置更近,说完即收:"...Neither could I."
3.4秒,他眨了一次眼。画面定格一拍,切黑。

声音
咖啡馆日常底噪:餐具碰撞、咖啡机蒸汽、隐约人声、远处一台收音机。极低沉沙哑、咬字含混的英语画外旁白清晰在最前,底噪在旁白出现时自动下沉;最后两秒底噪缓缓退远,只剩极轻的环境嗡鸣。无音乐,无实拍台词。

记忆的语法:梦境般浓重柔焦——边缘融化、高光晕成椭圆、动作带极轻拖影。白天色调是《杀手》式浑浊橄榄绿与硫磺黄,整体欠曝一档半,画面活在阴影上部;黑位深沉但保留质感;肤色自然温暖,浑浊的绿黄留在环境、瓷器和桌面上,不落在脸上。空气里有缓慢浮动的尘埃。

光线(本场关键)
唯一有动机的光源是他右侧那一整面临街大窗的日光:柔和、大面积,从他的右后方斜切进来,勾亮他右侧的头发边缘、右肩与右脸颊的轮廓线,并在他身后的窗玻璃上形成明亮的背景。窗外明亮但绝不过曝、绝不发白成一片,仍能看清街对面建筑与电线的轮廓。
因为是逆光,他的脸需要唯一一处补光:来自身前浅色桌面与对面墙面的柔和反射,自下而上、非常弱,只够把眼窝与下颌从黑里托出一点,让五官可读。除此之外没有任何补光、没有反光板、没有顶光、没有面光灯。
他左侧(画面右侧)的过道与卡座沉在阴影里,越往深处越暗。

镜头1——0.0至3.5秒——中景纵深,滑轨缓慢横移:那名黑人男子沿跑道跑来,步频稳定老练,呼吸的白雾一团团吐出,手腕上的运动手表亮着微光。迎面跑来穿浅灰色连帽卫衣、帽子罩在头上的杰克,步频同样平稳。两人在跑道中间交错而过,他礼貌地朝杰克抬了一下下巴;杰克点头回应。两人各自跑远。整条跑道再无别人。
3.5秒切
镜头2——3.5至6.5秒——跑道低角度中景,机位贴近地面朝前:他的背影在画面中央,节奏均匀地跑着,晨雾在他脚边被搅开。画面深处,浅灰色连帽卫衣的杰克跑进画面,由远及近,步频没有变化——他跑完一圈,从对方背后追了上来,距离迅速缩短。前面的人没有回头。
6.5秒切
镜头3——6.5至9.0秒——跑道侧面中景,机位固定,全程一镜。攻击方是穿浅灰色连帽卫衣、戴黑手套的杰克;被攻击方是穿深蓝色短袖、戴鸭舌帽的黑人男子。杰克在最后两步骤然加速,从背后用左臂横过对方的颈侧扣住,右手抓住对方的衣领,借着跑动的惯性把他整个人从跑道上拽偏——鸭舌帽被撞飞落在跑道上,脚跟离地,裸露的双臂徒劳地去抓那条横在颈前的手臂,手指抠进自己的脖子上,脸转向镜头一瞬,眼睛睁大,嘴张开。杰克不停顿、不调整,把他拽过路肩。杰克的脸自始至终没有任何变化,帽子始终罩在头上。
9.0秒切
镜头4——9.0至11.5秒——【只拍腿】贴地极低角度,机位藏在跑道边的草丛里,视线被前景的草叶切碎,画框上缘不超过膝盖高度:画面里只有腿。杰克的深色运动长裤与跑鞋稳稳地一步一步向后退,踩进湿草地;对方的两只跑鞋脚跟拖在草上,鞋尖朝上,双腿完全被动地被拖行,在湿草上压出两道深色的痕迹,带起几点泥。腿一路移入灌木丛的阴影,最后一只鞋跟消失在枝叶之间。灌木剧烈摇晃了几下,枝叶哗哗作响,然后慢下来、停住。
11.5秒切
镜头5——11.5至15.0秒——灌木丛内部近景,机位从枝叶缝隙间向内,极缓推近,最终落点是他的脖子:那名黑人男子仰倒在枝条之间,身体呈一个不自然的角度;头向后仰、偏向一侧,下颌抬起,整个喉咙完全朝向镜头暴露出来。眼睛睁着、一次也不眨,嘴微张,胸口完全静止;一条裸露的手臂掌心朝上摊在落叶上。
颈部细节(本镜头的落点):喉咙前侧与一侧颈部有一道宽而弥散的深色压痕,宽度约等于一条小臂,边缘模糊没有清晰界线,颜色是暗紫红渗进深色皮肤里的那种沉闷的深色,已经成形、不再变化;压痕之上与之下散着几道细小的月牙形抓痕,是他自己的指甲在拽那条手臂时抠出来的。深蓝色T恤的领口被扯得变形、歪向一边,领边的线脚绷开了一小段。没有伤口,没有血。

表演任务(功课在眼里,不演情绪)
杰克——
动机:这不是一场对抗,是一道工序;工序里没有对手,只有工件。
目标:在窗口时间内完成,不在这条跑道上留下任何值得记住的东西。
战术:他不追、不藏——他跑同一条路、点同一种头,让自己成为这条跑道上第二个普通的晨跑者;那个点头是纯粹的功能性动作,里面没有任何东西;第二圈他不加速也不减速地接近,直到最后两步才动手。把人拖进灌木的手法平稳仔细,那不是怜悯,是不能让东西留在路上被太早发现。最后他重新起跑,步频和第一圈一模一样。
目标——
战术:直到最后一刻他都还在用日常的逻辑理解眼前的事——他在数自己的配速,想着几点到家;真正的恐惧发生在"这解释不通"的那半秒里;他抓的不是那只手,是想让自己站住;身体先于头脑去找出口,然后发现出口不存在。
(安全线:活着的人目光始终投入各自的任务,绝不僵死呆滞、绝不空洞发直;自然眨眼节奏。已死的目标绝不眨眼、绝无呼吸起伏。)

物理
晨雾贴地缓慢流动,被跑动的人扰出涡流;呼吸的白雾成团吐出并消散;鸭舌帽被撞飞后在跑道上弹一下、翻转、停住;拖行时鞋跟在湿草上刮出连续的深色痕迹并带起泥点,鞋子在拖行中有真实的重量与晃动;灌木枝叶被扰动后摇晃衰减、逐渐停止;运动手表屏幕保持恒定亮度。
颈部压痕的物理:那是被一条小臂横向压迫留下的痕迹——宽、弥散、边缘不清,不是细线,不是绳索勒痕,不是环绕一整圈的闭合痕迹;颜色沉在皮肤下面,表面完整、不破皮、不出血、不结痂;自己抓出的月牙形抓痕很浅、颜色更淡。T恤领口被拉伸后保持变形,不回弹。记忆段拖影严格跟随动作方向。

声音
黎明的鸟叫、远处车流、两人交错时的呼吸与脚步声;鸭舌帽落地的一声轻响;拖行时衣料与湿草、枝叶的摩擦声;之后是彻底的安静,只剩鸟叫;最后压上规律的、跑远的脚步声,渐渐远去。无音乐,无台词。

禁止
颈部出现细线状的绳索勒痕、环绕颈部一整圈的闭合痕迹、绳索或任何凶器;开放性伤口、破皮、出血、结痂、血迹;夸张的紫黑色妆效;
死者眨眼、胸口起伏、任何微动;死者的头转正、下巴收回、脖子被遮住;
推近停止、倒退或加速;手持晃动、变焦、慢动作、变速;
镜头眩光、横向光条、星芒、多边形亮斑、鬼影、光晕溢出、亮处发白失去细节;
字幕、Logo、UI、边框、水印;音乐;非动画、非游戏CG、无塑料感皮肤。

场景背景
影片开场。白天,一家老式美式咖啡馆。杰克独自坐在窗边卡座,背对镜头。咖啡、苹果派和一只黑色账单夹先后被放上桌面。他掀开账单夹——热敏纸上,他点的两行之下、虚线之外,是点阵打印的一份新订单。最后一个镜头才第一次给到他的脸。全程有男性英语画外旁白;杰克本人一句话都不说。

旁白声音(最高优先级,贯穿全片不变)
声音属于一个四十五岁上下的男人。音高极低,男低音区,重心完全压在胸腔里,共鸣厚重发闷。质地非常沙哑粗粝,带砂砾与低频毛刺,喉咙深处带一点近似低吼的摩擦音,声带明显磨损,句尾破音带气。咬字含混、往回吞,像在自言自语地嘟囔,词尾常被吞掉,辅音软化模糊,音与音之间黏连,绝不字正腔圆、绝不清晰利落。音量不大,压着嗓子说,几乎是低声咕哝,但密度很高,像贴着耳朵。节奏紧凑往前推,词与词之间不留空隙,句尾干脆收掉。情绪平直,不加重任何词。绝不清亮、绝不年轻、绝不圆润、绝不明亮、绝不中性、绝不播音腔、绝不温和,也绝不是老人的颤抖声。

表演任务——杰克(功课在眼里,不演情绪)
场景方向:把这二十秒过成一顿普通的午饭。
本场事件:一次送达——东西被送来,人接收。
动机(一生的,只设一次):他杀过几十个人,这是他唯一做得好的事,也是他唯一还在做的事。他不为此痛苦,也不为此骄傲——他里面早就空了,没有什么东西能被这张纸碰到。一份订单对他来说不是消息,是工作分配。
目标:接收内容,把它记住,然后按时去做。
障碍:没有。这正是关键——这个人今天没有任何障碍。

场景方向:把这二十秒过成一顿普通的午饭。
本场事件:一次送达——东西被送来,人接收。

目标:接收内容,把它记住,然后按时去做。
障碍:没有。这正是关键——这个人今天没有任何障碍。
战术:他不检查这个房间,不确认有没有人在看他,不评估任何人是不是威胁——检查是害怕被抓的人才做的事,而他早就不做了;他坐在窗边、背对着整个店,因为他根本不在意身后有什么。读纸的时候一行一拍,像读一张送货单;读完抬眼,不是查看,是眼睛落下之后就没有再动的理由。他的目光落在哪里就停在哪里,又沉又不移开——不是盯着谁,是根本没有把那个方向上的东西当成活的东西看。
关于这张脸(给演员的说明,不是画面指令):他脸上的严峻不是此刻产生的,是这些年长在他脸上的——低垂的眉、沉重的眼皮、绷着的下颌,是一个长期做这种事的人的静息状态,不是对这份订单的反应。他没有在生气,他没有在压抑,他也没有什么要证明——他就是这么一张脸,而这张脸让人不想靠近。冷与危险来自完全的松弛加上眼睛的绝对静止,不来自任何表演出来的凶狠。

表演任务——杰克(功课在眼里,不演情绪)
场景方向:把这二十秒过成一顿普通的午饭。
本场事件:一次送达——东西被送来,人接收。
动机(一生的,只设一次):他杀过几十个人,这是他唯一做得好的事,也是他唯一还在做的事。他不为此痛苦,也不为此骄傲——他里面早就空了,没有什么东西能被这张纸碰到。一份订单对他来说不是消息,是工作分配。
目标:接收内容,把它记住,然后按时去做。
障碍:没有。这正是关键——这个人今天没有任何障碍。
战术:他不检查这个房间,不确认有没有人在看他,不评估任何人是不是威胁——检查是害怕被抓的人才做的事,而他早就不做了;他坐在窗边、背对着整个店,因为他根本不在意身后有什么。读纸的时候一行一拍,像读一张送货单;读完抬眼,不是查看,是眼睛落下之后就没有再动的理由。他的目光落在哪里就停在哪里,又沉又不移开——不是盯着谁,是根本没有把那个方向上的东西当成活的东西看。
关于这张脸(给演员的说明,不是画面指令):他脸上的严峻不是此刻产生的,是这些年长在他脸上的——低垂的眉、沉重的眼皮、绷着的下颌,是一个长期做这种事的人的静息状态,不是对这份订单的反应。他没有在生气,他没有在压抑,他也没有什么要证明——他就是这么一张脸,而这张脸让人不想靠近。冷与危险来自完全的松弛加上眼睛的绝对静止,不来自任何表演出来的凶狠。

【第一条规矩:这家店不放音乐】

【服装锁定:七个镜头完全一致】
杰克全程只穿这一套,从第一帧到最后一帧不变:里面是一件炭灰色连帽卫衣,帽子翻在颈后垂着、帽绳很短、领口是圆领;外面套一件深色工装夹克,布面结实、有磨损、前襟敞着或半敞、袖口卷起一点点;没有手套。

场景背景
记忆闪回。白天,一家老式美式咖啡馆。杰克独自坐在窗边卡座。先是他的背影,然后一杯黑咖啡与苹果派上桌,随后是黑色账单夹。他掀开夹子。热敏纸上,他点的两行之下、虚线之外,是点阵打印的另一份订单——一个地址,一个人的体貌,没有名字。读完之后,他把眼睛抬起来,看向侧前方的某一点。全场只有女服务员画外的一句话。

【第一条规矩:这家店不放音乐】

【服装锁定:七个镜头完全一致】
杰克全程只穿这一套,从第一帧到最后一帧不变:里面是一件炭灰色连帽卫衣,帽子翻在颈后垂着、帽绳很短、领口是圆领;外面套一件深色工装夹克,布面结实、有磨损、前襟敞着或半敞、袖口卷起一点点;没有手套。

他绝不只穿一件T恨衫或短袖:不露手臂、不露肩、不露胸口、没有印花T恤、没有衬衫加领带、没有西装、没有毛衣、没有卫衣以外的连帽衫颜色、没有围巾、没有帽子戴在头上、没有配饰。

【账单夹与纸张的物理:必须自然】
账单夹是一只普通的黑色人造革对折夹,里面夹着一张单层热敏纸,纸的上缘被订书钉固定在夹子内侧。掀开的动作就是掀开一张普通餐厅账单:拇指抵住封面边缘,封面绕折线平顺地翻过去,纸张跟着被带起一点、随即自然落平,只有纸面固有的轻微不平与一次极小的回弹。
纸和封面之间没有任何粘连:纸不吸在封面上、不被带起后又贴回去、不反复吸附与剥离、不像湿纸一样黏住、不产生拉丝或胶感。封面翻开一次到位,不来回摆动,不重复开合。
纸上印着的字只有下面时间轴里写明的那几行,其余全是干净空白的纸面——没有别的字、没有店名、没有地址栏、没有电话、没有编号、没有条码、没有logo、没有印章、没有手写、没有涂改。

空间调度
杰克坐在窗边卡座里。窗在他的右手边并延伸到他身后,明亮街景在他右肩外侧形成亮背景。他左手边是餐厅室内纵深:另一排卡座、吊灯、远处两个虚化的客人剪影,全部沉在阴影里。桌面上:装着纯黑咖啡的厚壁白瓷杯、白瓷小盘、黑色人造革账单夹、一张纸巾、一个不锈钢糖包架。

格式模式
七个镜头,共22.5秒,每个镜头景别与角度都不同——背影中远景、桌面特写、俯拍顶视、低角半侧推镜、侧后近景、微距、中景。全程记忆柔焦,全程无音乐,服装全程不变。台词为英语。

动作时间轴

镜头1——0.0至3.5秒——背影中远景,机位在他正后方,略高于肩线,画面绝对水平,构图完全锁死。画内是他的后脑、后颈、垂在颈后的卫衣帽子与深色工装夹克的两肩剪影、卡座椅背的上缘,以及他前方那面临街大窗与窗外街景的明亮背景;餐厅纵深的吊灯与虚化客人落在画面一侧的暗部。他只是坐着,一动不动,肩膀随一次平缓的呼吸轻微起伏一下,窗外偶尔有一个虚化的行人经过。什么也没发生。
3.5秒切

镜头2——3.5至5.9秒——桌面特写,构图锁死,极浅景深,机位低、几乎贴桌面:一只年轻女性的手、手指细长、指甲修短干净、手腕纤细、袖口浅色,从画面一侧稳稳伸入,先放下厚壁白瓷杯——杯里是纯黑的咖啡,液面深黑平整、只反出一点暖色高光,细弱的热气从液面升起,杯底与桌面轻轻一响、液面晃了一下;接着放下白瓷小盘,盘里是一整块完整的苹果派,银叉端正搁在盘缘——派在盘里稳稳不动,一点碎渣都没有掉。手收回,退出画面。
5.9秒切

镜头3——5.9至8.1秒——顶视俯拍(top shot),机位在桌子正上方垂直向下,画面绝对水平,构图锁死:画内是整张桌面——那杯深黑的咖啡与升起的细弱热气、那块完整的苹果派、纸巾与糖包架,以及桌沿两侧杰克平放的双手、深色工装夹克的两肩与头顶的一部分。那只女性的手连着浅色围裙的袖口从画面一侧伸进来,把黑色人造革账单夹平稳地放在他手边的桌面上,封面落桌一声闷响,黑咖啡的液面轻微一动。画外女声带着笑意:"Your check." 围裙下摆退出画面。杰克的双手不动。
8.1秒切

镜头4——8.1至12.9秒——半侧面低角度推镜。机位在他左手一侧的餐厅纵深方向,压得很低、几乎与桌面齐平并略微仰视他的下颌与侧脸,与他成约四十五度半侧角;荷兰角倾斜约12度,从第一帧起锁死、全程不变、绝不旋转回正。窗落在他身后:窗光从画面深处逆向打来,把他的侧脸轮廓线、肩线、卫衣领口与后脑发梢勾成一条亮边,前景桌沿沉在暗部,桌面浅色反射把眼窝与下颌托出一点。
从中景开始,极缓匀速一路推近到他脸部的近景,推镜不中断,焦点始终咬在他的眼睛上:他的眼睛垂下去落在那只合着的夹子上,身体不动;黑咖啡的热气在他与夹子之间被逆光勾成明亮细丝、缓慢升起。咖啡没喝、派一口没碰。推到脸部近景停住,定住一拍。
12.9秒切

镜头5——12.9至15.3秒——侧后方近景,景别更紧。机位在他左肩后方,越过肩线向下看桌面,保持12度倾斜锁死:深色夹克的肩与后颈成为前景暗色边框,窗光从画面深处把桌面与夹子的边缘勾亮。他的左手伸过去,拇指抵住封面边缘,封面平顺地翻过去一次到位,纸张被带起一点后自然落平,纸面上的字立刻可见。没有粘连,没有反复吸附与剥离,没有二次开合。
15.3秒切

镜头6——15.3至19.7秒——微距俯拍特写,构图回正、画面绝对水平,极浅景深,极缓匀速下移。纸上只有这些字,其余是空白纸面:上半部清晰可读"1 COFFEE 2.50"、"1 APPLE PIE 4.75"、"TOTAL 7.25";相机越过一条虚线撕口,焦点死死咬住虚线之下的等宽点阵打印字体,一行一行锐利清晰地进入画面,每一行都停留足够看清:
"YOUR NEW ORDER"
"447 MAPLE ST, QUEENS NY"
"APT 2, SECOND FLOOR"
"MALE, BLACK, EARLY 40S, ATHLETIC BUILD"
"PRIORITY: HIGH"
读到最后一行,下移停住。
19.7秒切

镜头7——19.7至24.0秒——中景,半侧面,机位低于桌面高度并略微仰视,画面略微倾斜(荷兰角约10度,从第一帧锁死、绝不回正),构图锁死不推不移。机位在他左手一侧,与他成约四十度半侧角;前景是桌沿与虚化的咖啡杯下缘,他的上半身、卫衣领口与夹克的肩、桌上的夹子与身后那面亮窗都在画内。窗光从他右后方逆向勾出侧脸与肩线的亮边,背景的餐厅纵深沉在暗部。
他的动作只有一个:眼睛从纸面抬起来,越过桌沿看向侧前方的某一点,并且停在那里。眼神很重——不是愤怒,不是威胁,是已经算完的人。下颌不抬、眉毛不动、嘴角不动、鼻翼不动,全部的重量都在目光和一次极慢的呼气上。头几乎不转,只有眼睛先到位。停住一拍,画面定格,切黑。

表演任务(功课在眼里,不演情绪)
场景方向:把这二十二秒过成一顿普通的午饭,直到最后四秒。
本场事件:一次送达——东西被送来,人接收;杀人和苹果派通过完全相同的流程被送到同一张桌上。
杰克——
动机:这套仪式是这份工作里他唯一没得选的部分;它早就不再意味着什么,只是每次都要重新排一遍的队。
目标:接收内容,不给任何人留下一个可以记住的理由。

(安全线:目光始终投入任务,绝不僵死呆滞、绝不空洞发直;自然眨眼节奏,最后一拍才停止眨眼。)

物理
黑咖啡的热气细弱真实,在逆光里被勾成明亮的细丝;深黑的液面平整,落杯时晃动一次即止;瓷杯与瓷盘落桌各有清脆轻响与微小晃动;派完整稳定、不掉渣、不塌不裂;账单夹落桌一声闷响,封面掀开时有人造革的硬度与一次自然回弹,纸张平顺落平、不粘连;热敏纸有真实的哑光反射与细微不平;夹克与卫衣的布料随呼吸有极小的自然起伏,褶皱位置全程不变;围裙布料撤出时有惯性延迟;女性的手动作轻稳,收手时手指自然收拢;尘埃颗粒在窗光里缓慢无规则漂浮。

声音(只有实景音效,整段无音乐)
这家店按规矩不放音乐,所以画面里能听到的全部是人和器物发出的实景音效,并且隔着一层水般发闷:
餐具与瓷器碰撞、咖啡机蒸汽的嘶声、后厨隐约的翻动与油声、听不清词的低语人声、门铃一响、椅子在地面上拖动一声、远处水龙头与洗碗池的水声、头顶风扇的低频转动。
唯一的台词:"Your check." 清晰在前,底噪自动下沉。
近处清晰的细节音:厚壁瓷杯落桌的闷厚一响、瓷盘落桌的清脆轻响、银叉碰到盘缘、账单夹落桌的闷响、人造革封面翻开的一次干涩摩擦、纸张落平的细碎脆响、夹克布料的一次轻微摩擦;最后四秒只剩底噪与他一次极慢的呼气。

场景背景
记忆闪回。白天,一家老式美式咖啡馆。杰克独自坐在窗边卡座。先是他的背影,然后一杯黑咖啡与苹果派上桌,随后是黑色账单夹。他掀开夹子。热敏纸上,他点的两行之下、虚线之外,是点阵打印的另一份订单——一个地址,一个人的体貌,没有名字。读完之后,他把眼睛抬起来,看向侧前方的某一点。全场只有女服务员画外的一句话。

风格
记忆的语法:梦境般浓重柔焦——边缘融化、高光晕成椭圆、动作带极轻拖影。白天色调是《杀手》式浑浊橄榄绿与硫磺黄,整体欠曝一档半,画面活在阴影上部;黑位深沉但保留质感;肤色自然温暖,浑浊的绿黄留在环境、瓷器和桌面上,不落在脸上。空气里有缓慢浮动的尘埃。

光线(本场关键)
唯一有动机的光源是他右侧那一整面临街大窗的日光:柔和、大面积,从他的右后方斜切进来,勾亮他右侧的头发边缘、右肩与右脸颊的轮廓线,并在他身后的窗玻璃上形成明亮的背景。窗外明亮但绝不过曝、绝不发白成一片,仍能看清街对面建筑与电线的轮廓。
因为是逆光,他的脸只有唯一一处补光:来自身前浅色桌面与对面墙面的柔和反射,自下而上、非常弱,只够把眼窝与下颌从黑里托出一点。除此之外没有任何补光、没有反光板、没有顶光、没有面光灯。
他左侧(餐厅纵深那一侧)的过道与卡座沉在阴影里,越往深处越暗。

【账单夹与纸张的物理:必须自然】
账单夹是一只普通的黑色人造革对折夹,里面夹着一张单层热敏纸,纸的上缘被订书钉固定在夹子内侧。掀开的动作就是掀开一张普通餐厅账单:拇指抵住封面边缘,封面绕折线平顺地翻过去,纸张跟着被带起一点、随即自然落平,只有纸面固有的轻微不平与一次极小的回弹。
纸和封面之间没有任何粘连:纸不吸在封面上、不被带起后又贴回去、不反复吸附与剥离、不像湿纸一样黏住、不产生拉丝或胶感。封面翻开一次到位,不来回摆动,不重复开合。
纸上印着的字只有下面时间轴里写明的那几行,其余全是干净空白的纸面——没有别的字、没有店名、没有地址栏、没有电话、没有编号、没有条码、没有logo、没有印章、没有手写、没有涂改。
